author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Zurarah narrated that a man asked him (Abu Ja'far {a.s}):
"If a person sees a scorpion, a snake, or a serpent while he is praying, should he kill
it?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, if he wishes to do so."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى زُرَارَةُ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ لَهُ: رَجُلٌ يَرَى الْعَقْرَبَ وَ الْأَفْعَى وَ ٱلْحَيَّةَ وَ هُوَ يُصَلِّي أَيَقْثُلُهَا قَالَ «نَعَمْ إنْ شَاءَ
فَعَلَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 257 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 905

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Suleiman ibn Jaafar al-Ja'fari asked the righteous servant Imam Musa ibn Jafar
Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a man who goes to the market and buys a fur garment without
knowing if it is from a properly slaughtered (halal) animal or not. Can he pray in it?
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, you are not obligated to inquire about that. Abu Ja'far {a.s} used to
say, 'The Khawarij (a group known for extreme practices) imposed restrictions upon
themselves out of ignorance; indeed, religion is more accommodating than that.'".
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ جَعْفَرِ الْجَعْفَرِيُ الْعَبْدَ الصَّالِحَ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي السُّوقَ
فَيَشتَرِي جُبَّةَ فِرَاءٍ لا يَدْرِي أَذَكِيَّةٌ هِيَ أَمْ غَيْرُ ذَكِيَّةِ أَيُصَلِّي فِيهَا فَقَالَ
«نَعَمْ لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَسْأَلَةُ إِنَّ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ كَانَ يَقُولُ «إِنَّ الْخَوَارِجَ ضَيَّقُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ بِجَهَالَتِهِمْ إِنَّ
الدِّينَ أَوْسَعُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 257 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 368 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 419 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 491 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 455 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 2, p. 281

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ismail ibn Isa asked Abu Al-Hasan al-Ridha about leather and fur items
purchased from a market in the mountain regions: Should a person inquire about their
source of slaughter (i.e., whether it was properly done) if the seller is a Muslim but not
a known believer?
He {a.s} replied: "You should inquire if you see that the sellers are polytheists selling
those items. But if you see them performing prayer, then you do not need to ask”.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ عِيسَى أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الْجُلُودِ وَ ٱلْفِرَاءِ يَشتَرِيهِ الرَّجُلُ فِي سُوقٍ
مِنْ أَسْوَاقِ الْجَبَلِ أَيَسْأَلُ عَنْ ذَكَاتِهِ إِذَا كَانَ ٱلْبَائعُ مُسْلِماً غَيْرَ عَارِفٍ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهُ إِذَا
رَأَيْتُمُ الْمُشْرِكِينَ يَبِيعُونَ ذَلِكَ وَ إِذَا رَأَيْثُمُوهُمْ يُصَلُونَ فَلاَ تَسْأَلُوا عَنْهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 258 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 371 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 420 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 492

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
It was narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus that his father wrote to
Imam Abu Al-Hasan {a.s} asking about wearing fur or leather socks (khuff) and praying
in them without knowing if they were from a properly slaughtered (halal) animal.
He {a.s} replied: "There is no harm in it”.
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ جَعْفَرِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يُونْسَ أَنْ أَبَاهُ كَتَبَ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: يَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ ٱلْفَرْوِ وَ الْخُفَّ
أَلْبَسُهُ وَ أَصَلِّي فِيهِ وَ لا أَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ ذَكِيّ فَكَتَبَ «لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 258 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 456

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
It was narrated from Hashim Al Hannat that he heard Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-
Kadhim {a.s} say: "Anything that eats leaves and plants, there is no problem in praying
while wearing it (its leather or fur), but anything that eats carrion, do not pray in it”.
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ هَاشِمِ الْحَنَّاطِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: «مَا أَكَلَ ٱلْوَرَقَ وَ ٱلشَّجَرَ
فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِأَنْ تُصَلِّيَ فِيهِ وَ مَا أَكَلَ ٱلْمَيْتَةَ فَلاَ تُصَلَّ فِيهِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 404 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 354 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 76

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Zurarah said that Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said: "The Commander
of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} came out to a group of people and saw them
praying in the mosque with their cloaks draped (over their shoulders), and Imam {a.s}
said to them:
'What is the matter with you that you drape your garments as if you are Jews coming
out of their synagogues?' Meaning, beware of draping your garments (while praying)."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ زُرَارَةُ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: «خَرَجَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ عَلَى قَوْمٍ فَرَآهُمْ يُصَلُونَ فِي
اَلْمَسْجِدِ قَدْ سَدَلُوا أَرْدِيَتَهُمْ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ «مَا لَكُمْ قَدْ سَدَلْتُمْ ثِيَابَكُمْ كَأَنَّكُمْ يَهُودُ قَدْ خَرَجُوا مِنْ فُهْرِهِمْ » يَغْنِي
بِيعَتَهُمْ إِيَّاكُمْ وَ سَدْلَ ثِيَابِكُمْ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 386 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Zurarah narrated that Abu Ja'far, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"Beware of the 'wrapped shroud' (al-samma')."
I asked: "And what is the 'wrapped shroud'?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is when you take your garment under your arm and place it over one
shoulder”.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ زُرَارَةُ قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ: «إيَّاكَ وَ اِلْتِحَافَ الصَّمَّاءِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ مَا الصَّمَّاءُ قَالَ «أَنْ تُدْخِلَ
الثَّوْبَ مِنْ تَحْتِ جَنَاحِكَ فَتَجْعَلَهُ عَلَى مَنْكِبٍ وَاحِدٍ.
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 394 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Ma’ani al-Akhbar, Part 1, p. 390 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 214 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 388 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 387 • Wasail Al- Shia, Vol. 4, p. 399 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 201

I asked: "And what is the 'wrapped shroud'?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is when you take your garment under your arm and place it over one

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} stated regarding a man who finds
himself outside without clothing and the time for prayer arrives, that he should pray
standing while uncovered if no one can see him. However, if he is in view of others, he
should pray sitting.
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ: «فِي الرَّجُلِ يَخْرُجْ عُرْيَاناً فَتُذْرِكُهُ الصَّلاةُ أَنْهُ يُصَلِّي عُرْيَاناً قَائِماً إِنْ لَمْ يَرَهُ أَحَدٌ وَ إِنْ رَآهُ أَحَدٌ
صَلّى جَالِساً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 365 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 438 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 449 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 449 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 213

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Abu Jamila narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that he
asked him about wearing the garment of a Magian (Zoroastrian) and praying in it.
Abu Abdullah {a.s} replied: "Yes." Then he asked: "But they drink wine."
He {a.s} said: "Yes, we buy Sabiriyyah garments (a type of fabric) and wear them without
washing."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى أَبُو جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَهُ عَنْ ثَوْبِ الْمَجُوسِيّ أَلْبَسُهُ وَ أُصَلِّي فِيهِ قَالَ
«نَعَمْ» قَالَ قُلْتُ يَشرَبُونَ الْخَمْرَ قَالَ «نَعَمْ نَحْنُ نَشَتَرِي التَّيَابَ السَّابِرِيَّةَ فَنَلْبَسُهَا وَ لا نَغْسِلُهَا.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 259 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 6, p. 210 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that a man, while in his
presence, asked about a person who exits the bathhouse or performs a ritual bath,
then wraps himself and wears a shirt over his lower garment and prays in this manner.
Imam {a.s} said: "This is from the actions of the people of Lot."
I (Ziyad) said: "He wraps the cloth over his shirt."
Imam {a.s} said: "This is an act of arrogance."
I said: "The shirt is thin, and he covers himself with it."
Imam {a.s} responded: "This, along with unfastening the buttons during prayer, flicking
pebbles, and chewing gum (frankincense) in gatherings or while on the street, are
among the practices of the people of Lot."

Scholar's Note:
It has also been narrated that there is leniency in wrapping the garment over the shirt
from the Righteous Servant (of Allah {SWT}), from Abu Al-Hasan al-Thalith, Imam Ali ibn
Muhammad Al-Hadi {a.s}, and from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Jawad {a.s} and they
accepted it in certain cases.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى زِيَادُ بْنُ ٱلْمُنْذِرِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سَأْلَهُ رَجُلٌ وَ هُوَ حَاضِرٌ عَنِ الرَّجْلِ يَخْرُجْ مِنَ ٱلْحَمَّامِ
أَوْ يَفْتَسِلُ فَيَتَوَشَّحُ وَ يَلْبَسُ قَمِيصَهُ فَوْقَ إِزَارِهِ فَيُصَلِّي وَ هُوَ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ «هَذَا مِنْ عَمَلِ قَوْمٍ لُوطِ » فَقُلْتُ إِنَّهُ
يَتَوَشَّحْ فَوْقَ ٱلْقَمِيصِ قَالَ «هَذَا مِنَ التَّجَبُّرِ» قُلْتُ إِنَّ ٱلْقَمِيصَ رَقِيقٌ يَلْتَحِفُ بِهِ قَالَ «هُوَ وَ حَلُ ٱلْأَزْرَارِ فِي الصَلاَةِ
وَ اَلْخَذْفُ بِالْحَصَى وَ مَضْغُ الْكُنْدُرِ فِي الْمَجَالِسِ وَ عَلَى ظَهْرِ الطَّرِيقِ مِنْ عَمَلٍ قَوْمِ لُوطِ».
وقد رويت رخصة في التوشح بالإزار فوق القميص عن العبد الصالح عليه السلام و عن أبي الحسن الثالث عليه السلام
وعن أبي جعفر الثاني عليه السلام وبها آخذوا فتى.
commentary:
It has also been narrated that there is leniency in wrapping the garment over the shirt
from the Righteous Servant (of Allah {SWT}), from Abu Al-Hasan al-Thalith, Imam Ali ibn
Muhammad Al-Hadi {a.s}, and from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Jawad {a.s} and they
accepted it in certain cases.

text_chunk:
Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that a man, while in his
presence, asked about a person who exits the bathhouse or performs a ritual bath,
then wraps himself and wears a shirt over his lower garment and prays in this manner.
Imam {a.s} said: "This is from the actions of the people of Lot."
I (Ziyad) said: "He wraps the cloth over his shirt."
Imam {a.s} said: "This is an act of arrogance."
I said: "The shirt is thin, and he covers himself with it."
Imam {a.s} responded: "This, along with unfastening the buttons during prayer, flicking
pebbles, and chewing gum (frankincense) in gatherings or while on the street, are
among the practices of the people of Lot." Scholar's Note:

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Abdullah ibn Bukayr asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man praying while letting the sides of his garment hang loose.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no issue with it”.

Scholar's Note:
Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, Abu al-Jaroud al-Hamdani, was a blind Kufi follower of the Zaydi
sect. Al-Kashi narrated some reports criticizing him, some of which included claims
that he was a liar and an infidel.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ بُكَيْرٍ ، أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَ: فِي الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ يُرْسِلُ جَانِبَي ثَوْبِهِ قَالَ « لا بَأْسَ بِهِ.
زياد بن المنذر أبو الجارود الهمداني كوفي تابعي زيدي أعمى، روى الكشي في ذمه روايات تضمن بعضها كونها كذابا
كافرا.

that he was a liar and an infidel.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Abu Basir asked Imam {a.s} about a man praying in extreme heat and fearing for
his forehead due to the hot ground.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should place his garment beneath his forehead”.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي فِي حَرِّ شَدِيدٍ فَيَخَافُ عَلَى جَبْهَتِهِ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ قَالَ «يَضَعُ ثَوْبَهُ تَحْتَ
جَبْهَتِهِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Dawud Al-Sarmi asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi {a.s}
about going on a journey where there may be no place to pray except on snow. How
should he pray in such a case?
Imam {a.s} replied: "If you can avoid prostrating on the snow, then do not prostrate on
it. But if it is not possible, then level it and prostrate on it."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ دَاوُدُ الصَّرْمِيُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلِيَّ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ فَقَالَ لَهُ: إِنِّي أَخْرُجُ فِي هَذَا الْوَجْهِ وَ رُبِّمَا لَمْ
يَكُنُ مَوْضِعُ أُصَلِّي فِيهِ مِنَ الثَّلْجِ فَكَيْفَ أَصْنَعُ قَالَ «إِنْ أَمْكَنَكَ أَنْ لا تَسْجَدَ عَلَى الثِّلْجِ فَلَا تَسْجُدْ عَلَيْهِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ
يُمْكِثْكَ فَسَوِّهٍ وَ أُسْجُدْ عَلَيْهِ.
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 390 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 261 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 310 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 336 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 452 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1051 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 164

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ibrahim ibn Abi Mahmoud said to Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} about a man
who prays on a bed made of teakwood and prostrates on the teakwood itself.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, there is no issue”.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ أَبِي مَحْمُودٍ لِلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ: الرَّجُلُ يُصَلِّي عَلَى سَرِيرٍ مِنْ سَاجٍ وَ يَسْجُدُ عَلَى السَّاجِ
قَالَ «نَعَمْ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"There is no issue with praying on mats made from reeds or on palm-leaf mats, and on
any plant-based material, except for fruit”.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ - «لا بَأْسَ بِالصَّلاةِ عَلَى الْبُورِيَاءِ وَ الْخَصَفَةِ وَ
كُلِّ نَبَاتٍ إِلاَّ الثَّمَرَةَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 261 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 311 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 744 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 345

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} regarding
eating the meat of wild animals, including birds and other beasts.
Imam responded, "As for eating their meat, we dislike it, but as for their skins, you may
use them to ride on but do not wear anything made from them for prayer."

Scholar's Note:
My father, may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:
"There is no issue with praying in clothing made from the hair or fur of any animal
whose meat is permissible to eat. However, if you have garments of squirrel, sable, or
marten fur, remove them before prayer, though concessions have been narrated for
this.
Be cautious not to pray wearing fox skins or clothing directly touching such skins."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ سَمَاعَةُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنْ لُحُومِ السَّبَاعِ مِنَ الطَّيْرِ وَ الدَّوَابِّ قَالَ «أَمَّا أَكْلُ
لَحَمِهَا فَإِنَّا نَكْرَهُهُ وَ أَمّا الْجُلُودُ فَارْكَبُوا عَلَيْهَا وَ لاَ تَلْبَسُوا مِنْهَا شَيْئاً تُصَلُونَ فِيهِ.
وقال أبي رضي اللّٰه عنه في رسالته إلي: لا بأس بالصلاة في شعر ووبر كل ما أكلت لحمه وإن كان عليك غيره من سنجاب
أو سمور أو فنك وأردت الصلاة فانزعه، قد روي في ذلك رخص وإياك أن تصلي في ثعلب ولا في الثوب الذي يليه من
تحته وفوقه.
commentary:
My father, may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:
"There is no issue with praying in clothing made from the hair or fur of any animal
whose meat is permissible to eat. However, if you have garments of squirrel, sable, or
marten fur, remove them before prayer, though concessions have been narrated for
this.
Be cautious not to pray wearing fox skins or clothing directly touching such skins."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
It has been narrated from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari that He said: "I saw
Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha {a.s} praying in a silk cloak (jubbah made of khazz)."
text_ar: - وَ قَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ جَعْفَرِ الْجَعْفَرِيّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يُصَلِّي فِي جُبَّةِ خَزّ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 262 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 359

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated: "I saw Abu Ja'far al-Thani (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali
Al-Jawad {a.s}) praying both the obligatory and non-obligatory prayers in a cloak made
of fine silk fabric (khazz taruni). He gave me a cloak made of khazz, informed me that
he had worn it on his body and prayed in it, and instructed me to pray in it as well."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَلِيْ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرِ الثَّانِيَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يُصَلِّي الْفَرِيضَةَ وَ غَيْرَهَا فِي جُبَّةِ خَزّ
طَارُونِيَّ وَ كَسَانِي جُبَّةَ خَزَّ وَ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَبِسَهَا عَلَى بَدَنِهِ وَ صَلَّى فِيهَا وَ أَمَرَنِي بِالصَّلاةِ فِيهَا.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 262 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 411 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 359 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 23, p. 387 • Awalim al-Ulum, Vol. 23, p. 521

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
It was narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Imran that He said: ‘I wrote to Abu Ja'far al-
Thani (Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Jawad {a.s}) concerning clothing made from squirrel
(sanjab), mink (fanak), and silk (khazz), and I said: 'May I be your ransom, I would like
you not to respond with dissimulation (taqiyya) regarding this matter.'
The Imam {a.s} wrote back in his own handwriting, 'Pray in them.'"
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ يَحْيَى بْنِ أَبِي عِمْرَانَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: كَتَبْتُ إِلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرِ الثّانِي عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ فِي السِّنْجَابِ وَ الْفَنَكِ
وَ الْخَزِّ وَ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ أُحِبُّ أَنْ لا تُجِيبَنِي بِالتَّقِيَّةِ فِي ذَلِكَ فَكَتَبَ بِخَطَّهِ إِلَيَّ «صَلِّ فيهَا.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
It was narrated from Dawud al-Sarmi that a man asked Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith
(Imam Ali ibn Muhammad Al-Hadi {a.s}), about praying in silk (khazz) that is mixed with
rabbit fur.
The Imam wrote in response: "That is permissible."

Scholar's Note:
This is a leniency for which the one who acts upon it will be rewarded, and the one who
rejects it will be blameworthy. The original ruling as mentioned by (the narrator's)
father in his letter states: "Pray in silk (khazz) as long as it is not mixed with rabbit fur."
He also stated: "Do not pray in brocade, pure silk, or embroidered silk, except if it is a
garment with silk warp and cotton or linen weft."
text_ar:
809 رُوِيَ عَنْ دَاوُدَ الصَرْمِيّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: سَأَلَ رَجَلٌ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الثَالِثَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِي ٱلْخَزَّ يُغَشُ
بِوَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ فَكَتَبَ «يَجُوزُ ذَلِكَ.
وهذه رخصة الآخذ بها مأجور ورادها مأثوم والأصل ما ذكره أبي رحمه اللهفى رسالته إلي: وصل في الخز ما لم يكن
مغشوشا بوبر الأرانب، وقال فيها: ولا تصل في ديباج ولا حرير ولا وشي ولا في شئ من إبريسم محض إلا أيكون ثوبا
سداه إبريسم ولحمته قطن أو كتان.
commentary:
This is a leniency for which the one who acts upon it will be rewarded, and the one who
rejects it will be blameworthy. The original ruling as mentioned by (the narrator's)
father in his letter states: "Pray in silk (khazz) as long as it is not mixed with rabbit fur."
He also stated: "Do not pray in brocade, pure silk, or embroidered silk, except if it is a
garment with silk warp and cotton or linen weft."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar wrote to Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali {a.s}, asking
about praying in garments dyed with crimson (qirmaz), saying, "Our companions avoid
praying in it."
The Imam wrote back: "There is no problem with it at all, and all praise is due to Allah
{SWT}."

Scholar's Note:
The author of this book commented:
This ruling applies if the crimson-dyed garment is not made of pure silk. The prohibition
pertains only to garments made from pure silk.
text_ar:
810 كَتَبَ إبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مَهْزِيَارَ إِلَى أَبِي مُحَمَّدِ الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: يَسْأَلْهُ عَنِ الصَّلاَةِ فِي الْقِرْمِزِ فَإِنَّ أَصْحَابَنَا
يَتَوَقَّوْنَ عَنِ الصَّلاةِ فِيهِ فَكَتَبَ «لا بَأْسَ مُطْلَقُ وَ الْحَمْدُ لِلْهِ.
قال مصنف هذا الكتاب رحمه الله: وذلك إذا لم يكن القرمز من إبريسم محض والذي نهى عنه هو ما كان من إبريسم محض.
commentary:
The author of this book commented:
This ruling applies if the crimson-dyed garment is not made of pure silk. The prohibition
pertains only to garments made from pure silk.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
He (Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar) wrote to Imam Abu Muhammad al-Hasan {a.s} asking
about a man who replaces cotton in his cloak with qazz (a type of silk): "Can he pray in
it?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, there is no problem with it."

Scholar's Note:
The explanation is that it refers to qazz from goats, not pure silk qazz.
The narrations have prohibited wearing brocade (dibaj), silk, and pure silk (ibrisim) and
praying in them for men.
However, there is an allowance for women to wear such materials, though it does not
extend to praying in them. The prohibition on praying in pure silk applies generally to
both men and women, unless a specific exception has been made for women
regarding prayer as there has been for wearing it. For men, wearing silk and brocade is
only permitted in times of war. It is also permissible even if it contains images.
This was narrated by Sama’a ibn Mehran from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.
text_ar:
وَ كَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ: فِي الرَّجْلِ يَجْعَلُ فِي جُبَّتِهِ بَدَلَ الْقُطْنِ قَزَا هَلْ يُصَلِّي فِيهِ فَكَتَبَ «نَعَمْ لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ."
يعني به قز المعز لا قز الإبريسم.
وقد وردت الاخبار بالنهي عن لبس الديباج والحرير والإبريسم المحض و الصلاة فيه للرجال، ووردت الرخصة في لبس
ذلك للنساء ولم يرد بجواز صلاتهن فيه فالنهي عن الصلاة في الإيريسم المحض على العموم للرجال والنساء حتى يخصهن
خبر بالاطلاق لهن في الصلاة فيه كما خصهن بلبسه ولم يطلق للرجال لبس الحرير والديباج إلا في الحرب، ولا بأس به
وإن كان فيه تماثيل. روى ذلك سماعة بن مهران عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام.
commentary:
The explanation is that it refers to qazz from goats, not pure silk qazz.
The narrations have prohibited wearing brocade (dibaj), silk, and pure silk (ibrisim) and
praying in them for men.
However, there is an allowance for women to wear such materials, though it does not
extend to praying in them. The prohibition on praying in pure silk applies generally to
both men and women, unless a specific exception has been made for women
regarding prayer as there has been for wearing it. For men, wearing silk and brocade is
only permitted in times of war. It is also permissible even if it contains images.
This was narrated by Sama’a ibn Mehran from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1
text_chunk:
He (Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar) wrote to Imam Abu Muhammad al-Hasan {a.s} asking
about a man who replaces cotton in his cloak with qazz (a type of silk): "Can he pray in
it?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, there is no problem with it." Scholar's Note:
The explanation is that it refers to qazz from goats, not pure silk qazz.
The narrations have prohibited wearing brocade (dibaj), silk, and pure silk (ibrisim) and
praying in them for men.
However, there is an allowance for women to wear such materials, though it does not
extend to praying in them. The prohibition on praying in pure silk applies generally to
both men and women, unless a specific exception has been made for women
regarding prayer as there has been for wearing it. For men, wearing silk and brocade is
only permitted in times of war. It is also permissible even if it contains images.
This was narrated by Sama’a ibn Mehran from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim narrated from the Imam {a.s} that He said:
"There is no issue if a garment's warp, buttons, or trim is made of silk; what is disliked
for men is pure silk (mubham)”.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى يُوسُفُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ - «لا بَأْسَ بِالتَّوْبِ أَنْ يَكُونَ سَدَاهُ وَ زِرْهُ وَ عَلَمُهُ حَرِيراً
وَ إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ الْحَرِيرُ الْمُبْهَمُ لِلرِّجَالِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 264 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 208 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 386 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 726 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 375 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 240

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
It was narrated from Mus'ab ibn Abdul Malik al-Basri that He said:
"There is no issue in taking (a piece) from the silk covering of the Ka’ba and using it as
a cover for a Quran or making it into a prayer mat to pray upon."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَنْهُ مِسْمَعُ بْنُ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ الْبَصْرِيّ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مِنْ دِيبَاجِ الْكَعْبَةِ فَيَجْعَلَهُ غِلافَ
مُصْحَفٍ أَوْ يَجْعَلَهُ مُصَلَّى يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 264 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 734 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 378 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 13, p. 258
text_chunk:
It was narrated from Mus'ab ibn Abdul Malik al-Basri that He said:
"There is no issue in taking (a piece) from the silk covering of the Ka’ba and using it as
a cover for a Quran or making it into a prayer mat to pray upon."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi' asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-
Ridha {a.s}, about praying in a garment with patterns (decorations), and the Imam
disliked it if it contained images (representations).

Scholar's Note:
Praying in a belt (headband) with a silk end is not permitted. There is no issue with
praying in garments made from Khwarazmian furs or those tanned in the land of Hijaz.
Also, there is no issue with praying in the wool of a dead animal because wool does
not have a soul.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ أَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ فِي الثَّوْبِ ٱلْمُعْلَمِ فَكَرِهَ مَا
فِيهِ مِنَ التَّمَاثِيلِ.
ولا تجوز الصلاة في تكة رأسها من إبريسم، ولا بأس بالصلاة في الفراء الخوارزمية وما يدبغ بأرض الحجاز، ولا بأس
بالصلاة في صوف الميتة لان الصوف ليس فيه روح.
commentary:
Praying in a belt (headband) with a silk end is not permitted. There is no issue with
praying in garments made from Khwarazmian furs or those tanned in the land of Hijaz.
Also, there is no issue with praying in the wool of a dead animal because wool does
not have a soul.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 264 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 437

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Sama’a ibn Mehran asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
wearing a sword during prayer that has glue or leather (adhesive substances, such as
glue made from animal parts) on it.
Imam {a.s} replied: "There is no problem as long as you do not know that it is from a dead
(non-slaughtered) animal”.
text_ar:
و سَأَلَ سَمَاعَةُ بْنُ مِهْرَانَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنْ تَقْلِيدِ السَّيْفِ فِي الصَّلاةِ فِيهِ اَلْغِرَاءُ وَ الْكَيْمُخْتُ
فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ مَا لَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ مَيْتَةٌ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 265 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 56

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ali ibn al-Rayan ibn al-Salt asked Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s} about a
man who cuts his hair or trims his nails and then goes to pray without shaking the
remnants off his clothes.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no issue (no problem)."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَلِيْ بْنُ الرِّيَّانِ بْنِ الصَّلْتِ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَأْخُذْ مِنْ شَعْرِهِ وَ أَطْفَارِهِ ثُمَّ
يَقُومُ إِلَى الصَّلاةِ مِنْ غَيْرِ أَنْ يَنْفُضَهُ مِنْ ثَوْبِهِ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 265 • The Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 66 • Bihar Al- Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 123
text_chunk:

man who cuts his hair or trims his nails and then goes to pray without shaking the

Imam {a.s} said: "There is no issue (no problem)."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Yunus ibn Ya'qub asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
praying while wearing a burṭulah (a type of hat or head covering).
The Imam said: "It does not harm him (there is no issue)."

Scholar's Note:
And I heard our esteemed scholars say that it is not permissible to pray in a ṭabaqiyyah
(a specific type of head covering), and a person wearing a turban (muʿtamim) must
have it wrapped (with a part of the turban under the chin).
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ يُونُسُ بْنُ يَعْقُوبَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ عَلَيْهِ الْبُرْطُلَةُ فَقَالَ «لا يَضُرُّهُ.
وسمعت مشائخنا رضي اللّٰه عنهم يقولون: لا تجوز الصلاة في الطابقية ولا يجوز للمعتم أن يصلي إلا وهو متحنك
commentary:
And I heard our esteemed scholars say that it is not permissible to pray in a ṭabaqiyyah
(a specific type of head covering), and a person wearing a turban (muʿtamim) must
have it wrapped (with a part of the turban under the chin).
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ammar al-Sabati narrated from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said: "Whoever goes
out on a journey without wrapping the turban under his chin and suffers from an
ailment for which there is no remedy, let him blame none but himself”.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَمَّارْ السَابَاطِيْ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ - «مَنْ خَرَجَ فِي سَفَرٍ فَلَمْ يُدِرِ ٱلْعِمَامَةَ تَحْتَ
حَنَكِهِ فَأَصَابَهُ أَلَمٌ لاَ دَوَاءَ لَهُ فَلا يَلُومَنَّ إِلاَّ نَفْسَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Makarem al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 245 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 398 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 745 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 402
text_chunk:

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
The truthful one, Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said: "I guarantee that whoever leaves his
house with his turban wrapped under his chin will return to it safely."
text_ar: - وَقَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ: «ضَمِئْتُ لِمَنْ خَرَجَ مِنْ بَيْتِهِ مُعْتَمَا تَحْتَ حَنَكِهِ أَنْ يَرْجِعَ إِلَيْهِمْ سَالِما».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1
text_chunk:
The truthful one, Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said: "I guarantee that whoever leaves his
house with his turban wrapped under his chin will return to it safely."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said:
"I am amazed by one who goes about seeking to fulfil a need while in a state of ritual
purity (wudu) - how is it that his need is not met?
And I am amazed by one who seeks to fulfil a need while wearing his turban wrapped
under his chin - how is it that his need is not met?"
text_ar:
وَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «إِنِّي لَأَعْجَبُ مِمَّنْ يَأْخُذُ فِي حَاجَةٍ وَ هُوَ عَلَى وُضُوءِ كَيْفَ لاَ تُقْضَى حَاجَتُهُ وَ إِنِّي
الَأَعْجَبُ مِمَّنْ يَأْخُذُ فِي حَاجَةٍ وَ هَوَ مُعْتَمٌ تَحْتَ حَتَكِهِ كَيْفَ لاَ تُقْضَى حَاجَثُهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 165

Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, said:

And I am amazed by one who seeks to fulfil a need while wearing his turban wrapped

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
The Prophet, said: "The distinction between the Muslims and the polytheists
is the wearing of turbans."

Scholar's Note:
This was during the early period of Islam and its establishment.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: «الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ ٱلْمُشَرِكِينَ التَّلَحَي بِالْعَمَائِمِ.
وذلك في أول الاسلام وابتدائه.
commentary: This was during the early period of Islam and its establishment.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 20, p. 745 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 403
text_chunk:
The Prophet, said: "The distinction between the Muslims and the polytheists
is the wearing of turbans." Scholar's Note:
This was during the early period of Islam and its establishment.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
It has also been reported from the Messenger, by those outside the Shi'a
tradition that he commanded the wearing of turbans (tallaḥḥi) and forbade wrapping
without a tail (iqti'āṭ).
text_ar: - وَقَدْ نَقَلَ عَنْهُ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ أَهلُ ٱلْخِلافِ أَيْضاً: أَنَّهُ أَمَرَ بِالتَلَحَي وَ نَهَى عَنِ ٱلاِقْتِعَاطِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 266 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 165 • Meftah al-Falah, Part 1, p. 165 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 403

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Al-Halabi and Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} whether a man may recite during prayer with his garment covering his mouth.
The Imam said: "There is no issue with that."
In another narration by Al-Halabi, it is added: "As long as he can hear his murmuring
(sound of his recitation)”.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ الْحَلَبِيْ وَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سِنَانٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ: هَلْ يَقْرَأْ الرَّجُلُ فِي صَلاَتِهِ وَ ثَوْبُهُ عَلَى فِيهِ
فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ. وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ الْحَلَبِيَّ: «إِذَا سَمِعَ ٱلْهَمْهَمَةَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Al-Halabi and Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} whether a man may recite during prayer with his garment covering his mouth.
The Imam said: "There is no issue with that."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Rifa'ah ibn Musa asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}
about a person who is dyed (with henna or similar) and whether they can pray while in
this state if they are able to perform prostration and recitation.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, as long as their cloth (used during the process) is pure and they
are in a state of wudu (ritual purity). There is also no issue if a woman prays while She
is dyed and her hands are bound (covered)."

Scholar's Note:
This was narrated by 'Ammar al-Sabati from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ رِفَاعَةُ بْنُ مُوسَى أَبَا الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السِّلامُ: عَنِ ٱلْمُخْتَضِبِ إِذَا تَمَكِّنَ مِنَ السِّجُودِ
وَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةِ أَيُصَلِّي فِي خِضَابِهِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ إِذَا كَانَتْ خِرْقَتُهُ طَاهِرَةً وَ كَانَ مُتَوَضِّئاً وَ لا بَأْسَ بِأَنْ تُصَلِّيَ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ وَ
هِيَ مُخْتَصِبَةٌ وَ يَدَاهَا مَرْبُوطَتَانٍ.
روى ذلك عمار الساباطي عن الصادق عليه السلام.
commentary: This was narrated by 'Ammar al-Sabati from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

about a person who is dyed (with henna or similar) and whether they can pray while in

Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, as long as their cloth (used during the process) is pure and they

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Ali ibn Ja'far and Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-
Kadhim {a.s} about whether a man and a woman may pray while dyed with henna or
wasmah (a type of dye).

الرَّجُلِ وَ الْمَرْأَةِ يَخْتَضِبَانٍ أَيْصَلَّيَانٍ وَ هُمَا مُخْتَصِبَانٍ بِالْجِنَّاءِ وَ الْوَسِمَةِ فَقَالَ «إِذَا أَبْرَزُوا ٱلْفَمَ وَ ٱلْمَنْجِرَ فَلَاَ بَأْسَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a
man praying without taking his hands out of his garment.
The Imam said: "If he takes his hands out, it is good, but if he does not, there is no issue
(no problem)."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلِّي وَ لا يُخْرِجُ يَدَيْهِ مِنْ ثَوْبِهِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ
أَخْرَجَ يَدَيْهِ فَهُوَ حَسَنْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُخْرِجْ يَدَيْهِ فَلَاَ بَأْسَ.

chapter_title: GARMENTS PERMISSIBLE FOR PRAYER AND WHAT GARMENTS ARE NOT

Ziyad ibn Suqah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Prostration (Sujood) on the earth is obligatory (fardh), while prostrating on other than
that is a recommended practice (sunnah)."
text_ar:
باب - ما يسجد عليه وما لا يسجد عليه
قال الصادق عليه السلام: " السجود على الأرض فريضة وعلى غير ذلك سنة.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR
text_en:
Imam {a.s} said: "Prostrating on the clay from the grave of Imam Hussain ibn Ali
{a.s} illuminates to the seventh layer of the earth."

Scholar's Note:
Whoever possesses a prayer bead (subha) made from the clay of the grave of Imam
Hussain ibn Ali {a.s}, is considered as having performed tasbih (glorification) even if they
do not actively recite.
Additionally, performing tasbih with one's fingers is superior to using anything else
because the fingers will be questioned (held accountable) on the Day of Judgment.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلاَمُ: «السُجُودُ عَلَى طِينٍ قَبْرِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلاَمُ يُنَوَّرُ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ السَّابِعَةِ.
ومن كان معه سبحة من طين قبر الحسين عليه السلام كتب مسبحا وإن لم يسبح بها. والتسبيح بالأصابع أفضل منه
بغيرها لأنها مسؤولات يوم القيامة.

Hussain ibn Ali {a.s}, is considered as having performed tasbih (glorification) even if they
do not actively recite.
Additionally, performing tasbih with one's fingers is superior to using anything else
because the fingers will be questioned (held accountable) on the Day of Judgment.

chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR
text_en:
Hamad ibn Uthman narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said:
"Prostration is to be done on what the earth produces, except for that which is eaten
or worn."
text_ar: - وَ رَوَى حَمَّادُ بْنُ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «السُجُودُ عَلَى مَا أَنْبَتَتِ الْأَرْضُ إِلَّ مَا أُكِلَ أَوْ لُبِسَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION
text_en:
It was narrated from the Yasir al-Khadim that He said:
"Abu al-Hasan {a.s} passed by me while I was praying on a piece of ṭabarī (a mat) upon
which I had placed something.
Imam {a.s} said: 'Why do you not prostrate on it? Is it not from what the earth produces?'"

Scholar's Note:
My father further explained in his letter: "Prostrate on the earth or on what grows from
the earth. Do not prostrate on the ḥuṣur (reed mats) of Medina because their bindings
are made of leather. Do not prostrate on hair, wool, leather, silk, glass, iron, brass,
bronze, lead, copper, feathers, or ashes. If the earth is hot and you fear burning your
forehead, or if it is a dark night and you fear scorpions or thorns that might harm you,
there is no issue with prostrating on your sleeve if it is made of cotton or linen.
If there is a swelling on your forehead, dig a small hole so that when you prostrate, the
swelling can fit inside.
If you have an ailment on your forehead that prevents you from prostrating, prostrate
on the right side of your forehead. If that is not possible, then prostrate on the left side
of your forehead. If you cannot do that, prostrate on the back of your hand. If even that
is not possible, then prostrate on your chin, for Allah {SWT}, says: 'Those who were given
knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down prostrating on their chins..
and it increases them in humility' (Surah Al-Isra, 17:107-109).
There is no issue with standing and placing your palms, knees, and big toes on
surfaces other than earth. You should bring your nose close to the ground, and for
placing the forehead, the amount from the hairline to the eyebrows equivalent to a
dirham suffices. Your prostration should be like a thin, gaunt camel lowering itself,
such that no part of your body rests on another."
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ يَاسِرِ الْخَادِمِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: مَرَّ بِي أَبُو الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ وَ أَنَا أَصَلِّي عَلَى الطَّبَرِيِّ وَ قَدْ أَلْقَيْتُ
عَلَيْهِ شَيْئاً فَقَالَ لِي «مَا لَكَ لا تَسْجُدُ عَلَيْهِ أَلَيْسَ هُوَ مِنْ نَبَاتِ ٱلْأَرْضِ.
وقال أبي رسالته إلي: اسجد على الأرض أو على ما أنبتت الأرض ولا تسجد على الحصر المدنية لان سيورها من جلد ولا
نسجد على شعر ولا صوف ولا جلد ولا إبريسم ولا زجاج ولا حديد ولا صفر ولا شبه ولا رصاص ولا نحاس ولا ريش ولا
رماد، وإن كانت الأرض حارة تخاف على جبهتك الاحتراق أو كانت ليلة مظلمة خفت عقربا أو شوكة تؤذيك فلا بأس أن
نسجد على كمك إذا كان من قطن أو كتان، وإن كان بجبهتك دمل فاحفر حفرة فإذا سجدت جعلت الدمل فيها، وان كانت
بجبهتك علة لا تقدر على السجود من اجلها فاسجد على قرنك الأيمن من جبهتك، فإن لم تقدر عليه فاسجد على قرنك
الأيسر من جبهتك، فإن لم تقدر عليه فاسجد على ظهر كفك، فإن لم تقدر عليه فاسجد على ذقنك لقول اللّٰه "إن الذين
أوتوا العلم من قبله إذا يتلى عليهم يخرون للأذقان سجدا إلى قوله ويزيدهم خشوعا" ولا بأس بالقيام ووضع الكفين
والركبتين والابهامين على غير الأرض، وترغم بأنفك، ويجزيك في وضع الجبهة من قصاص الشعر إلى الحاجبين مقدار
درهم، ويكون سجودك كما يتخوى البعير الضامر عند بروكه، تكون شبه المعلق لا يكون شئ من جسدك على شئ منه.

Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
praying on qufr (bare ground or desert soil) and qīr (a type of tar or pitch).
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no issue with it”.
text_ar: - وَسَأَلَ ٱلْمُعَلَّى بْنُ خَتَيْسِ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى الْقُفْرِ وَ ٱلْقِيرِ فَقَالَ « لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub asked Imam Abu al-Hasan {a.s} about gypsum (plaster)
that was fired using dung and the bones of the dead, and whether it would be
permissible to prostrate on it if a mosque was plastered with it.
The Imam wrote back in his own handwriting: "Fire and water have purified it”.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ الْحَسَنْ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الْجِصِّ يُوقَدُ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَذِرَةِ وَ عِظَامِ الْمَوْتَى ثُمَّ
يُجَصَّصُ بِهِ الْمَسْجِدُ أَيُسْجَدُ عَلَيْهِ فَكَتَّبَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ إِلَيْهِ بِخَطَّهِ «أَنَّ النَّارَ وَ الْمَاءَ قَدْ طَهَّرَاهُ.

Dawud ibn Abi Zayd asked Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Thalith {a.s} about prostrating
on papers and documents with writing on them.
The Imam wrote back: "It is permissible."

وَ سَأَلَ دَاوُدُ بْنُ أَبِي زَيْدِ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثَ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الْقَرَاطِيسِ وَ الْكَوَاغِذِ الْمَكْتُوبَةِ عَلَيْهَا هَلْ
يَجُوزُ عَلَيْهَا السُّجَودُ فَكَتَبَ «يَجُوزُ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION
text_en:
Ali ibn Yaqtin asked Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s} about a man prostrating
on a misḥ (a type of mat or rug) and on a carpet.
The Imam said: "There is no issue if it is in a situation of taqiyya (precautionary
dissimulation to protect oneself)."

Scholar's Note:
It is no issue with prostrating on clothing in situations of taqiyya.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَلِيْ بَنُ يَقْطِينٍ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الْأَوّلَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَسْجُدُ عَلَى الْمِسْحِ وَ اَلْبِسَاطِ فَقَالَ «لا
بَأَسَ إِذَا كَانَ فِي حَالِ التَّقِيَّةِ.
اولا بأس بالسجود على الثياب في حال التقية.
commentary: It is no issue with prostrating on clothing in situations of taqiyya.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION
text_en:
Zurarah narrated from one of the Imams {a.s} that He said:
"I asked him about a man prostrating while wearing a cap or a turban.
Imam {a.s} said: 'If any part of his forehead touches the ground, between his eyebrows
and his hairline, then it suffices.'"
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى زُرَارَةُ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ الرَّجُلُ يَسْجُدُ وَ عَلَيْهِ قَلَنْسُوَةُ أَوْ عِمَامَةً فَقَالَ
«إِذَا مَسَّ شَيْءٌ مِنْ جَبْهَتِهِ الْأَرْضَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ حَاجِبَيْهِ وَ قُصَاصِ شَعْرِهِ فَقَدْ أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُ.

Imam {a.s} said: 'If any part of his forehead touches the ground, between his eyebrows

text_en:
Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:
"I saw Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} leveling the pebbles at the place of his
prostration between the two prostrations."

text_en:
It was narrated from Ali ibn Bajil that He said:
"I saw Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}, every time he prostrated and then
raised his head, he would take the pebbles from his forehead and place them back on
the ground."

وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ بَجِيلٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: رَأَيْتُ جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ كُلِّمَا سَجَدَ فَرَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ أَخَذَ الْحَصَى
مِنْ جَبْهَتِهِ فَوَضَعَهُ عَلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ.

text_en:
Ammar al-Sabati narrate from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He
said:
"The area between the hairline and the tip of the nose is considered a place of
prostration (masjid), so whatever part of it touches the ground suffices."

وَ رَوَى عَمَّارْ السَّابَاطِيُ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَا بَيْنَ قُصَاصِ الشَّعْرِ إِلَى طَرَفِ ٱلْأَنْفِ
مَسْجِدٌ فَمَا أَصَابَ الْأَرْضَ مِنْهُ فَقَدْ أَجْرَأَكَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION
text_en:
A man asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} bout a place with dust
where he wanted to blow it away before prostrating.
The Imam said: "There is no issue”.

Scholar's Note:
The narrator's father further explained in his letter:
"Do not blow on your place of prostration during the prayer. If you wish to blow, do so
before entering the prayer."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ رَجُلُ الصَّادِقَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الْمَكَانِ يَكُونُ فِيهِ الْغُبَارُ فَأَنْفُخُهُ إِذَا أَرَدْتُ السُّجُودَ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ.
وفي رسالة أبي رضي اللّٰه عنه إلي: ولا تنفخ في موضع سجودك فإذا أردت النفخ فليكن قبل دخولك في الصلاة.

chapter_title: WHAT CAN AND CANNOT BE USED FOR PROSTRATION
text_en:
It was narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"It is disliked (makruh) because it may cause harm to the person next to him."

Scholar's Note:
It is disliked for a man to wipe the dust from his forehead while in prayer, and it is also
disliked to leave it there after the prayer. However, if a person wipes the dust from his
forehead while in prayer, there is no issue, as leniency has been reported regarding
this matter.
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنِ الصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِنَّمَا يُكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ خَشِيَةَ أَنْ يُؤْذَى مَنْ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ.
ويكره أن يمسح الرجل التراب عن جبهته وهو في الصلاة، ويكره أن يتركه بعد ما صلى فإن مسح التراب من جبهته وهو
في الصلاة فلا شئ عليه لورود الرخصة فيه.

this matter.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE REASON FOR THE PROHIBITION OF
text_en:
Hisham ibn al-Hakam said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"Tell me about what is permissible to prostrate on and what is not."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Prostration is only permissible on the earth or what grows from the
earth, except for what is eaten or worn."
Hisham then asked: "May I be your ransom, what is the reason for that?"
The Imam said: "Prostration is an act of humility before Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and
Majestic, and it should not be on what is eaten or worn because the people of the world
are slaves to what they eat and wear.
The one who prostrates in worship of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, should not
place his forehead on what is worshipped by the people of the world who are deceived
by its allure. Prostration on the earth is superior because it is more effective in
demonstrating humility and submission to Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic."
text_ar:
باب - علة النهى عن السجود على المأكول والملبوس دون - الأرض وما أنبتت من سواهم
قَالَ هِشَامُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ ، لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: أَخْبِرُنِي عَمَّا يَجُوزُ السُّجُودُ عَلَيْهِ وَ عَمَّا لاَ يَجُوزُ قَالَ
«السُّجُودُ لا يَجُوزُ إِلاَّ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ أَوْ عَلَى مَا أَنْبَتَتِ الْأَرْضُ إِلَّ مَا أَكِلَ أَوْ لُبِسَ» فَقَالَ لَهُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ مَا ٱلْعِلَّةُ فِي
ذَلِكَ قَالَ «لأَنَّ السُّجُودَ خُضُوعُ لِلْهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَلاَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَكُونَ عَلَى مَا يُوْكَلُ أَوْ يُلْبَسُ لِأَنَّ أَبْنَاءَ اَلدُّثْيَا عَبِيدُ مَا
يَأْكُلُونَ وَ يَلْبَسُونَ وَ السَّاجِدُ فِي سُجُودِهِ فِي عِبَادَةِ اللهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فَلاَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَضَعَ جَبْهَتَهُ فِي سُجُودِهِ عَلَى
مَعْبُودِ أَبْنَاءِ الدُّنْيَا آلَّذِينَ اِغْتَرُوا بِغُرُورِهَا وَ السُّجُودُ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ أَفْضَلُ لِأَنَّهُ أَبْلَغُ فِي التَّوَاضُعِ وَ الْخُضُوعِ لِلَّهِ عَزَّ
وَ جَلَّ

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said :
"Indeed, Allah {SWT}, Blessed and Exalted, made the Ka’ba the Qiblah (direction of
prayer) for the people of the mosque (Masjid al-Haram), and He made the mosque the
Qiblah for the people of the sanctuary (Haram), and He made the sanctuary the Qiblah
for the people of the world."
text_ar:
باب - باب القبلة
قَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وتَعَالَى جَعَلَ ٱلْكَعْبَةَ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ وَ جَعَلَ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ قِبْلَةً
الأَهْلِ الْحَرَمِ وَ جَعَلَ الْحَرَمَ قِبْلَةً لِأَهْلِ ٱلدُّنْيَا.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 272 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2, p. 195 • Ilal al-Sharai’ Vol. 2, p. 415 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 44 • Awaali al-La’aali, Part 3, p. 71 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 541 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 303 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 304 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 81, p. 50

for the people of the world."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
the deviation of some of our companions to the left from the Qiblah and the reason for
it.
Imam {a.s} replied: "When the Black Stone (Hajar al-Aswad) was brought down from
Paradise and placed in its position, the boundaries of the Haram (sanctuary) were
determined by the reach of the light emanating from the Stone. It is four miles to the
right of the Ka’ba and eight miles to the left, making a total of twelve miles.
Thus, if a person deviates to the right, they leave the boundary of the Qiblah due to the
lesser extent of the Haram's boundary, but if they deviate to the left, they do not leave
the boundary of the Qiblah."

Scholar's Note:
For those within Masjid al-Haram, it is permissible to face any side of the Ka’ba during
prayer. One praying inside the Ka’ba may also face any of its walls. However, the best
position is to stand between the two columns on the red tile and face the corner
containing the Black Stone. If someone is above the Ka’ba and it is time for prayer, they
should lie down and incline their head toward the Bayt al-Ma'mur (Heavenly House).
Similarly, anyone praying on Mount Abu Qubays should face the Ka’ba, as the Qiblah
extends upward to the sky.
The Prophet {saws} prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) for thirteen years in
Makkah after receiving prophethood and for nineteen months in Madinah.
The Jews mocked him, saying that he was following their Qiblah, causing him great
distress. One night, he turned his face toward the heavens in anticipation, and in the
morning, after completing two units (rak'ahs) of the Dhuhr prayer, Archangel Jibril {a.s}
came to him and said:
"We have seen you turning your face toward the sky, so We shall turn you to a Qiblah
that pleases you. Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144)."
Archangel Jibril {a.s} then took the Prophet’s hand and turned him toward the Ka’ba, and
those behind him also turned, so that men and women changed their positions.
Thus, his initial prayer was toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and the remainder was toward the
Ka’ba.
The news reached a mosque in Madinah where people had already prayed two rak'ahs
of 'Asr. They turned toward the Ka’ba, and so their initial prayer direction was toward
Bayt al-Maqdis and its completion was toward the Ka’ba. This mosque became known
as Masjid al-Qiblatayn (the Mosque of the Two Qiblahs).
The Muslims then asked:
"O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}, what happens to our prayers toward Bayt al-Maqdis?"
Allah {SWT} revealed: "Allah {SWT} would not make your faith to be in vain (Surah Al-
Baqarah 2:143)," meaning that their prayers toward Bayt al-Maqdis were accepted.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ الْمُفَضَّلُ بْنُ عُمَرَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ: عَنِ التَّحْرِيفِ لِأَصْحَابِنَا ذَاتَ الْيَسَارِ عَنِ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ عَنِ
السَّبَبِ فِيهِ فَقَالَ «إِنَّ الْحَجَرَ الْأَسْوَدَ لَمَّا أَنْزِلَ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ وَ وُضِعَ فِي مَوْضِعِهِ جُعِلَ أَنْصَابُ الْحَرَمِ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَحِقَهُ
اَلنُورُ نُورُ الْحَجَرِ فَهُوَ عَنْ يَمِينِ الْكَفْبَةِ أَرْبَعَةُ أَمْيَالٍ وَ عَنْ يَسَارِهَا ثَمَانِيَةُ أَمْيَالٍ كُلُهُ إِثْنَا عَشَرَ مِيلاً فَإِذَا اِنْحَرَفَ
اَلْإِنْسَانُ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ خَرَجَ عَنْ حَدِّ الْقِبْلَةِ لِقِلَّةِ أَنْصَاب الْحَرَمِ وَ إِذَا اِنْحَرَفَ الْإِنْسَانُ ذَاتَ الْيَسَارِ لَمْ يَكُنْ خَارِجاً عَنْ
حَدَّ الْقِبْلَةِ.
ومن كان في المسجد الحرام صلى إلى الكعبة إلى إي جوانبها شاء، ومصلى في الكعبة صلى إلى أي جوانبها شاء، وأفضل
ذلك أن يقف بين العمودين على لبلاطة الحمراء، ويستقبل الركن الذي فيه الحجر الأسود، ومن كان فوق الكعبة وحضرت
الصلاة اضطجع وأوماً برأسه إلى البيت المعمور، ومن كاف فوق أبى قبيس استقبل الكعبة وصلى فان الكعبة ما فوقها إلى
السماء. وصلى رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وآله إلى البيت المقدس بعد النبوة ثلاث عشرة سنة بمكة وتسعة عشر شهرا
بالمدينة، ثم عيرته اليهود فقالوا له: إنك تابع لقبلتنا فاغتم لذلك غما شديدا فلما كان في بعض الليل خرج صلى اللّٰه عليه
وآله وسلم يقلب وجهه في آفاق السماء فلما أصبح صلى الغداة، فلما صلى من الظهر ركعتين جاءه جبرئيل عليه السلام
فقال له: " قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام الآية " ثم أخذ بيد
النبي صلى اللّه عليه وآله فحول وجهه إلى الكعبة وحول من خلفه وجوههم حتى قام الرجال مقام النساء والنساء مقام
الرجال فكان أول صلاته إلى بيت المقدس وآخرها إلى الكعبة، وبلغ الخبر مسجدا بالمدينة وقد صلى أهله من العصر
ركعتين فحولوا نحو الكعبة، فكانت أول صلاتهم إلى بيت المقدس وآخرها إلى الكعبة فسمي ذلك المسجد مسجد القبلتين
فقال المسلمون: صلاتنا إلى بيت - المقدس تضيع يا رسول الله؟ فأنزل اللّٰه عز وجل " وما كان اللّٰه ليضيع إيمانكم " يعني
صلاتكم إلى بيت المقدس، وقد أخرجت الخبر في ذلك على وجهه في كتاب النبوة.
commentary:
For those within Masjid al-Haram, it is permissible to face any side of the Ka’ba during
prayer. One praying inside the Ka’ba may also face any of its walls. However, the best
position is to stand between the two columns on the red tile and face the corner
containing the Black Stone. If someone is above the Ka’ba and it is time for prayer, they
should lie down and incline their head toward the Bayt al-Ma'mur (Heavenly House).
Similarly, anyone praying on Mount Abu Qubays should face the Ka’ba, as the Qiblah
extends upward to the sky.

Makkah after receiving prophethood and for nineteen months in Madinah.
The Jews mocked him, saying that he was following their Qiblah, causing him great

came to him and said:

حَدَّ الْقِبْلَةِ.
ومن كان في المسجد الحرام صلى إلى الكعبة إلى إي جوانبها شاء، ومصلى في الكعبة صلى إلى أي جوانبها شاء، وأفضل
ذلك أن يقف بين العمودين على لبلاطة الحمراء، ويستقبل الركن الذي فيه الحجر الأسود، ومن كان فوق الكعبة وحضرت
الصلاة اضطجع وأوماً برأسه إلى البيت المعمور، ومن كاف فوق أبى قبيس استقبل الكعبة وصلى فان الكعبة ما فوقها إلى
السماء. وصلى رسول اللّٰه صلى اللّٰه عليه وآله إلى البيت المقدس بعد النبوة ثلاث عشرة سنة بمكة وتسعة عشر شهرا
بالمدينة، ثم عيرته اليهود فقالوا له: إنك تابع لقبلتنا فاغتم لذلك غما شديدا فلما كان في بعض الليل خرج صلى اللّٰه عليه
وآله وسلم يقلب وجهه في آفاق السماء فلما أصبح صلى الغداة، فلما صلى من الظهر ركعتين جاءه جبرئيل عليه السلام
فقال له: " قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام الآية " ثم أخذ بيد
النبي صلى اللّه عليه وآله فحول وجهه إلى الكعبة وحول من خلفه وجوههم حتى قام الرجال مقام النساء والنساء مقام

صلاتكم إلى بيت المقدس، وقد أخرجت الخبر في ذلك على وجهه في كتاب النبوة.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
It was narrated from Abdul Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah that he asked Imam Jafar
Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a blind man who prayed facing a direction other than the Qiblah.
Imam {a.s} replied: "If it is still within the prayer time, he should repeat the prayer. If the
time has passed, he does not need to repeat it."
He further asked about a man who prayed during cloudy weather and afterward, when
the clouds cleared, realized he had prayed in the wrong direction.
The Imam said: "If it is still within the prayer time, he should repeat the prayer. If the
time has passed, he does not need to repeat it”.
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: أَنَّهُ سَأَلَ الصَّادِقَ عَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَعْمَى صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَقَالَ
«إِن كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَلْيُعِذْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ مَضَى ٱلْوَقْتُ فَلاَ يُعِيدُ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجْلٍ صَلّى وَ هِيَ مُتَغَيِّمَةً ثُمّ
تَجَلَّتْ فَعَلِمَ أَنَّهُ صَلَّى عَلَى غَيْرِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ فِي وَقْتٍ فَلْيُعِدْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ ٱلْوَقْتُ قَدْ مَضَى فَلاَ يُعِيدُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol 1, p. 276 • Al-Wafi, V. 7, p. 551 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 4, p. 318

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} that He
said: "For one who is confused (about the direction of the Qiblah), it suffices for him to
pray in whichever direction he faces if he does not know where the Qiblah is."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى زُرَارَةُ وَ مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «يُجْزِي ٱلْمُتَحَيَّرَ أَبَداً أَيْنَمَا تَوَجَّهَ إِذَا
لَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَيْنَ وَجَهُ الْقِبْلَةِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V 1, p. 276 • Al-Wafi, V. 7, p. 548 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 4, p. 311

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Muawiya ibn Ammar asked Him about a man who stands for prayer and, after
finishing, realizes that he had deviated to the right or the left of the Qiblah.
Imam {a.s} replied: "His prayer is valid, for the area between the east and the west is
(considered) the Qiblah."

Scholar's Note:
And this was revealed concerning those who are confused about the direction:
"To Allah {SWT} belongs the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the face of
Allah {SWT}" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:115)
text_ar:
وَ سَأْلَهُ مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقُومُ فِي الصَّلاَةِ ثُمَّ يَنظُرُ بَعْدَ مَا فَرَغَ فَيَرَى أَنَّهُ قَدِ اِنْحَرَفَ عَنِ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ
يَميناً أَوْ شِمَالاً فَقَالَ لَهُ «قَدْ مَضَتْ صَلاَثُهُ وَ مَا بَيْنَ ٱلْمَشرِقِ وَ الْمَعْرِبِ قِبْلَةً.
ونزلت هذه في قبلة المتحير " ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله.
commentary:
And this was revealed concerning those who are confused about the direction:
"To Allah {SWT} belongs the east and the west; wherever you turn, there is the face of
Allah {SWT}" (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:115)

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal {a.s}
that He said:
"If a seepage (liquid or discharge) appears behind a latrine (toilet) and it is in the
direction of the Qiblah, one should cover it with something."

Scholar's Note:
Nothing that passes in front of a Muslim while he is praying - whether it be a dog, a
woman, a donkey, or anything else - invalidates the prayer.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي اَلْحَسَنِ الْأَوْلِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا ظَهَرَ النَّزُ مِنْ خَلْفِ الْكَنِيفِ
وَ هُوَ فِي الْقِبْلَةٍ يَسْتُرُهُ بِشَيْءٍ.
ولا يقطع صلاة المسلم شئ يمر بين يديه من كلب أو امرأة أو حمار أو غير ذلك.
commentary:
Nothing that passes in front of a Muslim while he is praying - whether it be a dog, a
woman, a donkey, or anything else - invalidates the prayer.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en: The Messenger of Allah {saws} forbade spitting in the direction of the Qiblah.
text_ar: - وَ نَهَى رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ، عَنِ الْبُزَاقِ فِي الْقِبْلَةِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Volume 1, p. 277 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 500 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 319
text_chunk: The Messenger of Allah {saws} forbade spitting in the direction of the Qiblah.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
The Prophet {saws} saw phlegm (or a spittle) in the mosque. He walked over to it
with a palm branch from the branches of Ibn Tab and scraped it off, then returned
backward and continued his prayer.
And Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "This opens many doors regarding
(permissible) actions during prayer."
text_ar:
وَ رَأْى ص نُخَامَةً فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فَمَشَى إِلَيْهَا بِعُرْجُونٍ مِنْ عَرَاجِينِ اِبْنِ طَابٍ فَحَكُهَا ثُمَّ رَجَعَ الْقَهْقَرَى فَبَنَى
عَلَى صَلاَتِهِ وَقَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «وَ هَذَا يَفْتَحُ مِنَ الصَّلاَةِ أَبْوَاباً كَثِيرَةً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Volume 1, p. 277 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 500

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
The Prophet, forbade engaging in sexual intercourse while facing or with one's
back to the Qiblah.
He also forbade facing the Qiblah when urinating or defecating.
text_ar:
وَ نَهَى صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ عَنِ الْجِمَاعِ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ مُسْتَدْبِرَهَا وَ نَهَى عَنِ اِسْتِقْبَالِ الْقِبْلَةِ بِبَوْلٍ أَوْ
غَائِطِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1
text_chunk:
The Prophet, forbade engaging in sexual intercourse while facing or with one's
back to the Qiblah.
He also forbade facing the Qiblah when urinating or defecating.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"None of you should spit in front of themselves or to their right while praying. Instead,
they should spit to their left or beneath their left foot."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «لاَ يَنْزُقَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الصَّلاةِ قِبَلَ وَجْهِهِ وَ لا عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ لَيَبْزُقَ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ
وَتَحْتِ قَدَمِهِ الْيُسْرَى.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Whoever holds back their saliva out of reverence for Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and
Majestic, during prayer, Allah {SWT} will grant them health until their death."

Scholar's Note:
It has also been narrated regarding someone who cannot determine the Qiblah in a
desert or wilderness that they should pray in all four directions.
text_ar:
قَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ: «مَنْ حَبَسَ رِيقَهُ إِجْلاَلاً لِلَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَ فِي صَلاَتِهِ أَوْرَتَهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى صِحَةً حَتَّى
اَلْمَمَاتِ
وقد روى فيمن لا يهتدي إلى القبلة في مفازة أنه يصلي إلى أربع جوانب.

It has also been narrated regarding someone who cannot determine the Qiblah in a
desert or wilderness that they should pray in all four directions.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"There is no prayer except toward the Qiblah."
Zurarah asked: "And where is the boundary of the Qiblah?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "The entire area between the east and the west is the Qiblah."
Zurarah then asked: "What if someone prays facing a direction other than the Qiblah,
or on a cloudy day when they miss the correct time?"
Imam {a.s} said: "They must repeat the prayer”.
text_ar:
855 رَوَى زُرَارَةُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَلَامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لا صَلاةَ إلاً إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ وَ أَيْنَ حَدُّ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ قَالَ
«مَا بَيْنَ ٱلْمَشِرِقِ وَ الْمَغْرِبِ قِبْلَةٌ كُلُهُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَمَنْ صَلَّى لِغَيْرِ ٱلْقِبْلَةِ أَوْ فِي يَوْمٍ غَيْمٍ فِي غَيْرِ ٱلْوَقْتِ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 278 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 540 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 4, p. 312 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 1, p. 137 • Tafseer Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 2, p. 186

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
In another narration, the Imam said :
"Then turn your face toward the Qiblah and do not turn your face away from the Qiblah,
lest your prayer become invalid. Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His
Prophet in the obligatory prayer:
'Turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:144); and wherever
you are, turn your faces toward it.' Stand upright."
Prophet {saws} said: "Whoever does not straighten their spine (while standing) has no
prayer."
And lower your gaze in humility before Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic; do not raise
it to the sky. Let your gaze be directed in front of you toward your place of prostration”.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ فِي حَدِيثٍ آخَرَ ذَكَرَهُ لَهُ: «ثُمَّ اِسْتَقْبِلِ ٱلْقِبْلَةَ بِوَجْهِكَ وَ لا تَقَلْبُ بِوَجْهِكَ عَنِ الْقِبْلَةِ فَتَفْسُدَ صَلاَثُكَ
فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ لِنَبِيِّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ «فَوَلَ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرْامِ وَ حَيْثُ مَا
كُنْثُمْ فَوَلُوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ» فَقُمْ مُنْتَصِباً» فَإنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ «مَنْ لَمْ يُقِمْ صُلْبَهُ فَلا
صَلَاَةَ لَهُ وَ اِخْشَعْ بِبَصَرِكَ لِلْهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ وَ لا تَرْفَعْهُ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ وَ لَيَكُنْ جِذَاءَ وَجْهِكَ فِي مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِكَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
Imam {a.s} said to Zurarah:
"The prayer is not to be repeated except for five things: purification (taharah), time
(observing the prayer time), facing the Qiblah, bowing (ruku'), and prostration
(Sujood)”.

Scholar's Note:
My father, may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him, said in his letter to me:
"If you want to perform a supererogatory (nafl) prayer while riding, pray and turn the
head of your mount in whatever direction it faces, whether toward the Qiblah or
otherwise, right or left. If you pray a mandatory (fardh) prayer while on the back of your
mount, face the Qiblah, say the opening takbir (Allahu Akbar), and then proceed in
whichever direction your mount takes you, reciting. When you wish to bow and
prostrate, bow and prostrate on something you have with you that is permissible to
prostrate upon. Do not pray a mandatory prayer in this manner unless there is a severe
necessity. If you are walking, follow the same procedure, but when you wish to
prostrate, you must prostrate on the ground."
The letter also stated : "If a wild animal approaches and you fear missing the prayer,
face the Qiblah and pray using gestures. If you fear the animal and it continues to circle
you, move with it as it moves and pray using gestures."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ لِزُرَارَةَ: «لا تُعَادُ الصَّلاَةُ إِلاَّ مِنْ خَمْسَةِ الطَّهُورِ وَ الْوَقْتِ وَ الْقِبْلَةِ وَ الرُّكُوعِ وَ السُّجُودِ.
وقال أبي رضي اللّٰه عنه في رسالته إلي: إذا أردت أن تصلي نافلة وأنت راكب فصلها، واستقبل برأس دابتك حيث توجهت
بك مستقبل القبلة ومستدبرها ويمينا ويسارا، فان صليت فريضة على ظهر دابتك فاستقبل القبلة وكبر تكبيرة الافتتاح
ثم امض حيث توجهت بك دابتك واقراً، فإذا أردت الركوع والسجود فاركع واسجد على شئ يكون معك مما يجوز عليه
السجود ولا تصلها إلا على حال اضطرار شديد وتفعل فيها إذا صليت ماشيا مثل ذلك إلا أنك إذا أردت السجود سجدت
على الأرض. وقال فيها: إذا تعرض لك سبع وخفت فوت الصلاة فاستقبل القبلة وصل صلاتك بالايماء، وإن خشيت السبع
وتعرض لك فدر معه كيف دار وصل بالايماء.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
It is narrated that "If the wind blows strongly upon someone on a ship, and they
are unable to turn toward the Qiblah, they should pray facing the front of the ship”.
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ: «أَنَّهُ إِذَا عَصَفَتِ الرِّيحُ بِمَنْ فِي السَّفِينَةِ وَ لَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى أَنْ يَدُورَ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ صَلَّى إِلَى صَدْرٍ
السَّفِينَة.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 280 • Al-Wafi, V. 7, p. 528 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 4, p. 321

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
The Prophet {saws}, said:
"Every preacher is a Qiblah, and every one being preached to is a Qiblah for the
preacher."

Scholar's Note:
This means that during the Jumu’ah sermon (Khutbah), the Eid prayers, and the prayer
for rain (Salat al-Istisqa), the Imam (preacher) faces the people, and they face him until
he completes his sermon.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: «كُلُّ وَاعِظٍ قِبْلَةٌ وَ كُلُّ مَوْعُوظِ قِبْلَةٌ لِلْوَاعِظِ.
يعني في الجمعة والعيدين وصلاة الاستسقاء في الخطبة يستقبلهم الامام و يستقبلونه حتى يفرغ من خطبته.
commentary:
This means that during the Jumu’ah sermon (Khutbah), the Eid prayers, and the prayer
for rain (Salat al-Istisqa), the Imam (preacher) faces the people, and they face him until
he completes his sermon.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CHAPTER OF THE QIBLA
text_en:
A man said to Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"I am sometimes traveling and cannot determine the Qiblah at night."
The Imam asked: "Do you know the star that is called 'al-Jady' (the North Star)?"
The man replied: "Yes."
The Imam said: "Place it to your right, and if you are on the pilgrimage route, place it
between your shoulders”.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ رَجُلٌ لِلصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: إِنَّي أَكُونُ فِي السَّفَرِ وَ لاَ أَهْتَدِي إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ بِاللَّيْلِ فَقَالَ «أَ تَعْرِفُ الْكَوْكَبَ
اَلَّذِي يُقَالُ لَهُ الْجَديَ» قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ «فَاجْعَلْهُ عَلَى يَمِينِكَ وَ إِذَا كُنْتَ عَلَى طَرِيقِ ٱلْحَجِّ فَاجْعَلْهُ بَيْنَ كَتِفَيْكَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE AGE AT WHICH CHILDREN ARE REQUIRED TO
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"We command our children to pray when they are five years old, so you should instruct
your children to pray when they are seven years old.
We also command our children to fast when they are seven years old, as much as they
can bear of fasting for the day - whether it is until midday, more, or less. If thirst or
hunger overwhelms them, they may break their fast so that they can gradually get
accustomed to fasting and be able to bear it. So, instruct your children to fast when
they are nine years old, as much as they are capable of fasting for the day. If thirst
overwhelms them, they may break their fast."
text_ar:
باب - الحد الذي يؤخذ فيه الصبيان بالصلاة
قَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: « إِنَّا نَأْمُرُ صِبْيَانَنَا بِالصَّلاَةِ وَ هُمْ أَبْنَاءُ خَمْسِ سِنِينَ فَمُرُوا صِبْيَانَكُمْ بِالصَّلاَةِ إِذَا
كَانُوا أَبْنَاءَ سَبْعِ سِنِينَ وَ نَحْنُ نَأْمُرُ صِبْيَانَنَا بِالصِّيَامِ إِذَا كَانُوا أَبْنَاءَ سَبْعِ سِنِينَ مَا أَطَاقُوا مِنْ صِيَامِ الْيَوْمِ إِنْ كَانَ
إِلَى نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ أَوْ أَقَلَّ فَإِذَا غَلَبَهُمُ الْعَطَشُ أَوِ الْجُوعُ أَفْطَرُوا حَتَّى يَتَعَوَّدُوا الصَّوْمَ وَيُطِيقُوهُ
فَمُرُوا صِبْيَانَكُمْ بِالصِّيَامِ إِذَا كَانُوا أَبْنَاءَ تِسْعِ سِنِينَ مَا أَطَاقُوهُ مِنْ صِيَامِ الْيَوْمِ فَإِذَا غَلَبَهُمُ ٱلْعَطَشِ أَفْطَرُوا.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE AGE AT WHICH CHILDREN ARE REQUIRED TO
text_en:
It is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Qarin that He said:
"I asked Imam al-Ridha {a.s}, or he was asked while I was listening, about a man who
circumcises his son, and the boy does not pray for a day or two."
Imam {a.s} asked: "How old is the boy?"
The response was, "Eight years old."
Imam {a.s} said: "Glory be to Allah {SWT}! He leaves prayer?"
The narrator replied: "He is in pain."
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray to the extent that he is able."
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنِ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ قَارِنٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَوْ سُئِلَ وَ أَنَا أَسْمَعُ عَنِ الرّجُلِ
يَخْتِنُ وَلَدَهُ وَ هُوَ لا يُصَلِّي الْيَوْمَ وَ الْيَوْمَيْنِ فَقَالَ «وَ كَمْ أَتَّى عَلَى ٱلْغُلامِ» فَقَالَ ثَمَانِيَ سِنِينَ فَقَالَ «سُبْحَانَ ٱللَّهِ
يَثرُكُ الصَّلاَةَ» قَالَ قُلْتُ يُصِيبُهُ الْوَجَعُ قَالَ «يُصَلِّي عَلَى نَحْوِ مَا يَقْدِرُ».

text_chunk:
It is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Qarin that He said:
"I asked Imam al-Ridha {a.s}, or he was asked while I was listening, about a man who
circumcises his son, and the boy does not pray for a day or two."
Imam {a.s} asked: "How old is the boy?"
The response was, "Eight years old."
Imam {a.s} said: "Glory be to Allah {SWT}! He leaves prayer?"
The narrator replied: "He is in pain."
Imam {a.s} said: "He should pray to the extent that he is able."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE AGE AT WHICH CHILDREN ARE REQUIRED TO PRAY
text_en:
Abdullah ibn Fadalah narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
and Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"When a boy reaches the age of three, he should be instructed to say 'la illaha illa Allah
{SWT}' seven times.
Then he is left until he completes three years, seven months, and twenty days, at
which point he is instructed to say 'Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah {saws}' seven
times.
He is then left until he reaches four years of age, after which he is instructed to say
seven times, 'May Allah {SWT} bless Muhammad and his family.'
He is then left until he turns five years old and is asked: 'Which hand is your right and
which is your left?' When he recognizes this, his face is turned toward the Qiblah, and
he is told to prostrate.
He is then left until he turns seven years old, at which point he is told to wash his face
and hands. When he washes them, he is told to pray.
He is then left until he reaches the age of nine. At nine, he is taught the proper way of
performing ablution (wudu) and is disciplined for neglecting it. He is also instructed to
perform prayer and disciplined for neglecting it.
When he has learned wudu and prayer, Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, forgives
him and his parents, if Allah {SWT} wills."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَنْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ وَ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ قَالَ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا بَلَغَ ٱَلْغَلامُ
ثَلاَثَ سِنِينَ يُقَالُ لَهُ قُلْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلَّ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ ثُمَّ يُثْرَكُ حَتَّى يَتِمّ لَهُ ثَلاَثُ سِنِينَ وَ سَبْعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَ عِشرُونَ يَوْماً
فَيُقَالَ لَهُ قُلْ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ وَ يُثْرَكُ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ لَهُ أَرْبَعُ سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يُقَالَ لَهُ قُلْ سَبْعَ مَرَّاتٍ: صَلَّى اَللّهُ
عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَ آلِهِ - ثُمَّ يُثْرَكُ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ لَهُ خَمْسُ سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يُقَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهُمَا يَمِينُكَ وَ أَيُّهُمَا شِمَالُكَ فَإِذَا عَرَفَ ذَلِكَ
حُوِّلَ وَجْهُهُ إِلَى الْقِبْلَةِ وَ يُقَالُ لَهُ أُسْجُدْ ثُمَّ يُثْرَكُ حَتَّى يَتِمَ لَهُ سَبْعُ سِنِينَ فَإِذَا تَمَّ لَهُ سَبْعُ سِنِينَ قِيلَ لَهُ اِغْسِلْ
وَجْهَكَ وَ كَفَّيْكَ فَإِذَا غَسَلَهُمَا قِيلَ لَهُ صَلَّ ثُمَّ يُثْرَكُ حَتَّى يَتِمَّ لَهُ تِسْعُ سِنِينَ فَإِذَا تَمَّثْ لَهُ عُلَّمَ الْوُضُوءَ وَ ضُرِبَ
عَلَيْهِ وَ أَمِرَ بِالصَّلاَةِ وَ ضُرِبَ عَلَيْهَا فَإِذَا تَعَلَّمَ الْوُضُوءَ وَ الصَّلاةَ غَفَرَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ لَهُ وَ لِوَالِدَيْهِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF
text_en:
Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrate from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} :
"When the Messenger of Allah {saws} was taken on the night journey (Isra'), the time for
prayer arrived, and Archangel Jibril {a.s} called the adhan (call to prayer).
When He said 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar' (Allah {SWT} is the Greatest, Allah {SWT} is the
Greatest), the angels said 'Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar.'
When He said 'Ashhadu an la ilaha illallah {SWT}' (I bear witness that there is no god but
Allah {SWT}), the angels said: 'He has renounced rivals (associating others with Allah
{SWT}).'
When He said 'Ashhadu anna Muhammadan Rasulullah' (I bear witness that
Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah {saws}), the angels said: 'A Prophet has been sent.'
When He said 'Hayya 'ala as-Salah' (Come to prayer), the angels said: 'He calls to the
worship of his Lord {AZJ}.'
When He said 'Hayya 'ala al-Falah' (Come to success), the angels said: 'Success is for
the one who follows him.'".
text_ar:
باب - الأذان والإقامة وثواب المؤذنين
رَوَى حَفْصُ بْنُ البَخْتَرِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لَمَّا أُسْرِيَ بِرَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ
آلِهِ حَضَرَتِ الصَّلاَةُ فَأَذَّنَ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ فَلَمَّا قَالَ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ فَلَمًّا
قَالَ أَشهَدُ أَنْ لا إِلَهَ إِلَّ اللَّهُ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلائِكَةُ خَلَعَ ٱلْأَنْدَادَ فَلَمّا قَالَ أَشهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّداً رَسُولُ اللَّهِ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ نَبِيّ
بُعِثَ فَلَمًا قَالَ حَيٍّ عَلَى الصَّلاَةِ قَالَتِ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ حَثَّ عَلَى عِبَادَةِ رَبَّهِ فَلَمّا قَالَ حَيَّ عَلَى ٱلْفَلاَحِ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ أُفْلَحَ
مَنِ اِتَّبَعَهُ

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
text_en:
Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said: "Archangel Jibril {a.s} descended with the adhan (call to prayer) upon
Messenger of Allah {saws} while his head was resting in the lap of Imam Ali {a.s}. Archangel
Jibril {a.s} pronounced the adhan and the iqamah (second call to prayer).
When the Messenger of Allah {saws} awoke, He said: 'O’ Ali, did you hear?'
Imam {a.s} replied: 'Yes, O’ Messenger of Allah {saws}.'
He {saws} said: 'Did you memorize it?'
Imam {a.s} replied: 'Yes.'
The Prophet {saws} then said: 'Call Bilal and teach him,'
So Imam Ali {a.s} called Bilal and taught him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مَنْصُورُ بْنُ حَازِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «هَبَطَ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ بِالْأَذَانِ عَلَى
رَسُولِ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلهِ وَ كَانَ رَأْسُهُ فِي حَجْرٍ عَلِيَّ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَأَذَنَ جَبْرَئِيلُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ وَ أَقَامَ فَلَمًا
اِنْتَبَهَ رَسُولُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ «يَا عَلِيْ سَمِعْتَ» قَالَ «نَعَمْ يَا رَسُولَ اللّهِ » قَالَ «حَفِظْتَ» قَالَ «نَعَمْ»
قَالَ « أَدْعُ بِلالاً فَعَلَّمْهُ فَدَعَا بِلالاً فَعَلَّمَهُ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE CALL TO PRAYER AND THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PRAYER AND THE REWARD OF THE MUEZZINS
text_en:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"You may give the adhan (call to prayer) without being in a state of wudu (ritual purity),
wearing a single garment, whether standing or sitting, and in any direction you face.
However, when you perform the iqamah (second call to prayer), you must be in a state
of wudu, prepared for the prayer."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى زُرَارَةُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «تُؤَذَّنُ وَ أَنْتَ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءِ فِي ثَوْبِ وَاجِدٍ قَائِماً أَوْ
قَاعِداً وَ أَيْنَمَا تَوَجَّهْتَ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا أَقَمْتَ فَعَلَى وُضُوءٍ مُتَهَيِّئاً لِلصَّلاَةِ.
