author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
In a narration from Zurarah about Imam Al-Baqir {a.s}, He said:
"If you are behind an Imam, do not recite anything during the first two rak'ahs; instead,
listen to his recitation and remain silent. Do not recite anything in the last two rak'ahs
either, for Allah {SWT}, the Almighty, says to the believers:
'When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy' (Surah
Al-A'raf 7:204). The last two rak'ahs are a continuation of the first two."
text_ar:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «وَ إِنْ كُنْتَ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ فَلا تَقْرَأَنّ شَيْئاً فِي الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ
وَ أَنْصِتْ لِقِرَاءَتِهِ وَ لا تَقْرَأْنَّ شَيْئاً فِي الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ، «وَ إِذا قُرِئَ الْقُرْآنُ » يَعْنِي
فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ «فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ وَ أَنْصِتُوا لَعَلَكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ » فَالْأَخِيرَتَانِ تَبَعاً لِلْأَوْلَتَيْنِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 392 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1200 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 355 • Tafsir Kanz al-Daqa’iq, Part 5, p. 270
text_chunk:
In a narration from Zurarah about Imam Al-Baqir {a.s}, He said:
"If you are behind an Imam, do not recite anything during the first two rak'ahs; instead,
listen to his recitation and remain silent. Do not recite anything in the last two rak'ahs
either, for Allah {SWT}, the Almighty, says to the believers:
'When the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy' (Surah
Al-A'raf 7:204). The last two rak'ahs are a continuation of the first two."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Bakr ibn Muhammad Al-Azdi narrated by Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} that He said: "I dislike it for a person to pray behind the Imam in a prayer where the
recitation is not audible, and he stands there like a donkey."
I (Bakr) asked: "May I be your ransom, what should he do then?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should engage in tasbih (glorification)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى بَكْرُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ الْأَزْدِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِنَّي أَكْرَهُ لِلْمَرْءِ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ خَلْفَ
اَلْإِمَامِ صَلاَةً لا يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بالْقِرَاءَةِ فَيَقُومَ كَأَنَّهُ جِمَارٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ فَيَصْنَعُ مَا ذَا قَالَ «يُسَبِّحُ.
cross_references: Qurb al-Isnād, Part 1, p. 37 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 392 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 276 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1205 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 360 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 79

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Umar ibn Udhayna narrated from Zurarah by Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-
Baqir {a.s} that He said:
"If a person joins a congregational prayer after some of it has passed but counts their
prayer as valid behind the Imam, then what they have caught counts as the beginning
of their prayer.
For example, if they join the Dhuhr, Asr, or Isha prayers and catch two rak'ahs and miss
two, they should recite Surah Al-Fatiha (the Mother of the Book) quietly in each of the
two rak'ahs they perform behind the Imam.
When the Imam completes the prayer (with taslim), the individual should stand and
complete their remaining two rak'ahs, during which they do not recite but engage in
tasbih (glorification), tahleel (saying 'La ilaha illAllah {SWT}'), and supplication without
recitation. If the person joins and catches one rak'ah, they should recite Surah Al-
Fatiha quietly in that rak'ah behind the Imam.
When the Imam finishes with taslim, the individual should stand, recite Surah Al-
Fatiha, sit for tashahhud, then stand and complete two more rak'ahs without
recitation."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عُمَرُ بْنُ أَذَيْنَةَ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا أَدْرَكَ الرّجُلُ بَعْضَ الصَّلاةِ وَ فَاتَهُ
بَعْضّ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ يَحْتَسِبُ بِالصَّلاَةِ خَلْفَهُ جَعَلَ مَا أَدْرَكَ أَوّلَ صَلاَتِهِ إِنْ أَدْرَكَ مِنَ الظُّهْرِ أَو الْعَصْرِ أَو الْعِشَاءِ الْآخِرَةِ
رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ فَاتَتْهُ رَكْعَتَانٍ قَرَأْ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ مِمّا أَدْرَكَ خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ فِي نَفْسِهِ بِأُمّ الْكِتَابِ ، فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ ٱلْإِمَامُ قَامَ
فَصَلّى الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ لا يَقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا إِنَّمَا هُوَ تَسْبِيحُ وَ تَهْلِيلٌ وَ دُعَاءً لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا قِرَاءَةً وَ إِنْ أَدْرَكَ رَكْعَةً قَرَأَ فِيهَا خَلْفَ
اَلْإِمَامِ فَإِذَا سَلَّمَ الْإِمَامُ قَامَ فَقَرَأَ أُمَّ الْكِتَابِ، ثُمَّ قَعَدَ فَتَشَهْدَ ثُمَّ قَامَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ لَيْسَ فِيهِمَا قِرَاءَةً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi narrated from Zurarah from Imam Al-Sadiq {a.s}
who said: I asked him about a person who is behind the Imam, and the Imam prolongs
the tashahhud (sitting for testimony).
Imam {a.s} said: "He may perform the taslim (salutation of peace) and leave if he
wishes."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عُبَيْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عَلِيَّ الْحَلَبِيْ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ
خَلْفَ ٱلْإِمَامِ فَيُطِيلُ ٱلْإِمَامُ التَّشَهْدَ قَالَ «يُسَلَّمُ وَ يَمْضِي لِحَاجَتِهِ إِنْ أَحَبَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 393 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 2, p. 317 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Part 2, p. 349 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1273 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 6, p. 416 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 413

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ishaq ibn Ammar asked Imam {a.s}: "I enter the mosque, and the Imam is
already in the bowing position (ruku'), so I bow with him while I am alone and then
prostrate. When I lift my head, what should I do next?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Stand up and go to join them (the congregation). If they are standing,
then stand with them, and if they are sitting, then sit with them."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَهُ إسْحَاقُ بْنُ عَمَّارِ قَالَ لَهُ: أَدْخُلُ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ رَكَعَ ٱلْإِمَامُ فَأَرْكَعُ بِرُكُوعِهِ وَ أَنَا وَحْدِي وَ أَسْجُدُ
فَإِذَا رَفَعْتُ رَأْسِي فَأَيَّ شَيْءٍ أَصْنَعُ قَالَ «قُمْ فَاذْهَبْ إِلَيْهِمْ فَإِنْ كَانُوا قِيَاماً فَقُمْ مَعَهُمْ وَ إِنْ كَانُوا جُلُوساً فَاجْلِسْ
مَعَهُمْ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 394 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 281 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1196 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 386

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Sama’a asked the Imam {a.s} about a man who enters the mosque and finds
that the congregation has already prayed. Should he begin with the obligatory (fardh)
prayer or offer a voluntary (nafl) prayer?
Imam {a.s} said: "If there is still ample time, there is no harm in offering a voluntary
prayer before the obligatory one. However, if he fears that the time for the obligatory
prayer will end, he should prioritize the obligatory prayer, as it is the right of Allah {SWT},
the Almighty. Afterward, he may offer as many voluntary prayers as he wishes."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَهُ سَمَاعَةُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي الْمَسْجِدَ وَ قَدْ صَلَّى أَهْلُهُ يَبْدَأُ بِالْمَكْتُوبَةِ أَوْ يَتَطَوَّعُ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ فِي
وَقْتِ حَسَنٍ فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِالتَّطَوْعِ قَبْلَ ٱلْفَرِيضَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ خَافَ خُرُوجَ ٱلْوَقْتِ أَخَرَهُ وَ لَيَبْدَأْ بِالْفَرِيضَةِ وَ هُوَ حَقُّ ٱللَّهِ
عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ ثُمَّ لَيَتَطَوَّعْ مَا شَاءَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of the Imams {a.s} regarding a man
who enters the mosque and fears that he will miss the rak'ah (unit of prayer).
Imam {a.s} said: "He should bow (in ruku') before reaching the congregation and then
walk while in the bowing position until he joins them."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ: فِي الرَّجُلِ يَدْخَلُ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ فَيَخَافُ أَنْ تَفُوتَهُ الرَّكْعَةُ
قَالَ «يَرْكَعُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَبْلُغَ إِلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ وَ يَمْشِي وَ هُوَ رَاكِعْ حَتّى يَبْلَغَهُمْ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 394 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 44 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 436 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1196 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 384

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ibrahim ibn Maymun narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
regarding a man leading women in the obligatory prayer, with no other man present.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, he may lead them, and if there is a boy present, he should stand
beside him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مَيْمُونٍ عَنِ الصَّادِقِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ: فِي الرَّجُلِ يَؤُمُ النِّسَاءَ لَيْسَ مَعَهُنَّ رَجُلٌ فِي الْفَرِيضَةِ
قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ صَبِيٌّ فَلْيَقُمْ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ.
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 377 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 394 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 268 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1221 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 333 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 342

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ammar Al-Sabati narrated that he asked Imam {a.s} about a man who gives the
adhan (call to prayer) and iqamah (call to commence the prayer) intending to pray
alone. Then another person arrives and asks to pray in congregation. He asked
whether they may use the same adhan and iqamah.
Imam {a.s} replied: "No, rather he should give the adhan and iqamah again."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَنْهُ عَمَّارْ السَابَاطِيُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنِ اَلرَّجُلِ يُوَذِّنُ وَ يُقِيمُ لِيُصَلَّيَ وَحْدَهُ فَيَجِيءُ رَجُلٌ آخَرُ فَيَقُولُ
لَهُ أَتُصَلِّي جَمَاعَةً هَلْ يَجُوزُ أنْ يُصَلَّيَا بِذَلِكَ الْأَذَانِ وَ ٱلْإِقَامَةِ قَالَ «لا وَ لَكِنْ يُؤَذَنُ وَ يُقِيمُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 394 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 282 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 605 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 432

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"There is no problem if a young boy (who has not yet reached puberty) gives the adhan
(call to prayer), but he should not lead the prayer until he has reached puberty. If he
leads, his own prayer is valid, but the prayer of those who follow him is invalid."
text_ar:
وَ كَانَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يَقُولُ: «لا بَأسَ أَنْ يُوَذِّنَ ٱلْغُلامُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَحْتَلِمَ وَ لا يَوْمُ حَتَّى يَحْتَلِمَ
فَإِنْ أَمّ جَازَتْ صَلاَثُهُ وَ فَسَدَتْ صَلاَةُ مَنْ يُصَلِّي خَلْفَهُ
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 395 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 29 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 423 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1179 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 322

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ammar al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
who arrives at the mosque just as the Imam is concluding the prayer with the taslim
(final salutation).
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should give the adhan (call to prayer), make the iqamah (call to
commence the prayer), and then begin his prayer."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَمَّارْ السَابَاطِيُّ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَدرَكَ الْإمَامَ جينَ يُسَلَّمُ قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُؤَذِّنَ
وَ يُقِيمَ وَ يَفْتَتِحَ الصَّلاَةَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
A question was asked about a man who enters the mosque while the
congregation is already in prayer, and the Imam is ahead of him by one rak'ah. He
pronounces the takbir, and then the Imam becomes unable to continue (due to illness
or another reason) and takes the man’s hand (indicating him to lead), and he happens
to be the nearest person to the Imam.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should lead them in completing the prayer, then sit until they finish
their tashahhud (final testimony). He should gesture to the right and left with his hand
as a sign of completing the prayer (taslim) or wait until the prayer is completed by the
congregation, after which he can complete what he missed of his own prayer."
text_ar:
وَ سُئِلَ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَأْتِي الْمَسْجِدَ وَ هُمْ فِي الصَّلاةِ وَ قَدْ سَبَقَهُ ٱلْإِمَامُ بِرَكْعَةِ فَيُكَبِّرُ فَيَعْتَلُ ٱلْإِمَامُ فَيَأْخُذْ
بِيَدِهِ وَ يَكُونُ أَدْنَى الْقَوْمِ إِلَيْهِ فَيُقَدَّمُهُ فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ «يُتِمُّ بِهِمُ الصَّلاةَ ثُمَّ يَجْلِسُ حَتَّى إِذَا فَرَغُوا مِنَ التَّشَهُدِ
أَوْمَأَ بِيَدِهِ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَ الشَّمَالِ وَ كَانَ ذَلِكَ اَلَّذِي يُومِئُ بِيَدِهِ التَّسْلِيمَ أَوْ تُقْضَى صَلاَتُهُمْ وَ أَتَمّ هُوَ مَا كَانَ فَاتَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1
text_chunk:
A question was asked about a man who enters the mosque while the
congregation is already in prayer, and the Imam is ahead of him by one rak'ah. He
pronounces the takbir, and then the Imam becomes unable to continue (due to illness
or another reason) and takes the man’s hand (indicating him to lead), and he happens
to be the nearest person to the Imam.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should lead them in completing the prayer, then sit until they finish
their tashahhud (final testimony). He should gesture to the right and left with his hand
as a sign of completing the prayer (taslim) or wait until the prayer is completed by the
congregation, after which he can complete what he missed of his own prayer."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated from his father who said:
“I asked Imam Al-Ridha {a.s} about a person who bows (in ruku') with an Imam of a
congregation who is followed, and then raises his head before the Imam.”
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should repeat his bowing (ruku') with him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَهْلٍ عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ عَمَّنْ رَكَعَ مَعَ إِمَامٍ قَوْمٍ يُقْتَدَى بِهِ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ
رَأْسَهُ قَبْلَ ٱلْإِمَامِ قَالَ «يُعِيدُ رُكُوعَهُ مَعَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a
man who prays behind an Imam whom he is following and raises his head from
prostration (Sujood) before the Imam raises his head.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should prostrate again."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ الْفُضَيْلُ بْنُ يَسَارِ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ: عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى مَعَ إِمَامٍ يَأْتَمُ بِهِ ثُمَّ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ
السُّجُودِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْفَعَ الْإِمَامُ رَأْسَهُ مِنَ السُّجُودِ قَالَ «فَلْيَسْجُدْ»
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 396 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1255

Imam {a.s} said: "He should prostrate again."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Hussain ibn Yasar narrated that he heard someone asking Imam Al-Ridha
{a.s} about a man who was praying next to another man and stood on his left side without
knowing what to do upon realizing this during the prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should move him to his right side."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ يَسَارٍ أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ مَنْ يَسْأَلُ اَلرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: عَنْ رَجُلٍ صَلَّى إلَى جَانِبِ رَجُلٍ فَقَامَ
عَنْ يَسَارِهِ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَعْلَمُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ إِذَا عَلِمَ وَ هُوَ فِي الصَلاَةِ قَالَ «يُحَوِّلُهُ إِلَى يَمِينِهِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

Imam {a.s} said: "He should move him to his right side."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said:
"The women used to pray with The Prophet {saws}, and they were instructed not to raise
their heads (from prostration) before the men due to the tightness of the garments”.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ: «كَانَ النَّسَاءُ يُصَلِّينَ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ فَكُنَّ يُوْمَرْنَ أَنْ لا
يَرْفَعْنَ رُءُوسَهُنَّ قَبْلَ اَلرِّجَالِ لِصِيقِ الْأُزْرِ.
cross_references: Qurb al-Isnad, Part 1, p. 18 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 396 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1223 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 343 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 8, p. 343 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 42 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Vol. 6, p. 511

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Hisham ibn Salim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about
whether a woman can lead other women in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "She may lead them in the nafl (supererogatory) prayers, but not in the
obligatory (fardh) prayers. Moreover, She should not stand in front of them; rather, She
should stand in their midst."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ هِشَامُ بْنُ سَالِمِ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ: عَنِ ٱلْمَرْأَةِ هَلْ تَوُمُ النِّسَاءَ قَالَ «تَوُمُهُنَّ فِي النَّافِلَةِ فَأَمَّا
فِي الْمَكْتُوبَةِ فَلا وَ لا تَتَقَدَّمُهُنَّ وَ لَكِنْ تَقُومُ وَسَطَهُنَّ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 396 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 205

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} that He said:
“I asked him whether a woman can lead other women in prayer.”
Imam {a.s} said: "No, except for the prayer over the deceased (funeral prayer) if there is
no one more appropriate than her. In that case, She should stand among them in the
row, and She recites the takbir and they follow her."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى زُرَارَةُ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ قَالَ: قُلْتُ لَهُ ٱلْمَرْأَةُ تَوُمُ ٱلنِّسَاءَ قَالَ «لا إِلاَّ عَلَى ٱلْمَيَّتِ إِذَا لَمْ
يَكُنْ أَحَدٌ أَوْلَى مِنْهَا تَقُومُ وَسَطَهُنَّ مَعَهُنَّ فِي الصِّفَّ فَتَكَبِّرُ وَ يُكَبِّرْنَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V. 1, p. 397 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, P 3, p. 206 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, P 3, p. 268 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 326 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 331 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 427 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1225 • Al-Wafi, V. 24, p. 418 • Wasail Al-Shia, Part 3, p. 117 • Wasail Al-Shia, V. 8, p. 334

no one more appropriate than her. In that case, She should stand among them in the

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"A woman's prayer in her private chamber (mikhdah) is better than her prayer in her
house, and her prayer in her house is better than her prayer in the courtyard."

Scholar's Note:
Also, when a man leads a woman in prayer, She should stand behind him on his right,
with her prostration aligning with his knees.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى هِشَامُ بْنُ سَالِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «صَلاَةُ ٱَلْمَرْأَةِ فِي مِخْدَعِهَا أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صَلاَتِهَا فِي
بَنْتِهَا وَصَلاَثُهَا فِي بَيْتِهَا أَفْضَلُ مِنْ صَلاَتِهَا فِي ٱلدَارِ.
والرجل إذا أم المرأة كانت خلفه عن يمينه سجودها مع ركبتيه.
commentary:
Also, when a man leads a woman in prayer, She should stand behind him on his right,
with her prostration aligning with his knees.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 397 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 7, p. 515 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Halabi asked Imam {a.s} about a man leading women in prayer.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, he may lead them, and if there are young boys among them,
position them in front of the women, even if they are servants."
text_ar:
وَ سَألَهُ اَلْحَلَبِيُّ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَوُمُّ النَّسَاءَ قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُنَّ غِلْمَانْ فَأَقِيمُوهُمْ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِنَّ وَ إِنْ
كانُوا عَبِيداً
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 397 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 343

Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, he may lead them, and if there are young boys among them,
position them in front of the women, even if they are servants."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Dawud ibn Al-Hussain narrated that the Imam {a.s} said:
"A resident (non-traveler) should not lead a traveler, nor should a traveler lead a
resident. If a man finds himself in a situation where he must lead a congregation of
residents and completes two rak'ahs, he should then offer the taslim (salutation of
peace), take the hand of one of the residents, and place him to lead the rest. When a
traveler prays behind a group of residents, he should complete his prayer with two
rak'ahs and then offer the taslim."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى دَاوُدُ بْنُ اَلْحُصَيْنِ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: « لا يَوُمُ الْحَضَرِيُ ٱلْمُسَافِرَ وَ لاَ يَوُمُ ٱلْمُسَافِرُ الْحَضَرِيَّ فَإِنِ أبْثُلِيَ
الرَّجُلُ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ ذَلِكَ فَأَمّ قَوْماً حَاضِرِينَ فَإِذَا أَتَمّ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ سَلَّمَ ثُمّ أَخَذَ بِيَدِ أَحَدِهِمْ فَقَدَّمَهُ فَأَمَّهُمْ فَإِذَا صَلَّى
الْمُسَافِرُ خَلْفَ قَوْمِ حُضُورٍ فَلْيُتِمَ صَلاَتَهُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ وَ يُسَلَّمُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
It has been narrated: "If a person fears for himself due to those praying with
him, he should pray the last two rak'ahs and make them voluntary (nafl) prayers”.
text_ar: - وَقَدْ رُوِيَ: «أَنَّهُ إِنْ خَافَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ مِنْ أَجْلٍ مَنْ يُصَلِّي مَعَهُ صَلَّى الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ وَ جَعَلَهُمَا تَطَوْعاً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 398 • Wasail Al-Shia, V8, p. 400 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, V6, p. 467
text_chunk:
It has been narrated: "If a person fears for himself due to those praying with
him, he should pray the last two rak'ahs and make them voluntary (nafl) prayers”.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
It has been narrated: "If it is during the Dhuhr prayer, he should make the first
two rak'ahs obligatory and the last two rak'ahs voluntary.
If it is during the Asr prayer, he should make the first two rak'ahs voluntary and the last
two rak'ahs obligatory."
text_ar:
وَ قَدْ رُوِيَ: «أَنَّهُ إِنْ كَانَ فِي صَلاَةِ الظُهْرِ جَعَلَ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ فَرِيضَةً وَ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً وَ إِنْ كَانَ فِي صَلاةِ
الْعَصْرٍ جَعَلَ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ نَافِلَةً وَ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ فَرِيضَةً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 398 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1258 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 400 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Vol. 6, p. 467
text_chunk:
It has been narrated: "If it is during the Dhuhr prayer, he should make the first
two rak'ahs obligatory and the last two rak'ahs voluntary.
If it is during the Asr prayer, he should make the first two rak'ahs voluntary and the last
two rak'ahs obligatory."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
It has been narrated: "If it is during the Dhuhr prayer, he should make the first
two rak'ahs for Dhuhr and the last two rak'ahs for Asr."

Scholar's Note:
These narrations are not contradictory, and the person praying has the option to follow
any of these practices, and it is permissible.
text_ar:
وَ قَدْ رُوِيّ: «أَنَّهُ إِنْ كَانَ فِي صَلاَةِ الظُهْرِ جَعَلَ الْأَوْلَتَيْنِ الظُهْرَ وَ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ ٱلْعَصْرَ.
وهذه الأخبار ليست مختلفة والمصلي بالخيار بأيها أخذ جاز.
commentary:
These narrations are not contradictory, and the person praying has the option to follow
any of these practices, and it is permissible.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Abdullah ibn al-Mughira narrated that Mansur ibn Hazim used to say:
"If you come to the Imam and he is sitting, having already prayed two rak'ahs, say the
takbir (Allahu Akbar) and then sit. When you stand up, say the takbir again."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ قَالَ كَانَ مَنْصُورُ بْنُ حَازِمِ يَقُولُ: «إِذَا أَتَيْتَ ٱلْإِمَامَ وَ هُوَ جَالِسٌ قَدْ صَلَّى
رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَكَبِّرْ ثُمّ اِجْلِسْ فَإِذَا قُمْتَ فَكَبِّرْ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1
text_chunk:
Abdullah ibn al-Mughira narrated that Mansur ibn Hazim used to say:
"If you come to the Imam and he is sitting, having already prayed two rak'ahs, say the
takbir (Allahu Akbar) and then sit. When you stand up, say the takbir again."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said: "It is sufficient for you to recite
like a whisper to yourself when you are with them (in congregation)."

Scholar's Note:
If someone is praying with those who differ in practice and recites a verse of
prostration but does not prostrate, they should bow their head as a gesture.
When the Imam says, "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah (Allah {SWT} hears the one who
praises Him)," those behind him should say, "Alhamdulillahi Rabbil 'Alamin (All praise
is due to Allah {SWT}, the Lord {AZJ} of all worlds)" but in a low voice.
If the person is praying with them, they should say, "Rabbana laka al-hamd (Our Lord
{AZJ}, to You is the praise)."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «يُجْزِيكَ مِنَ ٱلْقِرَاءَةِ إِذَا كُنْتَ مَعَهُمْ مِثْلُ حَدِيثِ ٱلنَّفْسِ.
ومن صلى مخالف فقراً السجدة ولم يسجد فليؤم برأسه . وإذ قال الام " سمع الله لمن حمده " قال الذين خلفه الحمد لله
ارب العالمين" ويخفضون أصواتهم، وإن كان معهم قال: " ربنا لك الحمد.
commentary:
If someone is praying with those who differ in practice and recites a verse of
prostration but does not prostrate, they should bow their head as a gesture.
When the Imam says, "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah (Allah {SWT} hears the one who
praises Him)," those behind him should say, "Alhamdulillahi Rabbil 'Alamin (All praise
is due to Allah {SWT}, the Lord {AZJ} of all worlds)" but in a low voice.
If the person is praying with them, they should say, "Rabbana laka al-hamd (Our Lord
{AZJ}, to You is the praise)."

text_en:
The Messenger of Allah {saws} said: "Whoever leads a group in prayer and
reserves the supplication for himself, excluding them, has betrayed them”.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Samal who said:
"I prayed behind Abu Abdullah {a.s} for Fajr (dawn prayer). When he finished the
recitation in the second rak'ah, he raised his voice slightly as if reciting and said:
'O’ Allah {SWT}, forgive us, have mercy on us, grant us well-being, and pardon us in this
world and the Hereafter. Truly, You have power over all things.'".
text_ar:
وَ قَدْ رُوِيَ عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سَمَّالٍ قَالَ: صَلَّيْتُ خَلْفَ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ الْفَجْرَ فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ
قِرَاءَتِهِ فِي الثَّانِيَةِ جَهَرَ بِصَوْتِهِ نَحْواً مِمَّا كَانَ يَقْرَأَ وَقَالَ » اَللّهُمْ اِغْفِرْ لَنَا وَ اِرْحَمْنَا وَ عَافِنَا وَ أُعْفُ عَنَّا فِي الدُّنْيَا
و الآخرَة «إِنَّكَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
who said: "It is appropriate for the Imam to sit until those behind him complete their
prayers. The Imam should also recite the tashahhud (testimony of faith) loud enough
for those behind him to hear, but they should not make their recitation audible to him
- referring to the two testimonies (Shahadatayn). He should also audibly recite 'Peace
be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah {SWT}.'"
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى حَفْصُ بْنُ الْبَخْتَرِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يَجْلِسَ حَتَّى يُتِمّ مَنْ
خَلْفَهُ صَلاَتَهُمْ وَ يَنْبَغِي لِلْإِمَامِ أَنْ يُسْمِعَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ التَّشَهُدَ وَ لاَ يُسْمِعُونَهُ هُمْ شَيْئا يَعْنِي الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ وَ يُسْمِعَهُمْ
أَيْضاً السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادٍ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"Ibn Mas'ud corrupted people's prayers with two things: by saying 'Blessed be Your
Name, and Exalted is Your Majesty,' which was something the jinn said ignorantly, and
Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, narrated it from them, and by saying 'Peace be upon us and
upon the righteous servants of Allah {SWT}'."

Scholar's Note:
This refers to the first tashahhud. However, in the second tashahhud after the two
testimonies (Shahadatayn), there is no problem because when the worshipper
completes the two testimonies in the final tashahhud, they have concluded their
prayer.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «أَفْسَدَ إِبْنُ مَسْعُودٍ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ صَلاَتَهُمْ بِشَيْئَيْنِ بِقَوْلِهِ تَبَارَكَ اِسْمُكَ وتَعَالَى
جَدُّكَ وَ هَذَا شَيْءٌ قَالَتْهُ الْجِنّ بِجَهَالَةٍ فَحَكَاهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَنْهَا وَ بِقَوْلِهِ السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَ عَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ.
يعني في التشهد الأول، وأما في التشهد الثاني بعد الشهادتين فلا بأس به لان المصلي إذا تشهد الشهادتين في التشهد
الأخير فقد فرغ من الصلاة.
commentary:
This refers to the first tashahhud. However, in the second tashahhud after the two
testimonies (Shahadatayn), there is no problem because when the worshipper
completes the two testimonies in the final tashahhud, they have concluded their
prayer.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about a
man who is behind an Imam and the Imam prolongs the tashahhud, causing the man
to feel the urge to urinate, fear missing something, or experience pain. What should he
do?
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should perform the taslim (salutation of peace), leave, and leave
the Imam."

Scholar's Note:
The Imam should not leave his place of prayer until those behind him complete their
prayers, but if he does stand up, there is no blame on him.
My father, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, wrote to me in his letter:
If wind or anything else that breaks wudu' comes from you, or you remember that you
are not in a state of wudu', then say the Taslim, leave, and appoint someone else to
lead the congregation in completing the prayer. Then, perform wudu' and repeat your
prayer.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَلِيْ بْنُ جَعْفَرِ أَخَاهُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ خَلْفَ إِمَامٍ فَيَطُولُ فِي
التَّشَهْدِ فَيَأْخُذُهُ الْبَوْلُ أَوْ يَخَافُ عَلَى شَيْءٍ أَنْ يَفُوتَ أَوْ يَعْرِضُ لَهُ وَجَعْ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يُسَلَّمُ وَ يَنْصَرِفُ وَ
يَدَعُ الْإِمَامَ.
وعلى الامام أن لا يقوم من مصلاه حتى يتم من خلفه الصلاة، فإن قام فلاشئ عليه. وقال أبي رحمه اللّٰه في رسالته ألي:
إن خرجت منك ريح أو غيرها مما ينقض الوضوء أو ذكرت أنك على غير وضوء فسلم في أي حال كنت في الصلاة وقدم
رجلا يصلي بالقوم بقية صلاتهم وتوض وأعد صلاتك.
commentary:
The Imam should not leave his place of prayer until those behind him complete their
prayers, but if he does stand up, there is no blame on him.
My father, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, wrote to me in his letter:
If wind or anything else that breaks wudu' comes from you, or you remember that you
are not in a state of wudu', then say the Taslim, leave, and appoint someone else to
lead the congregation in completing the prayer. Then, perform wudu' and repeat your
prayer.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali {a.s} said:
"If an Imam leading the prayer realizes during the prayer that he is in a state of janabah
(major ritual impurity) due to forgetfulness, or if he experiences a minor impurity,
nosebleed, or a disturbance in his stomach, he should place his garment over his nose
and leave the prayer.
He should take the hand of a man to lead the prayer in his place, then perform wudu'
and complete what remains of his prayer.
If he is in a state of janabah, he should perform ghusl (ritual purification bath) and then
repeat the entire prayer."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُوْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «مَا كَانَ مِنْ إِمَامِ تَقَدَّمَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ وَ هُوَ جُنُبٌ نَاسِياً أَوْ أَحْدَثَ حَدَثاً
أَوْ رَعَفَ رُعَافاً أَوْ أَزَّ أَزاً فِي بَطْنِهِ فَلْيَجْعَلْ ثَوْبَهُ عَلَى أَئفِهِ ثُمّ ليَنْصَرِفُ وَ لَيَأْخُذْ بِيَدِ رَجُلٍ فَلْيَصَلّ مَكَانَهُ ثُمَّ ليَتَوَضَّأُ
وَلْيُتِمّ مَا سَبَقَهُ بِهِ مِنَ الصَّلاَةِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ جُنُبا فَلْيَفْتَسِلْ وَ لَيُصَلَ الصَّلاَةَ كُلَّهَا.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 402 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 426

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Muawiya ibn Maysara narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
who said:
"It is not appropriate for the Imam, if he becomes impure (breaks his wudu'), to appoint
someone else to lead except for someone who was present from the beginning of the
iqamah (call to start the prayer). If he appoints someone who has missed a rak'ah, it
should not be done."
Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from him {a.s} that He said:
"When the Imam completes his prayer with the congregation, he should gesture to
them to the right and left so they can disperse, and then he should complete whatever
part of the prayer he missed."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ مَيْسَرَةَ عَنِ الصَادِقِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «لا يَنْبَغِي لِلْإمَامِ إِذَا أَحْدَثَ أَنْ يُقَدَّمَ إِلاّ مَنْ
أَذْرَكَ الْإِقَامَةَ فَإِنْ قَدَّمَ مَسْبُوقاً بِرَكْعَةِ» فَإِنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ سِنَانٍ رَوَى عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا أَتَمَّ صَلاَتَهُ بِهِمْ
فَلْيُومٍ إِلَيْهِمْ يَمِينا وَ شِمَالاً فَلْيَنْصَرِفُوا ثُمَّ لَيُكَمَّلْ هُوَ مَا فَاتَهُ مِنْ صَلاَتِهِ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Imam {a.s} regarding a man who led a
congregation in prayer without wudu' (ritual purity), then left and appointed another
man to lead, but the new leader did not know what the previous Imam had prayed.
Imam {a.s} said: "Those behind him should remind him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى جَمِيلُ بْنُ دَرَّاجِ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ: فِي رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءِ فَانْصَرَفَ وَ قَدَّمَ رَجْلاً وَ لَمْ
يَذْرِ الْمُقَدَّمُ مَا صَلَّى الْإِمَامُ قَبْلَهُ قَالَ »يُذَكَّرُهُ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Zurarah asked Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who joined a group in their
prayer without intending it as his own prayer. Then, their Imam experienced an issue
(e.g., impurity) and took the hand of that man and appointed him to lead the prayer.
Zurarah asked: "Does their prayer count if they complete it with him, even though he
did not intend it as his own prayer?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "It is not appropriate for a man to join a group in their prayer without
intending it as his own prayer. Rather, he should intend it as such, even if he has
already prayed. This way, he will have another prayer counted. If not, he should not
join them. Nevertheless, the prayer of the group may be valid even if he did not intend
it as his own”.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ زُرَارَةُ لِأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ: رَجُلٌ دَخَلَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ وَ هُوَ لا يَنْوِيهَا صَلاَةً وَ أَحْدَثَ
إِمَامُهُمْ فَأَخَذَ بِيَدِ ذَلِكَ الرَّجُلِ فَقَدَّمَهُ فَصَلَّى بِهِمْ أتُجْزِيهِمْ صَلاَتُهُمْ بِصَلاَتِهِ وَ هُوَ لا يَنْوِيهَا صَلاَةً قَالَ «لا يَنْبَغِي
لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَدْخُلَ مَعَ قَوْمٍ فِي صَلاَتِهِمْ وَ هُوَ لاَ يَنْوِيهَا صَلاَةً بَلْ يَنْبَغِي لَهُ أَنْ يَنْوِيَهَا وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَدْ صَلَّى فَإِنَّ لَهُ
صَلاَةً أُخْرَى وَ إِلاَّ فَلاَ يَدْخُلَنّ مَعَهُمْ وَ قَدْ يُجْزِي عَنِ ٱلْقَوْمِ صَلاَتُهُمْ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَنْوِهَا.
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 382 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 403 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 41 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1241 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 376
text_chunk:
Zurarah asked Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who joined a group in their
prayer without intending it as his own prayer. Then, their Imam experienced an issue
(e.g., impurity) and took the hand of that man and appointed him to lead the prayer.
Zurarah asked: "Does their prayer count if they complete it with him, even though he
did not intend it as his own prayer?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "It is not appropriate for a man to join a group in their prayer without
intending it as his own prayer. Rather, he should intend it as such, even if he has
already prayed. This way, he will have another prayer counted. If not, he should not
join them. Nevertheless, the prayer of the group may be valid even if he did not intend
it as his own”.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ali ibn Ja'far asked his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s} about an
Imam who becomes impure (invalidates his wudu') and leaves the prayer without
appointing someone to continue leading. What is the status of the congregation?
Imam {a.s} replied: "There is no valid prayer for them without an Imam. Therefore, one of
them should step forward to lead the remainder of the prayer, and their prayer will be
completed."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَلِيْ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَخَاهُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ: عَنْ إِمَامِ أَحْدَثَ وَ اِنْصَرَفَ وَ
لَمْ يُقَدِّمْ أَحَداً مَا حَالُ الْقَوْمِ قَالَ «لَاَ صَلَاَةً لَهُمْ إِلاَّ بِإِمَامٍ فَلْيُقَدّمْ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضَهُمْ فَلْيُتِمَ بِهِمْ مَا بَقِيَ مِنْهَا وَ قَدْ تَمْثُ
صَلاَتُهُمْ.
cross_references: Questions of Ali bin Jaafar, Part 1, p. 256 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 403 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 283

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that he was
asked about a man who led a congregation, prayed one rak'ah with them, and then
passed away.
Imam {a.s} said: "They should appoint another man to lead them, count the rak'ah
(already prayed), and move the deceased to the back. Those who touched him must
perform ghusl (ritual purification).
If someone led a congregation while in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) or
without wudu', they must repeat their prayer, but the congregation does not need to
repeat theirs, and the Imam is not obligated to inform them. If he had to inform them,
it would cause great distress."
I asked: "How would this apply to someone who went to Khurasan or to those who are
unknown?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "This is not applicable to him (in such a case)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَلَبِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسّلَاَمُ: أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَمَّ قَوْماً وَ صَلَّى بِهِمْ رَكْعَةً ثُمَّ مَاتَ قَالَ
«يُقَدِّمُونَ رَجُلاً آخَرَ فَيَعْتَدْ بِالرَّكْعَةِ وَ يَطْرَحُونَ الْمَيِّتَ خَلْفَهُمْ وَ يَفْتَسِلُ مَنْ مَسَّهُ وَ مَنْ صَلَّى بِقَوْمٍ وَ هُوَ جُنْبٌ
أَوْ عَلَى غَيْرِ وُضُوءِ فَعَلَيْهِ الْإِعَادَةُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَنْ يُعِيدُوا وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُعْلِمَهُمْ وَ لَوْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ لَهَلَكَ»
قَالَ قُلْتُ كَيْفَ كَانَ يَصْنَعُ بِمَنْ قَدْ خَرَجَ إِلَى خُرَاسَانَ وَ كَيْفَ كَانَ يَصْنَعُ بِمَنْ لا يَعْرِفُ قَالَ «هَذَا عَنْهُ مَوْضُوعُ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"If you miss a part of the prayer with the Imam, consider what you perform upon joining
as the beginning of your prayer, and do not consider the beginning of your prayer as its
end”.

Scholar's Note:
If the Imam makes you sit at a place where you should stand, you should sit lightly
(without fully resting) and not sit in a fully settled manner.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَلَبِيْ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا فَاتَكَ شَيْءَ مَعَ الإِمَامِ فَاجْعَلْ أَوَّلَ صَلاَتِكَ
مَا اِسْتَقْبَلْتَ مِنْهَا وَ لا تَجْعَلْ أَوَّلَ صَلاَتِكَ آخِرَهَا.
ومن أجلسه الامام في موضع يجب أن يقوم فيه تجافي وأقعي إقعاء ولم يجلس ممكنا.
commentary:
If the Imam makes you sit at a place where you should stand, you should sit lightly
(without fully resting) and not sit in a fully settled manner.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ubayd ibn Zurarah reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
regarding a man who joined the prayer with the Imam but had missed one rak'ah. After
the Imam concluded the prayer, he left with the people and then remembered that he
had missed a rak'ah.
Imam {a.s} said: "He should perform one rak'ah”.
text_ar:
وروى عبيد بن زرارة عن أبي عبد اللّٰه عليه السلام " في رجل دخل مع الامام في الصلاة وقد سبقه
بركعة فلما فرغ الامام خرج مع الناس، ثم ذكر أنه فاتته ركعة، قال: يعيد ركعة واحدة.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 405 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 374

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
In the book of Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi and in the Nawadir of Muhammad
ibn Abi Umayr, it is narrated that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said regarding
a man who led a group in prayer from the time they left Khurasan until they reached
Mecca, and then it was discovered that he was a Jew or a Christian:
"They do not need to repeat their prayers”.

Scholar's Note:
I also heard a group of our elders say: They are not required to repeat any prayers in
which he recited aloud, but they must repeat those prayers in which he led them
silently. The detailed hadith takes precedence over the general statement.
text_ar:
وَ فِي كِتَابِ زِيَادِ بْنِ مَرْوَانَ ٱلْقَنْدِيِّ وَ فِي نَوَادِرٍ مُحَمَدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرِ أَنَّ الصَادِقَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي
رَجْلٍ صَلّى بِقَوْمٍ مِنْ جِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ خُرَاسَانَ حَتَّى قَدِمُوا مَكَّةَ فَإِذَا هُوَ يَهُودِيّ أَوْ نَصْرَانِيّ قَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِمْ
إعَادَةٌ.
وسمعت جماعة من مشايخنا يقلون: إنه ليس عليهم إعادة شئ مما جهر فيه وعليهم إعادة ما صلى بهم مما لم يجهر فيه،
والحديث المفصل يحكم على المجمل.
commentary:
I also heard a group of our elders say: They are not required to repeat any prayers in
which he recited aloud, but they must repeat those prayers in which he led them
silently. The detailed hadith takes precedence over the general statement.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ali ibn Ja'far was asked about his brother Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}
about a woman leading other women in prayer:
"What is the limit of raising her voice in the takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') and in
recitation?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "To the extent that they can hear her."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَلِيْ بْنُ جَعْفَرِ أَحَاهُ مُوسَى بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ: عَنِ الْمَرْأَةِ تَوُمُّ النِّسَاءَ مَا حَدُّ رَفْعِ صَوْتِهَا
بالتَكْبِيرِ وَ الْقِرَاءَةِ فَقَالَ «قَدْرُ مَا تُسْمِعُ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ammar al-Sabati narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who
said:
"I asked him about a man who, while praying behind an Imam, forgets to say the tasbih
(glorification) during Sujood (prostration) or ruku' (bowing) or forgets to say something
between the two prostrations."
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no obligation upon him (no penalty)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَمَّارْ السَّابَاطِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ الرّجُلِ يَنْسَى وَ هُوَ خَلْفَ ٱلْإِمَامِ أَنْ
يُسَبَّحَ فِي السُّجُودِ أَوْ فِي الرُّكُوعِ أَوْ يَنْسَى أَنْ يَقُولَ بَيْنَ السَّجْدَتَيْنِ شَيْئاً قَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءْ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 405 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 278 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1253 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 240 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 249

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} sked a man:
"What do these people say about a person who misses two rak'ahs with the Imam?"
The man replied: "They say he should recite Al-Hamd (Surah Al-Fatiha) and a Surah in
the two rak'ahs."
Imam {a.s} said: "This would reverse his prayer, making the beginning the end."
The man then asked: "So what should he do?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should recite Surah Al-Fatiha in each rak'ah”.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ لِرَجُلٍ «أَيِّ شَيْءٍ يَقُولُ هَؤلاءِ فِي الرَّجُلِ إِذَا فَاتَتَهُ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ الرَّكْعَتَانِ»
قُلْتُ يَقُولُونَ يَقْرَأْ فِي الرَكْعَتَيْنِ بِالْحَمْدِ وَ سُورَةِ فَقَالَ «هَذَا يُقَلَّبُ صَلاَتَهُ فَيَجْعَلُ أَوْلَهَا آخِرَهَا)) قُلْتُ فَكَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ
قَالَ «يَقْرَأَ فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ فِي كُلِّ رَكْعَةٍ
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 405 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 46 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 437 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 389 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 82, p. 95 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 54

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ammar al-Sabati asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} about a man
who becomes forgetful while praying behind an Imam after beginning the prayer. He
neither said anything, made the takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar'), glorified (did tasbih), nor
recited the tashahhud until the Imam concluded the prayer with the taslim.
Imam {a.s} said: "His prayer is valid, and there is no obligation upon him. If he was
forgetful while praying behind the Imam, he is not required to perform the two
prostrations for forgetfulness because the Imam is responsible for the prayer of those
who pray behind him”.
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ عَمَّارْ السَّابَاطِيُّ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: عَنْ رَجُلٍ سَهَا خَلْفَ إِمَامِ بَعْدَ مَا اِفْتَتَحَ الصَّلاَةَ فَلَمْ يَقْلْ
شَيْئاً وَ لَمْ يُكَبِّرْ وَ لَمْ يُسَبَّحْ وَ لَمْ يَتَشَهَدْ حَتَّى يُسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ «قَدْ جَازَتْ صَلاَتُهُ وَ لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ إِذَا سَهَا خَلْفَ
اَلْإِمَامِ وَ لا سَجْدَتَا السَّهْوِ لِأَنَّ اَلْإِمَامَ ضَامِنٌ لِصَلاَةِ مَنْ صَلَّى خَلْفَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 406 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 278 • Al-Istibsar, Part 1, p. 439 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1253 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 240 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 249

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated from Imam Al-Ridha {a.s} that He said:
"The Imam bears the mistakes (or forgetfulness) of those who pray behind him, except
for the opening takbir (takbirat al-ihram)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سَهْلٍ عَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «الْإِمَامُ يَحْمِلُ أَوْهَامَ مَنْ خَلْفَهُ إلا تَكْبِيرَةَ
الاِفْتِتَاحِ.

text_chunk:
Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated from Imam Al-Ridha {a.s} that He said:
"The Imam bears the mistakes (or forgetfulness) of those who pray behind him, except
for the opening takbir (takbirat al-ihram)."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Abu Basir narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that when
he asked: "Does the Imam guarantee (the correctness of) the prayer?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "No, he is not a guarantor."

Scholar's Note:
This is not contradictory to the narrations of Ammar and Imam Al-Ridha {a.s} because
the Imam is a guarantor for the prayer of those who pray behind him when they forget
something, except for the opening takbir. He is not a guarantor for what the follower
intentionally leaves out.
Another interpretation is that the Imam is not obligated to guarantee the completion
of the prayer for the congregation because it is possible that something may occur to
him before completing it, such as an event requiring him to break his prayer or realizing
that he is not in a state of purity.
text_ar:
وَ آَلَّذِي رَوَاهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ عَنِ الصَادِقِ عَلَيْهِ السَلاَمُ: جِينَ قَالَ لَهُ أَ يَضْمَنُ ٱلْإِمَامُ الصَّلاَةَ فَقَالَ «لاَ لَيْسَ
بِضَامِنٍ.
ليس بخلاف خبر عمار وخبر الرضا عليه السلام لان الامام ضامن لصلاة من صلى خلفه متى سها عن شئ منها غير تكبيرة
الافتتاح، وليس بضامن لما يتركه المأموم متعمدا.
ووجه آخر وهو أنه ليس على الامام ضمان لاتمام الصلاة بالقوم فربما حدث به حدث قبل أن يتمها أو يذكر أنه على غير
طهر وتصديق ذلك:

This is not contradictory to the narrations of Ammar and Imam Al-Ridha {a.s} because
the Imam is a guarantor for the prayer of those who pray behind him when they forget
something, except for the opening takbir. He is not a guarantor for what the follower
intentionally leaves out.
Another interpretation is that the Imam is not obligated to guarantee the completion
of the prayer for the congregation because it is possible that something may occur to
him before completing it, such as an event requiring him to break his prayer or realizing
that he is not in a state of purity.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Zurarah, from one of the Imams {a.s} who said:
"I asked him about a man who leads a congregation for two rak'ahs and then informs
them that he was not in a state of wudu' (ritual purity).
Imam {a.s} said: 'The congregation should complete their prayer because the Imam
bears no responsibility (for their prayers).'".

Scholar's Note:
The statements of the Imams {a.s} are consistent and not contradictory except when
circumstances differ.
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ جَمِيلُ بْنُ دَرَّاجِ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السِّلامُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ يُصَلِّي بِقَوْمِ رَكْعَتَيْنِ
ثُمَّ أَخْبَرَهُمْ أَنَّهُ لَيْسَ عَلَى وُضُوءٍ قَالَ «يُتِمُ ٱلْقَوْمُ صَلاَتَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُ لَيْسَ عَلَى ٱلْإِمَامِ ضَمَانْ.
جل حجج اللّٰه عليهم السلام أن تكون أخبارهم مختلفه إلا لاختلاف الأحول.
commentary:
The statements of the Imams {a.s} are consistent and not contradictory except when
circumstances differ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Abu al-Maghra' Humayd ibn al-Muthanna said:
"I was with Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} when Hafs al-Kalbi asked him:
"When I am behind the Imam and he is reciting aloud, may I make supplications and
seek refuge (in Allah {SWT})?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, you may supplicate."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَبُو الْمَغْرَاءِ حُمَيْدُ بْنُ ٱلْمُثَنَّى: كُثْتُ عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ فَسَأَلَهُ حَفْصّ الْكَلْبِيُ فَقَالَ أَكُونُ
خَلْفَ الْإِمَامِ وَ هُوَ يَجْهَرُ بِالْقِرَاءَةِ فَأَدْعُو وَ أَتَعَوَّذُ قَالَ «نَعَمْ فَادْعُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 407 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1205 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 361

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Hussain ibn Abdullah al-Arrajani narrated from Imam {a.s} who said:
"Whoever prays in his own mosque and then goes to one of their mosques and prays
with them, he will leave with the reward of their good deeds."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ اَلْأَرْجَانِيّ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَنْ صَلَّى فِي مَسْجِدِهِ ثُمَّ أَتَّى مَسْجِداً
مِنْ مَسَاجِدِهِمْ فَصَلَّى مَعَهُمْ خَرَجَ بِحَسَنَاتِهِمْ.
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Volume 3, p. 380 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 407 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 270 • The Forty Hadiths Vol. 1, p. 79 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1219 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 304 • Bihar Al Anwar, Vol. 85, p. 98

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Abdullah ibn Sinan narrated from Imam {a.s} who said:
"There is no servant who prays at the prescribed time, completes it, then joins another
group and prays with them while still in a state of wudu' except that Allah {SWT} writes
for him twenty-five degrees (levels of reward)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سِنَانٍ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «مَا مِنْ عَبْدِ يُصَلِّي فِي الْوَقْتِ وَ يَفْرُغُ ثُمَّ يَأْتِيهِمْ وَ
يُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ وَ هُوَ عَلَى وُضُوء إِلاَّ كَتَبَ ٱَللَهُ لَهُ خَمْساً وَ عِشرِينَ دَرَجَةً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 407 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 302

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
He also said to Imam {a.s}:
"There is a mosque near my door in which there are people who oppose and are
hostile. They remain in prayer during the evening, and I pray Asr and then go out and
join them in prayer."
Imam {a.s} said: "Would you not be pleased to have it counted for you as twenty-four
prayers?".
text_ar:
وَقَالَ لَهُ أَيْضاً: إِنَّ عَلَى بَابِي مَسْجِداً يَكُونُ فِيهِ قَوْمٌ مُخَالِفُونَ مُعَانِدُونَ فَهُمْ يُمْسُونَ فِي الصَّلاَةِ وَ أَنَا
أُصَلِّي الْعَصْرَ ثُمَّ أَخْرُجْ فَأُصَلِّي مَعَهُمْ فَقَالَ «أ مَا تَرْضَى أَنْ تُحْسَبَ لَكَ، بِأَزبَعِ وَ عِشرِينَ صَلاَةً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 407 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 302

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"If you pray with them, you will be forgiven to the extent of the number of those who
oppose you."
text_ar: - وَقَالَ ٱلصَادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ مَعَهُمْ غُفِرَ لَكَ بِعَدَدٍ مَنْ خَالَفَكَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 407 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 568 • Al- Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1218 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 299

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Halabi narrated from the Imam {a.s} from his father {a.s} who said:
"If you have already prayed and you are in the mosque, and the congregational prayer
is established, then if you wish, you may leave, or if you wish, you may pray with them
and consider it as a form of tasbih (remembrance and glorification)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اَلْحَلَبِيْ عَنْهُ عَنْ أَبِبِهِ عَلَيْهِمَا السَلَامُ قَالَ: «إِذَا صَلَّيْتَ صَلاةً وَ أَنتَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ فَأَقِيمَتِ الصَّلاَةُ
فَإِنْ شِئْتَ فَاخْرُجْ وَ إِنْ شِئْتَ فَصَلِّ مَعَهُمْ وَ اِجْعَلُهَا تَسْبِيحاً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 407 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Part 3, p. 279 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1250 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 5, p. 242 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 8, p. 402 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 80, p. 372

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Ishaq ibn Ammar narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that
He said: "Pray and consider it for what you missed."
text_ar: - وَ رَوَى إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «صَلِّ وَ اِجْعَلْهَا لِمَا فَاتَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Mu'awiyah ibn Sharih reported from Imam Jafar Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"If a person comes quickly while the Imam is in ruku' (bowing), one takbir (saying
'Allahu Akbar') suffices for him to enter the prayer and perform the ruku'."

Scholar's Note:
If someone joins the Imam while he is in Sujood (prostration), he should say the
takbir and join in Sujood with him, but it will not be counted (as a rak'ah).
If a person joins the Imam in the last rak'ah, he attains the merit of the congregation.
If he catches the Imam after he has raised his head from the final prostration and is
in the tashahhud (final testimony), he has caught the congregation, and there is no
need for adhan or iqamah. If he joins after the Imam has concluded with the taslim
(salutation of peace), he must perform the adhan and iqamah.
It is not permissible to have two congregations for the same prayer.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ شُرَيْحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا جَاءَ الرّجُلُ مُبَادِراً وَ الْإِمَامُ رَاكِعْ
أُجْزَأْتْهُ تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ لِدُخُولِهِ فِي الصَّلاَةِ وَ الرُّكُوعِ.
ومن أدرك الامام وهو ساجد كبر وسجد معه ولم يعتد بها. ومن أدرك الامام وهو في الركعة الأخيرة فقد أدرك فضل
الجماعة. ومن أدركه وقد رفع رأسه من السجدة الأخيرة وهو في التشهد فقد أدرك الجماعة وليس عليه أذان ولإقامة. ومن
أدركه وقد سلم فعليه الأذان والإقامة. ولا يجوز جماعتان في صلاة واحدة.
commentary:
If someone joins the Imam while he is in Sujood (prostration), he should say the
takbir and join in Sujood with him, but it will not be counted (as a rak'ah).
If a person joins the Imam in the last rak'ah, he attains the merit of the congregation.
If he catches the Imam after he has raised his head from the final prostration and is
in the tashahhud (final testimony), he has caught the congregation, and there is no
need for adhan or iqamah. If he joins after the Imam has concluded with the taslim
(salutation of peace), he must perform the adhan and iqamah.
It is not permissible to have two congregations for the same prayer.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ali al-Harrani who said:
“We were with Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} when a man came and said:
"We prayed Fajr in the mosque, and some of us left while others stayed for tasbih
(glorification). Then, a man entered the mosque and began to give the adhan. We
prevented and stopped him from doing that."
Abu Abdullah {a.s} said: "You did well to stop and prevent him firmly."
I asked him, "What if a group enters?"
Imam {a.s} said: "They should pray in a corner of the mosque without appointing an
Imam”.

Scholar's Note:
Regarding someone who forgets to say the taslim (final salutation of peace) behind the
Imam, the Imam's taslim suffices for him. If someone mistakenly performs the taslim
before the Imam, there is no harm in it.
text_ar:
فَقَدْ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيَّ ٱلْحَرَانِيّ قَالَ: كُنَّا عِنْدَ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ فَأْتَاهُ رَجُلْ
فَقَالَ صَلَّيْنَا فِي مَسْجِدِ الْفَجْرَ فَانْصَرَفَ بَعْضُنَا وَ جَلَسَ بَعْضّ فِي التَّسْبِيحِ فَدَخَلَ عَلَيْنَا رَجُلُ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ فَأَذَّنَ
فَمَنَعْنَاهُ وَ دَفَعْنَاهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «أَحْسَنْتُمْ اِدْفَعُوهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ وَ اِمْنَعُوهُ أَشَدَّ ٱلْمَنْعِ» فَقُلْتُ
لَهُ فَإِنْ دَخَلَ جَمَاعَةٌ فَقَالَ «يَقُومُونَ فِي نَاحِيَةِ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ وَ لاَ يَبْدُو لَهُمْ إِمَامٌ.
ومن نسي التسليم خلف الامام أجزاه تسليم الامام ومن سها فسلم قبل الامام فليس به بأس..
commentary:
Regarding someone who forgets to say the taslim (final salutation of peace) behind the
Imam, the Imam's taslim suffices for him. If someone mistakenly performs the taslim
before the Imam, there is no harm in it.

Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ali al-Harrani who said:
“We were with Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} when a man came and said:
"We prayed Fajr in the mosque, and some of us left while others stayed for tasbih
(glorification). Then, a man entered the mosque and began to give the adhan. We
prevented and stopped him from doing that."
Abu Abdullah {a.s} said: "You did well to stop and prevent him firmly."
I asked him, "What if a group enters?"
Imam {a.s} said: "They should pray in a corner of the mosque without appointing an
Imam”. Scholar's Note:
Regarding someone who forgets to say the taslim (final salutation of peace) behind the
Imam, the Imam's taslim suffices for him. If someone mistakenly performs the taslim
before the Imam, there is no harm in it.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CONGREGATIONAL PRAYER AND ITS VIRTUE
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Sama’a, from Imam
Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} regarding a man who was behind the Imam and
missed one rak'ah, but then the Imam mistakenly performed five rak'ahs.
Imam {a.s} said: "He (the follower) should make up the missed rak'ah and should not
count the Imam's mistake”.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ صَالِحِ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجْلٍ
سَبَقَهُ الْإِمَامُ بِرَكْعَةِ ثُمَّ أَوْهَمَ الْإِمَامُ فَصَلّى خَمْسا قَالَ «يَقْضِي تِلْكَ الرَّكْعَةَ وَ لَاَ يَعْتَدْ بِوَهَمِ ٱلْإِمَامِ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS
text_en:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said to Zurarah ibn A'yan:
"Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic, has enjoined upon people thirty-five prayers from
one Jumu’ah to the next, one of which Allah {SWT} has made obligatory in congregation
- that is, the Jumu’ah prayer.
It is waived for nine categories: the young, the elderly, the insane, the traveler, the
slave, the woman, the sick, the blind, and anyone who is more than two farsakhs
(about six miles) away.
Recitation in it must be done aloud, and ghusl (ritual washing) is obligatory for it. The
Imam is required to perform two Qunoot (special supplications): one in the first rak'ah
before bowing (ruku') and one in the second rak'ah after bowing."

Scholar's Note:
For one who prays it alone, there is one Qunoot in the first rak'ah before bowing.
This narration was uniquely transmitted by Hariz from Zurarah.
The practice that I adhere to and my teachers - may Allah {SWT} have mercy on them -
followed and issued legal opinions on is that the Qunoot in all prayers, including
Jumu’ah, is in the second rak'ah after the recitation and before bowing.
text_ar:
باب - وجوب الجمعة وفضلها ومن وضعت عنه والصلاة والخطبة فيها
قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرِ الْبَاقِرُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ لِزُرَارَةَ بْنِ أَغْيَنَ: «إِنَّمَا فَرَضَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَلَى النَّاسِ مِنَ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ إِلَى
الْجُمُعَةِ خَمْساً وَ ثَلاَثِينَ صَلَاةً مِنْهَا صَلاةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَرَضَهَا اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ وَ هِيَ الْجُمُعَةُ وَ وَضَعَهَا عَنْ
تِسْعَةٍ عَنِ الصَّغِيرِ وَ اَلْكَبِيرِ وَ الْمَجْنُونِ وَ ٱلْمُسَافِرِ وَ الْعَبْدِ وَ ٱلْمَرْأَةِ وَ الْمَرِيضِ وَ الْأَعْمَى وَ مَنْ كَانَ عَلَى رَأْسٍ
فَرْسَخَيْنِ وَ الْقِرَاءَةُ فِيهَا بِالْجَهْرِ وَ الْغُسْلُ فِيهَا وَاجِبٌ وَ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ فِيهَا قُنُوتَانِ قُنُوتُ فِي الرّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى قَبْلَ
الرُّكُوعِ وَ فِي الرَّكْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ بَعْدَ الرُّكُوعِ.»

الثانية بعد القراءة وقبل الركوع .

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Zurarah said:
"I asked Imam {a.s} upon whom is the Jumu’ah prayer obligatory?"
Imam {a.s} said: "It is obligatory upon seven people among the Muslims, and there is no
Jumu’ah prayer for fewer than five Muslims, one of whom is the Imam. When seven
gather and do not fear (any threat), one of them leads them in prayer and delivers the
sermon."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ زُرَارَةُ: قُلْتُ لَهُ عَلَى مَنْ يَجِبُ الْجُمُعَةُ قَالَ «تَجِبُ عَلَى سَبْعَةٍ نَفَرٍ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ لاَ جُمُعَةَ لِأَقَلَّ
مِنْ خَمْسَةٍ مِنَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ أَحَدُهُمُ ٱلْإِمَامُ فَإِذَا اِجْتَمَعَ سَبْعَةٌ وَ لَمْ يَخَافُوا أَمّهُمْ بَعْضُهُمْ وَ خَطَبَهُمْ.

text_en:
Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} said:
"The two rak'ahs that The Prophet {saws} added on the day of Jumu’ah are for those who
attend with the Imam because of the two sermons. Whoever prays on Jumu’ah but not
in congregation should pray it as four rak'ahs, like the Dhuhr prayer on other days."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: «إِنَّمَا وُضِعَتِ الرَكْعَتَانِ اللّتَانِ أَضَافَهُمَا النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ يَوْمَ
الْجُمُعَةِ لِلْمُقِيمِ لِمَكَانِ الْخَطِبَئَيْنِ مَعَ الْإِمَامِ فَمَنْ صَلَّى يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ فِي غَيْرِ جَمَاعَةٍ فَلْيُصَلَّهَا أَرْبَعاً كَصَلاَةِ الظُهْرِ
فِي سَائِرِ الْأَيَّامِ.

chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
The Imam {a.s} said:
"The time for the Jumu’ah prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) is on Jumu’ah at the hour when the
sun begins to decline (zawal). Its timing is the same for both travelers and residents
and is considered limited (specific). The Asr prayer on Jumu’ah is performed at the
time of Dhuhr on other days."
text_ar:
وقال عليه السلام: " وقت صلاة الجمعة يوم الجمعة ساعة تزول الشمس ، ووقتها في السفر والحضر
واحد وهو من المضيق، وصلاة العصر يوم الجمعة في الأولى في سائر الأيام.

الْمَطَرٍ

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Imam Al-Baqir {a.s} who said:
"The Jumu’ah prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) is obligatory upon seven believers: the Imam,
his judge, one who claims a right, two witnesses, and the one who executes
punishments in front of the Imam. It is not obligatory for fewer than these."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: « تَجِبُ الْجُمْعَةُ عَلَى سَبْعَةٍ نَفَرٍ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَ
لا تَجِبُ عَلَى أَقَلَّ مِنْهُمُ الْإِمَامُ وَ قَاضِيهِ وَ مُدَّعِيَا حَقٌّ وَ شَاهِدَانٍ وَ الَّذِي يَضْرِبُ الْحُدُودَ بَيْنَ يَدَي ٱلْإِمَامِ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Imam Abu Ja'far {a.s} said:
"The beginning time for the Jumu’ah prayer is when the sun declines (zawal) until an
hour has passed. Maintain it carefully, for the Messenger of Allah {saws} said:
'No servant asks Allah {SWT} for good at this time except that He grants it.'"

Scholar's Note:
My father (may Allah {SWT} be pleased with him) wrote in his letter to me:
"If you can pray six rak'ahs when the sun rises on Jumu’ah, six rak'ahs when it spreads
out, two rak'ahs before the obligatory prayer, and six rak'ahs after the obligatory
prayer, then do so."
In the Nawadir of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, it is mentioned: "And two rak'ahs
after Asr." If you perform all your nawafil (supererogatory prayers) on Jumu’ah before
the sun declines or delay them until after the obligatory prayer, it will be sixteen
rak'ahs. Delaying them is better than performing them earlier. Once the sun declines
on Jumu’ah, do not perform anything but the obligatory prayer. In the Isha' prayer of
Thursday night, recite Surah al-Jumu'ah and Surah al-A'la (Sabih isma rabbika al-a'la).
In the Fajr, Dhuhr, and Asr prayers on Jumu’ah, recite Surah al-Jumu'ah and Surah al-
Munafiqun. If you forget them or one of them during Dhuhr and recite something else,
return to reciting Surah al-Jumu'ah and Surah al-Munafiqun, as long as you have not
read half of the Surah. If you have read half, then complete it, consider the two rak'ahs
as voluntary (nafl), and repeat the prayer with Surah al-Jumu'ah and Surah al-
Munafiqun. It is not an issue if you perform Isha', Fajr, and Asr without Surah al-
Jumu'ah and Surah al-Munafiqun, though it is preferred to recite them. If someone
intends to recite a Surah in prayer but recites a different one, they should return to the
intended Surah, except for Surah Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Surah al-Ikhlas), from which
they should not turn away except during the Dhuhr prayer on Jumu’ah, when they may
return to Surah al-Jumu'ah and Surah al-Munafiqun. The dispensation to recite other
than these two Surahs during Dhuhr on Jumu’ah applies to those who are ill, in a hurry,
or traveling.
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: «أَوَّلُ وَقْتِ الْجُمُعَةِ سَاعَةَ تَزُولُ الشَّمْسُ إِلَى أَنْ تَمْضِيَ سَاعَةٌ فَحَافِظ
عَلَيْهَا فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صَلْى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ «لا يَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَبْدٌ فِيهَا خَيْراً إِلاَّ أَعْطَاهُ».
وقال أبي - رضي اللّٰه عنه - في رسالته إلي: إن استطعت أن تصلي يوم الجمعة إذا طلعت الشمس ست ركعات، وإذا
انبسطت ست ركعات وقبل المكتوبة ركعتين و بعد المكتوبة ست ركعات فافعل.
وفي نوادر أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى " وركعتين بعد العصر. وإن قدمت نوافلك كلها في يوم الجمعة قبل الزوال أو أخرتها
إلى بعد المكتوبة فهي ست عشرة ركعة، وتأخيرها أفضل من تقديمها، فإذا زالت الشمس في يوم الجمعة فلا تصل إلا
المكتوبة، وقرأ في صلاة العشاء الآخر ليلة الجمعة سورة الجمعة وسبح اسم ربك [الاعلى] وفي صلاة الغداة والظهر
والعصر سورة الجمعة والمنافقين، فإن نسيتهما أو واحدة منهما في صلاة الظهر وقرأت غيرهما ثم ذكرت فارجع إلى سورة
الجمعة والمنافقين ما لم تقرأ نصف السورة، فإذا قرأت نصف السورة فتتم السورة وجعل الركعتين نافلة وسلم فيهما، وأعد
صلاتك بسورة الجمعة والمنافقين، ولا بأس بأن تصلي العشاء والغداة والعصر بغير سورة الجمعة والمنافقين إلا أن الفضل
في أن تصليها بالجمعة والمنافقين. ومن أراد أن يقرأ في صلاته بسورة فقرأ غيرها فليرجع إليها إلا أن تكون السورة قل
هو الله أحد فلا يرجع منها إلى غيرها إلا يوم الجمعة في صلاة الظهر فإنه يرجع منها إلى سورة الجمعة والمنافقين، وما
روي من الرخص في قراءة غير الجمعة والمنافقين في صلاة الظهر يوم الجمعة فهي للمريض والمستعجل والمسافر.

text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ: «أَوَّلُ وَقْتِ الْجُمُعَةِ سَاعَةَ تَزُولُ الشَّمْسُ إِلَى أَنْ تَمْضِيَ سَاعَةٌ فَحَافِظ
عَلَيْهَا فَإِنَّ رَسُولَ اللهِ صَلْى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ قَالَ «لا يَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ عَبْدٌ فِيهَا خَيْراً إِلاَّ أَعْطَاهُ».
وقال أبي - رضي اللّٰه عنه - في رسالته إلي: إن استطعت أن تصلي يوم الجمعة إذا طلعت الشمس ست ركعات، وإذا
انبسطت ست ركعات وقبل المكتوبة ركعتين و بعد المكتوبة ست ركعات فافعل.
وفي نوادر أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى " وركعتين بعد العصر. وإن قدمت نوافلك كلها في يوم الجمعة قبل الزوال أو أخرتها
إلى بعد المكتوبة فهي ست عشرة ركعة، وتأخيرها أفضل من تقديمها، فإذا زالت الشمس في يوم الجمعة فلا تصل إلا
المكتوبة، وقرأ في صلاة العشاء الآخر ليلة الجمعة سورة الجمعة وسبح اسم ربك [الاعلى] وفي صلاة الغداة والظهر
والعصر سورة الجمعة والمنافقين، فإن نسيتهما أو واحدة منهما في صلاة الظهر وقرأت غيرهما ثم ذكرت فارجع إلى سورة
الجمعة والمنافقين ما لم تقرأ نصف السورة، فإذا قرأت نصف السورة فتتم السورة وجعل الركعتين نافلة وسلم فيهما، وأعد
صلاتك بسورة الجمعة والمنافقين، ولا بأس بأن تصلي العشاء والغداة والعصر بغير سورة الجمعة والمنافقين إلا أن الفضل
في أن تصليها بالجمعة والمنافقين. ومن أراد أن يقرأ في صلاته بسورة فقرأ غيرها فليرجع إليها إلا أن تكون السورة قل
هو الله أحد فلا يرجع منها إلى غيرها إلا يوم الجمعة في صلاة الظهر فإنه يرجع منها إلى سورة الجمعة والمنافقين، وما
روي من الرخص في قراءة غير الجمعة والمنافقين في صلاة الظهر يوم الجمعة فهي للمريض والمستعجل والمسافر.

text_en:
Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Ali ibn Yaqtin who said: "I asked Imam Abu
al-Hasan {a.s} about the Jumu’ah prayer while traveling. What should I recite in them?"
Imam {a.s} said: "Recite in them 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Surah Al-Ikhlas)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى صَفْوَانُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ يَقْطِينِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ عَنِ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ فِي السَّفَرِ
مَا أَقْرَأَ فِيهِمَا قَالَ «اِقْرَأْ فِيهِمَا «قُلْ هُوَ اللَهُ أَحَدٌ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Ja'far ibn Bashir and Abdullah ibn Jabalah narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan,
who reported from Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}: "I heard him say: 'In the Jumu’ah prayer,
there is no problem in reciting other than Surah al-Jumu'ah and Surah al-Munafiqun if
you are in a hurry.'"

Scholar's Note:
The ritual washing (ghusl) for Jumu’ah is from the time of the rising of the dawn until
the sun passes its zenith, and it’s a advised (sunnah) obligation, beginning with wudu
(ablution).
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى جَعْفَرُ بْنُ بَشِيرٍ وَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَبَلَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ
سَمِعْتُهُ يَقُولُ: «فِي صَلاَةِ الْجُمُعَةِ لا بَأْسَ أَنْ تَقْرَأَ فِيهَا بِغَيْرِ الْجُمُعَةِ وَ الْمُنَافِقِينَ إِذَا كُنْتَ مُسْتَفْجِلاً.
وغسل يوم الجمعة من وقت طلوع الفجر إلى أن تزول الشمس وهو سنة واجبة ويبدأ فيها بالوضوء .

(ablution).

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that He said:
"The time for the Jumu’ah prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) is at the sun's decline (zawal), and
the time for the Dhuhr prayer while traveling is also at the sun's decline. The time for
the Asr prayer on Jumu’ah for those who are not traveling is approximately the same
as the Dhuhr prayer on other days."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَلَبِيْ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «وَقْتُ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ وَ وَقْتُ صَلاَةِ ٱَلظُهْرِ
فِي السَّفَرِ زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ وَ وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ فِي الْحَضَرِ نَحْوْ مِنْ وَقْتِ ٱلظُهْرِ فِي غَيْرِ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ.
cross_references: Fiqh al-Reza {a.s}, vol. 1, p. 123 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 416 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1111 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 318

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
The Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s} said: "There is to be
no speaking while the Imam is delivering the sermon, and no turning around except as
is permissible during prayer. The Jumu’ah prayer was made two rak'ahs because of
the two sermons, which have taken the place of the last two rak'ahs. Therefore, it
remains as part of the prayer until the Imam descends (finishes the sermon)."
text_ar:
وَقَالَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ: «لاَ كَلاَمَ وَ ٱلْإِمَامُ يَخْطُبُ وَ لاَ اِلْتِفَاتَ إِلاَّ كَمَا يَحِلُّ فِي الصَّلاَةِ وَ إِنَّمَا
جُعِلَتِ الْجُمُعَةُ رَكْعَتَيْنٍ مِنْ أَجْلِ الْخُطْبَتَيْنِ جُعِلَنَا مَكَانَ الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَجِيرَتَيْنِ فَهِيَ صَلاَةً حَثَّى يَنْزِلَ الْإِمَامُ.
cross_references: Fiqh al-Reza {a.s}, vol. 1, p. 123 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 416 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 8, p. 1146 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 331

text_en:
Al-'Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"There is no harm if a person speaks after the Imam has finished the sermon on
Jumu’ah, during the time between the sermon and the establishment of the prayer,
whether he hears the recitation (during the prayer) or not; it is sufficient for him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْعَلاَءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا بَأْسَ أَنْ يَتَكَلّمَ الرّجُلُ إِذَا فَرَغَ
اَلْإِمَامُ مِنَ الْخُطْبَةِ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ، مَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ أَنْ تُقَامَ الصَّلاَةُ وَ إِنْ سَمِعَ الْقِرَاءَةَ أَوْ لَمْ يَسْمَعْ أُجْزَأَهُ.

"The Jumu’ah prayer with the Imam consists of two rak'ahs, but whoever prays it alone,
it is four rak'ahs."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى سَمَاعَةُ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «صَلاَةُ يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ مَعَ اَلْإِمَامِ رَكْعَتَانٍ قَمَنْ صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ فَهِيَ
أزبَعُ رَكَعَاتٍ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Hammad ibn Uthman narrated from Imran Al-Halabi, who said:
"Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who prays the
Jumu’ah prayer as four rak'ahs. Should he recite aloud?
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes, and there is Qunoot (a supplication) in the second rak'ah."

Scholar's Note:
And this is a concession that can be acted upon permissibly, but the original ruling is
that one should recite aloud (in the Jumu’ah prayer) when there is a sermon [3].
If a person prays it alone, it is treated like the regular Dhuhr prayer on other days, with
the recitation done quietly.
Similarly, when traveling, if one prays the Jumu’ah prayer in congregation without a
sermon, they should recite aloud, even if others object. Likewise, if one delivers a
sermon and then prays two units of prayer during travel, they should recite aloud.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى حَمَّادُ بْنُ عُثُمَانَ عَنْ عِمْرَانَ ٱلْحَلَبِيّ قَالَ: سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُصَلَّي الْجُمُعَةَ
أَرْبَعَ رَكَعَاتٍ أَ يَجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ وَ الْقُنُوتُ فِي الثَانِيَةِ.
وهذه رخصة الاخذ بها جائز والأصل أنه إنما يجهر فيها إذا كانت خطبة فإذا صلاها الانسان وحده فهي كصلاة الظهر في
سائر الأيام يخفي فيها القراءة وكذلك في السفر من صلى الجمعة جماعة بغير خطبة جهر بالقراءة وإن أنكر ذلك عليه
وكذلك إذا صلى ركعتين بخطبة في السفر جهر فيها .
commentary:
And this is a concession that can be acted upon permissibly, but the original ruling is
that one should recite aloud (in the Jumu’ah prayer) when there is a sermon [3].
If a person prays it alone, it is treated like the regular Dhuhr prayer on other days, with
the recitation done quietly.
Similarly, when traveling, if one prays the Jumu’ah prayer in congregation without a
sermon, they should recite aloud, even if others object. Likewise, if one delivers a
sermon and then prays two units of prayer during travel, they should recite aloud.

text_en:
Al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} who said:
"If a person catches one rak'ah (of the Jumu’ah prayer), he has caught the Jumu’ah
prayer. If he misses it, he should pray four (rak'ahs)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْفَضْلُ بْنُ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا أَدْرَكَ الرَّجُلُ رَكَعَةً فَقَدْ أَدْرَكَ ٱلْجُمُعَةَ
وَ إنْ فَاتَثَهُ فَلْيْصَلِّ أَرْبَعاً.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Al-Halabi narrated from Imam {a.s} who said:
"If you join the Imam before he bows in the last rak'ah, you have caught the (Jumu’ah)
prayer. But if you join him after he has bowed, then it is considered as four rak'ahs, like
the Dhuhr prayer."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَلَبِي عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: «إِذَا أَدْرَكْتَ الْإِمَامَ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَرْكَعَ الرَّكْعَةَ الْأَخِيرَةَ فَقَدْ أَدْرَكْتَ
الصَّلاةً وَ إِنْ أُذْرَكْتَهُ بَعْدَ مَا رَكَعَ فَهِيَ أَرْبَعْ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الظُّهْرِ
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 419 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 345

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: THE OBLIGATION OF THE JUMU’AH PRAYER, ITS VIRTUE, WHO IS EXEMPT FROM IT, AND THE PRAYER AND
text_en:
Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj narrated from Imam Abu al-Hasan {a.s} regarding
a man who prayed in congregation on Jumu’ah. When the Imam bowed, the crowd
pushed him against a wall or pillar, preventing him from bowing or prostrating until the
people raised their heads. He asked if he should bow, then prostrate, and catch up
with the row when the people stand, or what he should do.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should bow and prostrate, then stand with the row, and there is
no issue with that."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ الرّحْمَنِ بْنُ الْحَجَاجِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ: فِي رَجْلٍ صَلِّى فِي جَمَاعَةٍ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ
فَلَمَّا رَكَعَ اَلْإمَامُ الْجَأَهُ النَّاسُ إِلَى جِدَارٍ أَوْ أُسْطُوَانَةٍ فَلَمْ يَقْدِرْ عَلَى أَنْ يَزْكَعَ وَ لا أَنْ يَسْجُدَ حَتَّى يَرْفَعَ الْقَوْمُ
رُءُوسَهُمْ أَيَرْكَعُ ثُمَّ يَسْجُدُ وَ يَلْحَقُ بِالصَّفِّ وَ قَدْ قَامَ ٱلْقَوْمُ أَمْ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ فَقَالَ «يَزكَعُ وَ يَسْجُدُ ثُمَّ يَقُومُ فِي
الصّفّ وَلاَ بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 1, p. 419 • Wasail Al-Shia, Vol. 7, p. 335
