author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated from Isa ibn Yunus:
Ibn Abi Al-Awja' was one of the students of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, but he deviated from
monotheism. When asked why he abandoned his teacher's path and followed a belief
with neither foundation nor truth, he said: "My teacher was inconsistent. At times, he
spoke of free will (qadar), and at other times, of predestination (jabr). I do not know of
him adhering to any belief consistently."
He entered Mecca in rebellion and denial of those performing Hajj. Scholars disliked
engaging with him in discussions or sitting with him because of his sharp tongue and
corrupt intentions. However, he went to Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad {a.s}, sat with him
in a gathering of scholars, and said to him:
"Discussions in such gatherings are a trust, and anyone with a cough must eventually
cough. Will you permit me to speak?"
Imam Ja'far {a.s} said: "Speak."
Ibn Abi Al-Awja' then said: "For how long will you tread upon this threshing floor, cling
to this stone, worship this house built of mud and clay, and run around it like a camel
driven in frenzy? Whoever reflects on this or considers it carefully will realize that this
is an act established by someone lacking wisdom and insight."
Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} replied: "Indeed, one whom Allah {SWT} has led astray and whose
heart He has blinded finds truth bitter and fails to savor its sweetness. Satan becomes
his ally, leading him to the waters of destruction without ever returning him from them.
This is a House through which Allah {SWT} has subjected His creation to servitude,
testing their obedience by their journey to it. He has urged them to venerate and visit
it, making it the station of His Prophets and the direction (qiblah) for those who pray to
Him. It is a branch of His pleasure and a pathway to His forgiveness, established in the
utmost perfection and the gathering point of majesty and grandeur.
Allah {SWT} created it two thousand years before the spreading of the earth. It is most
fitting that He be obeyed in what He commands and refrained from what He {SWT}
prohibits and warns against - Allah {SWT}, who forms souls and shapes them into their
forms."
Ibn Abi Al-Awja' responded: "You speak of something, O Abu Abdullah, and refer to the
unseen."
Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} said: "Woe to you! How can He {SWT} be unseen, He who is
present with His creation, nearer to them 'than their jugular vein,' hears their speech,
sees their forms, and knows their secrets? Only a created being becomes unseen
when he moves from one place to another, so that the place he left becomes empty of
him, and the place he reaches becomes occupied by him. Such a being cannot know
what occurs in the place he left while being in the place he arrived at."
The Imam {a.s} continued: "As for Allah {SWT}, the Magnificent in status, the Sovereign, the
Judge, no place is devoid of Him, no place preoccupies Him, and He is no closer to
one place than to another. By the One who sent His Prophet with clear signs, definitive
proofs, and supported him with His victory, and who chose him to deliver His
messages, we affirm his claim that his Lord {AZJ} sent him and spoke to him."
Ibn Abi Al-Awja’ rose from the gathering and said to his companions: "Who cast me
into the ocean of this man's discourse? I asked you to find me a shade, and you threw
me onto burning embers!"
They replied: "You were insignificant in his assembly."
He responded: "He is the son of the one who shaved the heads of those you see
(referring to his lineage and the Imam's profound knowledge and authority)."
text_ar:
[ مَنْ أَرَادَ الْكَعْبَةَ بِسُوء]
وما أراد الكعبة أحد بسوء إلا غضب اللّٰه عزوجل لها، ونوى يوما تبع الملك أن يقتل مقاتلة أهل الكعبة ويسبي ذريتهم ثم
يهدم الكعبة فسالت عيناه حتى وقعتا على خدية فسأل عن ذلك، فقالوا: ما نرى الذي أصابك إلا بما نويت في هذا البيت
لان البلد حرم اللّٰه والبيت بيت الله، وسكان مكة ذرية إبراهيم خليل الله، فقال: صدقتم فما مخرجى مما وقعت فيه؟ قالوا:
تحدث نفسك بغير ذلك فحدث نفسه بخير فرجعت حدقتاه حتى ثبتتا في مكانهما، فدعا القوم الذين أشاروا عليه بهدمها
فقتلهم ثم أتى البيت فكساه الانطاع وأطعم الطعام ثلاثين يوما كل يوم مائة جزور حتى حملت الجفان إلى السباع في
رؤوس الجبال ونثرت الاعلاف للوحوش، ثم انصرف من مكة إلى المدينة فأنزل بها قوما من أهل اليمن من غسان وهم
الانصار وروي: أنه ذبح له ستة آلاف بقرة بشعب ابن عامر، وكان يقال لها مطابخ تبع حتى نزلها ابن عامر فاضيفت إليه
فقيل: شعيب ابن عامر، ولم يكن تبع مؤمنا ولا كافرا ولكنه كان ممن يطلب الدين الحنيف، ولم يملك المشرق إلا تبع
وكسرى. وقصده أصحاب الفيل وملكهم أبو يكسوم: أبرهة بن الصباح الحميري ليهدمه. فأرسل اللّٰه عليهم طيرا ابابيل
ترميهم بحجارة من سجيل، فجعلهم كعصف مأكول. وإنما لم يجر على الحجاج ما جرى على تبع وأصحاب الفيل لان قصد
الحجاج لم يكن إلى هدم الكعبة إنما كان قصده إلى ابن الزبير وكان ضدا لصاحب الحق، فلما استجار بالكعبة أراد اللّٰه أن
يبين للناس أنه لم يجره فامهل من هدمها عليه.
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ عِيسَى بْنِ يُونُسَ قَالَ : كَانَ إِبْنُ أَبِي الْعَوْجَاءِ مِنْ تَلاَمِدَةِ الْحَسَنِ الْبَصْرِيِّ فَانْحَرَفَ عَنِ
التَّوْجِيدِ فَقِيلَ لَهُ تَرَكْتَ مَذْهَبَ صَاحِبِكَ وَ دَخَلْتَ فِيمَا لاَ أَصْلَ لَهُ وَ لا حَقِيقَةَ فَقَالَ إِنَّ صَاحِبِي كَانَ مِخْلَطاً كَانَ
يَقُولُ طَوْراً بِالْقَدَرِ وَ طَوْراً بِالْجَبْرِ وَ مَا أَعْلَمُهُ اِعْتَقَدَ مَذْهَباً دَامَ عَلَيْهِ قَالَ وَ دَخَلَ مَكَّةَ تَمَرّداً وَ إِنْكَاراً عَلَى مَنْ
يَحْجُ وَ كَانَ يَكْرَهُ الْعُلَمَاءُ مُسَاءَلَتَهُ إِيَّاهُمْ وَ مُجَالَسَتَهُ لَهُمْ لِخُبْثِ لِسَانِهِ وَ فَسَادٍ ضَمِيرِهِ فَأَتَى جَعْفَرَ بْنَ مُحَمَّدٍ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ فَجَلَسَ إِلَيْهِ فِي جَمَاعَةٍ مِنْ نُظَرَائِهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ ٱلْمَجَالِسَ أَمَانَاتٌ وَ لابُدَ لِكُلِّ مَنْ كَانَ بِهِ سُعَالٌ أَنْ
بَسْعَلَ أَفَتَأْذَنُ لِي فِي الْكَلاَمِ فَقَالَ «تَكَلَّمْ» فَقَالَ إِلَى كَمْ تَدُوسُونَ هَذَا الْبَيْدَرَ وَ تَلَوذُونَ بِهَذَا الْحَجَرِ وَ تَعْبُدُونَ
هَذَا الْبَيْتَ الْمَرْفُوعَ بِالطُوبِ وَ الْمَدَرِ وَ تُهَزْوِلُونَ حَوْلَهُ هَرْوَلَةَ الْبَعِيرِ إِذَا نَفَرَ مَنْ فَكْرَ فِي هَذَا أَوْ قَدْرَ عَلِمَ أَنَّ هَذَا
فِعِلْ أَسَّسَهُ غَيْرُ حَكِيمٍ وَ لا ذِي نَظَرٍ فَقُلْ فَإِنَّكَ رَأْسُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ وَ سَنَامُهُ وَ أَبُوكَ أُسْهُ وَ نِظَامُهُ فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ
عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «إِنَّ مَنْ أَضَلَّهُ اللهُ وَ أَعْمَى قَلْبَهُ اِسْتَوْخَمَ الْحَقَّ فَلَمْ يَسْتَعْذِبْهُ وَ صَارَ اَلشَّيْطَانُ وَلِيَهُ يُورِدُهُ مَنَاهِلَ
اَلْهَلَكَةِ ثُمَّ لَا يُصْدِرُهُ و هَذَا بَيْتُ اِسْتَعْبَدَ اللهُ بِهِ خَلْقَهُ لِيَخْتَبِرَ طَاعَتَهُمْ فِي إِثْيَانِهِ فَحَثَّهُمْ عَلَى تَعْظِيمِهِ وَ زِيَارَتِهِ
وَ جَعَلَهُ مَحَلَّ أَنْبِيَائِهِ وَ قِبْلَةً لِلْمُصَلِّينَ لَهُ فَهُوَ شُعْبَةٌ مِنْ رِضْوَانِهِ وَ طَرِيقٌ يُؤَدِّي إِلَى غُفْرَانِهِ مَنْصُوبٌ عَلَى اِسْتِوَاءِ
اَلْكَمَالِ وَ مُجْتَمَعِ الْعَظَمَةِ وَ الْجَلَالِ خَلَقَهُ اللّهُ قَبْلَ دَحْوِ الْأَرْضِ بِأَلْفَي عَامٍ وَ أَحَقُ مَنْ أُطِيعَ فِيمَا أَمَرَ وَ أُنْتُهِيّ عَمّا
نَهَى عَنْهُ وَ زَجَرَ اللَّهُ الْمُنْشِ لِلْأَرْوَاحِ بِالصُوَرِ» فَقَالَ اِبْنُ أَبِي الْعَوْجَاءِ ذَكَزْتَ يَا أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ فَأَحَلْتَ عَلَى غَائِبٍ
فَقَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «وَيْلَكَ وَ كَيْفَ يَكُونُ غَائِباً مَنْ هُوَ مَعَ خَلْقِهِ شَاهِدٌ وَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَقْرَبُ «مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ»
بَسْمَعُ كَلامَهُمْ وَ يَرَى أَشخَاصَهُمْ وَ يَعْلَمُ أَسْرَارَهُمْ وَ إِنَّمَا ٱلْمَخْلُوقُ الَّذِي إِذَا اِنْتَقَلَ عَنْ مَكَانٍ اِشتَغَلَ بِهِ مَكَانْ وَ
خَلاَ مِنْهُ مَكَانٌ فَلاَ يَدْرِي فِي الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي صَارَ إِلَيْهِ مَا حَدَثَ فِي الْمَكَانِ الَّذِي كَانَ فِيهِ فَأَمَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الشَّأْنِ
اَلْمَلِكُ الدَّيَّانُ، فَإِنَّهُ لاَ يَخْلُو مِنْهُ مَكَانٌ وَ لا يَشتَغِلُ بِهِ مَكَانٍ وَ لَا يَكُونُ إِلَى مَكَانٍ أَقْرَبَ مِنْهُ إِلَى مَكَانٍ وَ الَذِي بَعَثَهُ
بِالْآيَاتِ ٱلْمُحْكَمَةِ وَ الْبَرَاهِينِ الْوَاضِحَةِ وَ أَيَّدَهُ بِنَصْرِهِ وَ اِخْتَارَهُ لِتَبْلِيغِ رِسَالاَتِهِ صَدَّقْنَا قَوْلَهُ بِأَنَّ رَبَّهُ بَعَتَهُ وَ كَلَّمَهُ»
فَقَامَ عَنْهُ اِبْنُ أَبِي الْعَوْجَاءِ فَقَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ مَنْ أَلْقَانِي فِي بَحْرِ هَذَا سَأَلْثُكُمْ أَنْ تَلْتَمِسُوا لِي خَمْرَةً فَأَلْقَيْثُمُونِي
عَلَى جَمْرَةِ قَالُوا لَهُ مَا كُنْتَ فِي مَجْلِسِهِ إلاَّ حَقِيراً فَقَالَ «إِنَّهُ اِبْنُ مَنْ حَلَقَ رُءُوسَ مَنْ تَرَوْنَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2
text_chunk:
It has been narrated from Isa ibn Yunus:
Ibn Abi Al-Awja' was one of the students of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, but he deviated from
monotheism. When asked why he abandoned his teacher's path and followed a belief
with neither foundation nor truth, he said: "My teacher was inconsistent. At times, he
spoke of free will (qadar), and at other times, of predestination (jabr). I do not know of
him adhering to any belief consistently."
He entered Mecca in rebellion and denial of those performing Hajj. Scholars disliked
engaging with him in discussions or sitting with him because of his sharp tongue and
corrupt intentions. However, he went to Imam Ja'far ibn Muhammad {a.s}, sat with him
in a gathering of scholars, and said to him:
"Discussions in such gatherings are a trust, and anyone with a cough must eventually
cough. Will you permit me to speak?"
Imam Ja'far {a.s} said: "Speak."
Ibn Abi Al-Awja' then said: "For how long will you tread upon this threshing floor, cling
to this stone, worship this house built of mud and clay, and run around it like a camel
driven in frenzy? Whoever reflects on this or considers it carefully will realize that this
is an act established by someone lacking wisdom and insight."
Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} replied: "Indeed, one whom Allah {SWT} has led astray and whose
heart He has blinded finds truth bitter and fails to savor its sweetness. Satan becomes
his ally, leading him to the waters of destruction without ever returning him from them.
This is a House through which Allah {SWT} has subjected His creation to servitude,
testing their obedience by their journey to it. He has urged them to venerate and visit
it, making it the station of His Prophets and the direction (qiblah) for those who pray to
Him. It is a branch of His pleasure and a pathway to His forgiveness, established in the
utmost perfection and the gathering point of majesty and grandeur.
Allah {SWT} created it two thousand years before the spreading of the earth. It is most
fitting that He be obeyed in what He commands and refrained from what He {SWT}
prohibits and warns against - Allah {SWT}, who forms souls and shapes them into their
forms."
Ibn Abi Al-Awja' responded: "You speak of something, O Abu Abdullah, and refer to the
unseen."
Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} said: "Woe to you! How can He {SWT} be unseen, He who is
present with His creation, nearer to them 'than their jugular vein,' hears their speech,
sees their forms, and knows their secrets? Only a created being becomes unseen
when he moves from one place to another, so that the place he left becomes empty of
him, and the place he reaches becomes occupied by him. Such a being cannot know
what occurs in the place he left while being in the place he arrived at."
The Imam {a.s} continued: "As for Allah {SWT}, the Magnificent in status, the Sovereign, the
Judge, no place is devoid of Him, no place preoccupies Him, and He is no closer to
one place than to another. By the One who sent His Prophet with clear signs, definitive
proofs, and supported him with His victory, and who chose him to deliver His
messages, we affirm his claim that his Lord {AZJ} sent him and spoke to him."
Ibn Abi Al-Awja’ rose from the gathering and said to his companions: "Who cast me
into the ocean of this man's discourse? I asked you to find me a shade, and you threw
me onto burning embers!"
They replied: "You were insignificant in his assembly."
He responded: "He is the son of the one who shaved the heads of those you see
(referring to his lineage and the Imam's profound knowledge and authority)."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said in another narration, in a
discussion about Islam and faith:
"If a man were to enter the Kaaba and urinate in it out of defiance, he would be
removed from the Kaaba and the Haram, and his neck would be struck."
text_ar:
وَ قَالَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ فِي خَبَرٍ آخَرَ : حَدِيثٍ يُذْكَرُ فِيهِ الْإِسْلامُ وَ الْإِيِمَانُ «وَ لَوْ أَنَّ رَجُلاً دَخَلَ
الْكَعْبَةَ فَبَالَ فِيهَا مُعَانِداً أُخْرِجَ مِنَ الْكَفْبَةِ وَ مِنَ الْحَرَمِ وَ ضُرِبَثْ عُنْقُهُ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about the words of Allah {SWT}, the
Mighty and Majestic: "And whoever enters it shall be safe." (Surah Aal-e-Imran 3:97)
Imam {a.s} replied: "Whoever enters the sanctuary (Haram) seeking refuge is safe from
the wrath of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic. Likewise, any wild animal or bird that
enters it is safe from being disturbed or harmed until it leaves the sanctuary."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar narrated:
It was brought to the attention of Abu Abdullah {a.s} that a predatory bird had taken up
a position on the Kaaba and was attacking any of the Haram's pigeons that passed by.
Imam {a.s} said: "Set up for it and kill it, for it has committed desecration (ilhad)."
text_ar:
ا اا ٣٠ه
[الإلْحَادُ فِي الْحَرَمِ وَالْجِنَايَاتُ ]
ومن أتى بموجب الحد في الحرم اخذ به في الحرم لأنه لم ير للحرم حرمة.
وَ رَوَى مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ : أَنَّهُ أَتِيَ أَبُو عَبْدِ آللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ فَقِيلَ لَهُ إِنَّ سَبُعاً مِنْ سِبَاعِ الطِّيْرِ عَلَى الْكَعْبَةِ
لَيْسَ يَمُرُّ بِهِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ إِلَّا ضَرَبَهُ فَقَالَ «اِنْصِبُوا لَهُ وَ أُقْتُلُوهُ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ أَلْحَدَ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
He (Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar) said:
I asked Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} about the words of Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic:
"And whoever intends a deviation therein or wrongdoing, We will make him taste a
painful punishment." (Surah Al-Hajj 22:25)
Imam {a.s} replied: "Every act of injustice is a form of deviation (ilhad), and striking a
servant without cause is among such deviation."
text_ar:
قَالَ : وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: « (
وَ مَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمِ نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذْابٍ أَلِيمِ )
قَالَ «كُلُّ ظُلْمِ إِلْحَادٌ وَ ضَرْبُ ٱلْخَادِمِ فِي غَيْرِ ذَنْبِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ ٱلْإِلْحَادِ.

servant without cause is among such deviation."

chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
In a narration from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}:
"Every act of injustice a person commits against himself in Mecca - be it theft,
oppression of someone, or any form of wrongdoing - I consider it to be deviation
(ilhad). For this reason, the jurists avoided residing in Mecca."
text_ar:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ أَبِي الصَّبَّاحِ الْكِنَانِيَّ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ : «كُلُّ ظُلْمِ يَظْلِمُهُ الرَّجُلُ نَفْسَهُ بِمَكَّةَ مِنْ سَرِقَةِ
أَوْ ظُلِمِ أَحَدٍ أَوْ شَيْءٍ مِنَ الظُلْمِ فَإِنِّي أَرَاهُ إِلْحَاداً وَ لِذَلِكَ كَانَ يَتّقِي الْفُقَهَاءُ أَنْ يَسْكُنُوا مَكَّةَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Abu Basir asked Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man intending to travel to
Mecca or Medina and whether it is disliked for him to carry weapons.
Imam {a.s} replied: "There is no harm in carrying weapons when leaving his hometown,
but when he enters Mecca, he should not display them."
text_ar:
[إظْهَارُ السِّلَاحِ بِمَكّةَ ]
وَ سَأَلَهُ أَبُو بَصِيرٍ : عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يُرِيدُ مَكَّةَ أَوِ الْمَدِينَةَ أَ يُكْرَهُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ مِنْهُ بِالسِّلاَحِ فَقَالَ «لا بَأْسَ أَنْ
يَخْرُجَ بِالسِّلاَحِ مِنْ بَلَدِهِ وَ لَكِنْ إِذَا دَخَلَ مَكَّةَ لَمْ يُظْهِرْهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

Abu Basir asked Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man intending to travel to
Mecca or Medina and whether it is disliked for him to carry weapons.
Imam {a.s} replied: "There is no harm in carrying weapons when leaving his hometown,
but when he enters Mecca, he should not display them."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
In a narration from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}:
"It is not appropriate to enter the Haram with a weapon unless it is placed in a sack or
concealed - meaning, the blade should be wrapped in something."
text_ar:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ حَرِيزِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ : « لا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْحَرَمَ بِسِلاَحِ إِلاَّ أَنْ يُدْجِلَهُ
فِي جُوَالِقٍ أَوْ يُغَيَّبَهُ يَعْنِي حَتَّى يَلُفَّ عَلَى الْحَدِيدِ شَيْئًا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 228 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 88 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 256

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Abdul Malik ibn Utbah asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about garments from the
coverings of the Kaaba that reach us. He inquired whether it is permissible to wear any
of it.
Imam {a.s} replied: "It is suitable for children, for covering copies of the Quran, and for
use as cushions, seeking blessings through it, if Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, wills."
text_ar:
[الإنْتِفَاعُ بِثِيَابِ الْكَعْبَةِ]
وَ سَأَلَ عَبْدُ الْمَلِكِ بْنُ عُثْبَةَ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : عَمَّا يَصِلُ إِلَيْنَا مِنْ ثِيَابِ الْكَفْبَةِ هَلْ يَصْلُحُ لَنَا أَنْ
تَلْبَسَ شَيْئاً مِنْهَا فَقَالَ «يَصْلُحُ لِلصِّبْيَانِ وَ ٱلْمَصَاحِفِ وَ ٱلْمِخَدَّةِ تَبْتَفِي بِذَلِكَ الْبَرَكَةَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

Abdul Malik ibn Utbah asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about garments from the
coverings of the Kaaba that reach us. He inquired whether it is permissible to wear any

Imam {a.s} replied: "It is suitable for children, for covering copies of the Quran, and for
use as cushions, seeking blessings through it, if Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, wills."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar: I said to Abu Abdullah {a.s}: "I
took some dust from the Maqam and soil from the House, along with seven pebbles."
Imam {a.s} replied: "What you have done is not good. As for the dust and the pebbles,
return them."
text_ar:
[كَرَاهِيَةُ أَخْذِ تُرَابِ الْبَيْتِ وَحَصَاهُ]
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَارِ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أُخَذْتُ سُكَاً مِنْ سُكَ الْمَقَامِ وَ تُرَاباً
مِنْ ثُرَابِ الْبَيْتِ وَ سَبْعَ حَصَيَاتٍ فَقَالَ «بِئسَ مَا صَنَعْتَ أَمَّا الثُرَابَ وَ الْحَصَى فَرُدَّهُ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 229 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 92 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 5, p. 232 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 220 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 3, p. 367
text_chunk:

took some dust from the Maqam and soil from the House, along with seven pebbles."
Imam {a.s} replied: "What you have done is not good. As for the dust and the pebbles,
return them."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdullah {a.s}:
"It is not appropriate for anyone to take soil from around the House (Kaaba), and if
someone takes anything from it, they must return it."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «لا يَنْبَغِي لأَحَدِ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مِنْ تُرْبَةِ مَا حَوْلَ
الْبَيْتِ وَ إِنْ أَخَذَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ شَيْئاً رَدَّهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 453

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Hudhayfah ibn Mansur said to Abu Abdullah {a.s}:
"My uncle swept the Kaaba and took some of its soil, and we use it for treatment."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Return it to the Kaaba."
text_ar:
وَ قَالَ حُذَيْفَةُ بْنُ مَنْصُورٍ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : إِنَّ عَمِّي كَنَسَ الْكَعْبَةَ فَأَخَذَ مِنْ تُرَابِهَا فَنَحْنُ
نَتَدَاوَى بِهِ فَقَالَ «رُدَّهُ إِلَيْهَا ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2
text_chunk:

"My uncle swept the Kaaba and took some of its soil, and we use it for treatment."
Imam {a.s} replied: "Return it to the Kaaba."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Zayd Al-Shahham said to Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}:
"May I take a pebble out of the mosque?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Return it or place it in another mosque."
text_ar: - وَقَالَ لَهُ زَيْدٌ الشَّحَامُ: أُخْرِجُ مِنَ ٱلْمَسْجِدِ حَصَاةَ قَالَ «فَرُدَهَا أَوِ اِطرَحهَا فِي مَسْجِدٍ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2
text_chunk:
Zayd Al-Shahham said to Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}:
"May I take a pebble out of the mosque?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Return it or place it in another mosque."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated by Al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja‘far
{a.s}, who said: "It is not appropriate for a person to reside in Mecca for a full year."
I asked: "What should he do?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should move away from it. Also, it is not appropriate for any
building to be raised higher than the Kaaba."
text_ar:
[كراهية المقام بمكة]
وَ رَوَى اَلْعَلاَءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «لا يَنْبَغِي لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يُقِيمَ بِمَكَّةَ سَنَةً»
قُلْتُ كَيْفَ يَصْنَعُ قَالَ «يَتَحَوَّلُ عَنْهَا وَ لا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُرْفَعَ بِنَاء فَوْقَ ٱلْكَعْبَةِ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 230 • Ilal al-Sharai’, Vol. 2, p. 446 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 448 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 463 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 88 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 233 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 96, p. 81

building to be raised higher than the Kaaba."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en: It has been narrated: "Residing in Mecca hardens the heart."
text_ar: - وَ رُوِيَ : «أَنَّ ٱلْمُقَامَ بِمَكَّةَ يُقْسِي الْقَلْبَ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 230 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 89 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 234

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated by Dawud Al-Raqqi from Abu Abdullah {a.s} that he said:
"When you have completed your rituals, then return, for it will make you more eager to
come back."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى دَاوُدُ الرَّقِّي عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ : «إِذَا فَرَغْتَ مِنْ نُسُكِكَ فَارْجِعْ فَإِنَّهُ أَشوَقُ لَكَ
إِلَى الرُّجُوعِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 230 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 89 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 234
text_chunk:
It has been narrated by Dawud Al-Raqqi from Abu Abdullah {a.s} that he said:
"When you have completed your rituals, then return, for it will make you more eager to

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar: I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s}
about a tree whose root is in the non-sacred area (hill) and its branches extend into
the sacred area (Haram).
Imam {a.s} replied: "The root is sanctified because of the branch's location."
I then asked: "What if its root is in the Haram and its branch extends into the hill?"
Imam {a.s} said: "The branch is sanctified because of the root's location."
text_ar:
[شَجَرُ الحَرَمِ]
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السْلاَمُ شَجَرَةٌ أَصْلُهَا فِي الْحِلِّ وَ فَرْعُهَا فِي
اَلْحَرَمِ فَقَالَ «حُرِّمَ أَضْلُهَا لِمَكَانِ فَرْعِهَا» قُلْتُ فَإِنَّ أَصْلَهَا فِي الْحَرَمِ وَ فَرْعَهَا فِي الْجِلَ قَالَ «حُرِّمَ فَرْعُهَا لِمَكَانِ
أصلِهَا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 231 • Ilal al-Sharai’, Vol. 2, p. 453 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 379 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 98 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 559 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 560 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 96, p. 153

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated from Hariz, from Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}, that he said:
"Everything that grows in the Haram is forbidden for all people, except for what you
yourself plant or cultivate."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى حَرِيزٌ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ : «كُلُّ شَيْءٍ يَنْبُتُ فِي الْحَرَمِ فَهُوَ حَرَامٌ عَلَى اَلنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ إِلاَّ
مَا أَثْبَنَّهُ أَنْتَ أَوْ غَرَسْتَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 380 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 553 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 197
text_chunk:
It has been narrated from Hariz, from Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s}, that he said:
"Everything that grows in the Haram is forbidden for all people, except for what you
yourself plant or cultivate."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Imam {a.s} said:
"The camel is to be left free in the Haram to eat whatever it wishes."
text_ar: - وَ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ : «يُخَلَّى عَنِ الْبَعِيرِ فِي الْحَرَمِ يَأْكُلُ مَا شَاءَ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 231 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 381 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 97 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 558
text_chunk:
Imam {a.s} said:
"The camel is to be left free in the Haram to eat whatever it wishes."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en: "And whatever the camels eat, there is no harm in removing it."
text_ar: - وَ مَا يَأْكُلُهُ الْإِبِلُ فَلَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسِّ أَنْ يَنْزِعَهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 97
text_chunk: "And whatever the camels eat, there is no harm in removing it."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Sulaiman ibn Khalid asked Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man who cuts
from the arak tree in Mecca.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He must pay its value as charity, and no one should remove anything
from the trees of Mecca except for palm trees and fruit trees."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَهُ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ خَالِدِ : عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَقْطَعُ مِنَ الْأَرَاكِ الَّذِي بِمَكَّةَ قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ ثَمَنُهُ يَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ وَ لا يَنْزِعُ
مِنْ شَجَرِ مَكَّةَ شَيْئًا إِلاَّ النَّخْلَ وَ شَجَرَ الْفَوَاكِهِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 174
text_chunk:
Sulaiman ibn Khalid asked Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man who cuts
from the arak tree in Mecca.
Imam {a.s} replied: "He must pay its value as charity, and no one should remove anything
from the trees of Mecca except for palm trees and fruit trees."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams {a.s},
who said:
I asked him: "Can a person in the state of ihram remove grass from outside the
Haram?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes."
I then asked: "What about from within the Haram?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "No."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لَهُ الْمُحْرِمُ يَنْزِعُ الْحَشِيشَ مِنْ غَيْرِ الْحَرَمِ
فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ» قُلْتُ فَمِنَ الْحَرَمِ قَالَ «لا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 94 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 552
text_chunk:
It has been narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams {a.s},
who said:
I asked him: "Can a person in the state of ihram remove grass from outside the
Haram?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "Yes."
I then asked: "What about from within the Haram?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "No."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Ishaq ibn Yazid asked Abu Ja'far {a.s} about a man entering Mecca and cutting
from its trees.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Cut what encroaches into your space, but do not cut what does not
enter into your dwelling."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَدْخُلُ مَكَّةَ فَيَقْطَعُ مِنْ شَجَرِهَا فَقَالَ «اقْطَعْ
مَا كَانَ دَاخِلاً عَلَيْكَ وَ لاَ تَقْطَعْ مَا لَمْ يَدْخُلْ مَنْزِلَكَ عَلَيْكَ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 231 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 95 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 555

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
Mansour bin Hazim asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about the arak tree being in the
sanctuary, and if he could cut it down.
Imam {a.s} said: "You may do so, and may you be ransomed for it."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ مَنصُورُ بْنُ حَازِم أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : عَنِ الْأَرَاكِ يَكُونُ فِي الْحَرَمِ فَأَقْطَعُهُ قَالَ «عَلَيْكَ
فِدَاؤُهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON ORIGIN OF THE KAABA, ITS VIRTUE, AND VIRTUE OF THE HARAM (SACRED SANCTUARY)
text_en:
It has been narrated from Ibrahim ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah {a.s}, who said:
"There are two types of lost property (luqata). As for the lost property of the Haram,
you must announce it for one year. If you find its owner, return it; otherwise, give it in
charity. As for lost property outside the Haram, announce it for one year. If its owner
comes, return it; otherwise, it becomes like your own property."
It has also been narrated:
"Among the names of Mecca are: Mecca, Bakkah, Umm al-Qura, Umm al-Rahm, and
Al-Bassah. When people commit oppression there, it destroys them (bassathum,
meaning annihilates them), and when they are oppressed there, they are shown
mercy."
text_ar:
[لْقَطَةُ الْحَرَمِ]
وَ رَوَى إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ عُمَرَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «اللَّقَطَةُ لُقَطَتَانِ لُقَطَةُ الْحَرَمِ تُعَرَّفُ سَنَةً
فَإِنْ وَجَدْتَ صَاحِبَهَا وَ إِلاَّ تَصَدَّقْتَ بِهَا وَ لُقَطَةُ غَيْرِ الْحَرَمِ تُعَرِّفُهَا سَنَةً فَإِنْ جَاءَ صَاحِبُهَا وَ إِلاَّ فَهِيَ كَسَبِيلِ مَالِكَ».
وَ رُوِيَ: «أَنَّ فِي أَسْمَاءِ مَكَّةَ أَنَّهَا مَكَّةُ وَبَكَةُ وَ أَمُ ٱلْقُرَى وَ أُمْ رُحْمِ وَ الْبَاسَّةُ كَانُوا إِذَا ظَلَمُوا بِهَا بَسْثَهُمْ أَيْ أَهْلَكَثَهُمْ
وَ كَانُوا إِذَا ظُلِمُوا رُحِمُوا».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE
text_en:
Zurara ibn A‘yan narrated from Abu Ja‘far {a.s}, who said:
"If a person in a state of ihram in the Haram kills a pigeon or anything up to the size of
a gazelle, he must offer a sacrificial animal (damm), slaughter it, and also give the
equivalent of its value in charity. However, if he does so while he is not in a state of
ihram, he must give the equivalent of its value in charity."
text_ar:
بَابُ تَحْرِيمِ صَيْدِ الْحَرَمِ وَحُكْمِهِ
رَوَى زُرَارَةُ بْنُ أَعْيَنَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «إِذَا أَصَابَ ٱلْمُحْرِمُ فِي الْحَرَمِ حَمَامَةً إِلَى أَنْ تَبْلُغَ
الظَّبْيَ فَعَلَيْهِ دَمْ يُهَرِيقُهُ وَ يَتَصَدَّقُ بِمِثْلِ ثَمَنِهِ أَيْضا فَإِنْ أَصَابَ مِنْهُ وَ هُوَ حَلاَلْ فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَتَصَدَّقَ بِمِثْلِ ثَمَنِهِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 13, p. 767 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 29 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 88

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE
text_en:
Sulayman ibn Khalid asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man who closed his door
on a bird, causing it to die.
Imam {a.s} replied: "If he closed the door on it after entering the state of ihram, then he
must offer a sacrificial animal (damm). If he closed it before entering ihram while he
was in a permissible state, he must pay its value."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ خَالِدٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَغْلَقَ بَابَهُ عَلَى طَيْرٍ فَمَاتَ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ
أَغْلَقَ الْبَابَ عَلَيْهِ بَعْدَ مَا أَحْرَمَ فَعَلَيْهِ دَمْ وَ إِنْ كَانَ أَعْلَقَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ يُحْرِمَ وَ هُوَ حَلاَلٌ فَعَلَيْهِ ثَمَنُهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE
text_en:
Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah {a.s} regarding a man who closed the
door of a house on a pigeon from the Haram, causing it to die.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must give a dirham in charity or use it to feed the pigeons of the
Haram."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَلَبِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ أَغْلَقَ بَابَ بَيْتٍ عَلَى طَيْرٍ مِنْ حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ فَمَاتَ
قَالَ «يَتَصَدَّقُ بِدِرْهَمِ أَوْ يُطْعِمُ بِهِ حَمَامَ الْحَرَمِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 110 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 41 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 50

Imam {a.s} said: "He must give a dirham in charity or use it to feed the pigeons of the
Haram."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl narrated from Abu Al-Hasan {a.s}:
I asked Imam {a.s} about a man who killed a pigeon from the pigeons of the Haram while
in the Haram but not in the state of ihram.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must pay its value, which is a dirham, and give it as charity or use it
to buy food for the pigeons of the Haram. However, if he killed it while in the state of
ihram within the Haram, he must offer a sheep as a sacrifice and also pay the value of
the pigeon."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْفُضَيْلِ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ حَمَامَةٌ مِنْ حَمَامٍ
اَلْحَرَمِ وَ هُوَ فِي الْحَرَمِ غَيْرُ مُحْرِمٍ فَقَالَ «عَلَيْهِ قِيمَثُهَا وَ هُوَ دِرْهَمْ يَتَصَدَّقُ بِهِ أَوْ يَشتَرِي بِهِ طَعَاماً لِحَمَامِ ٱلْحَرَمِ
فَإِنْ قَتَلَهَا وَ هُوَ مُحْرِمٌ فِي الْحَرَمِ فَعَلَيْهِ شَاة وَ قِيمَةُ الْحَمَامَةِ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 345 • Al-Istibsar, Part 2, p. 200 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 107 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 26

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Hafs ibn Al-Bakhtari narrated from Abu Abdullah {a.s} regarding someone who
catches a bird in the Haram:
"If the bird's wings are intact, let it go. But if its wings are not intact, care for it by feeding
and giving it water until its wings are restored, then release it."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى حَفْصُ بْنُ الْبَخْتَرِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِيمَنْ أَصَابَ طَيْراً فِي الْحَرَمِ قَالَ »إِنْ كَانَ
مُسْتَوِيَ الْجَنَاحِ فَلْيُخَلَ عَنْهُ وَ إِنْ كَانَ غَيْرَ مُسْتَوِي الْجَنَاحِ نَتَفَهُ وَ أَطْعَمَهُ وَ أَسْقَاهُ فَإِذَا اِسْتَوَى جَنَاحَاهُ خَلَّى
عَنْهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 105 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 30

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Al-'Ala narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man who enters into ihram while he has wild animals
or birds in his household.
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no harm in it."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْعَلاءُ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ : سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنِ الرَّجْلِ يُحْرِمُ وَ عِنْدَهُ فِي
أهْلِهِ صَيْدٌ إمَّا وَحْشٌ وَ إِمَّا طَيْرٌ قَالَ »لاَ بَأْسَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 13, p. 719 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 74

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Khallad, from Abu Abdullah {a.s}, regarding a man
who slaughtered a pigeon from the pigeons of the Haram.
Imam {a.s} said: "He must offer an expiation (fidya)."
I asked: "Can he eat it?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "No."
I asked: "Can he throw it away?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "If he does, another expiation will be required."
I asked: "Then what should he do with it?"
Imam {a.s} said: "He should bury it."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ خَلاَّدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ ذَبَحَ حَمَامَةً مِنْ حَمَامِ ٱلْحَرَمِ
قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ الْفِدَاءُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَيَأْكُلُهُ قَالَ «لا» قُلْتُ فَيَطْرَحُهُ قَالَ «إذاً يَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ فِدَاءً آخَرُ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَمَا يَصْنَعُ
بِهِ قَالَ «يَدْفِنُهُ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Usul al-Sitta ‘Ashar (Dar Shabestari Edition) Vol. 1, p. 106 • Al-Usul al-Sitta ‘Ashar (Dar Al-Hadith Edition) Vol. 1, p. 313 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 233 • Ilal al-Sharai’, Vol. 2, p. 454 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 378 • Al-Istibsar, Part 2, p. 215 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 105 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 431 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 102

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Ibn Faddal narrated from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, who said:
I sent a message to Abu Al-Hasan {a.s} asking about my brother, who had purchased
pigeons in Medina. We took them with us to Mecca, performed ‘Umrah, stayed until
Hajj, and then brought the pigeons with us from Mecca to Kufa. Is there any obligation
upon us for this?
Imam {a.s} replied to the messenger: "I believe they were wild pigeons. Tell him he must
sacrifice one sheep for each bird."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ فَضَّالٍ عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ يَعْقُوبَ قَالَ : أَرْسَلْتُ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّ أَخاً لِي اِشتَرَى
حَمَاماً مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ فَذَهَبْنَا بِهَا مَعَنَا إِلَى مَكَّةَ فَاعْتَمَرْنَا وَ أَقَمْنَا إِلَى الْحَجِّ ثُمَّ أَخْرَجْنَا الْحَمَامَ مَعَنَا مِنْ مَكَّةَ إِلَى
الْكُوفَةِ هَلْ عَلَيْنَا فِي ذَلِكَ شَيْءُ فَقَالَ لِلرَّسُولِ «إِنِّي أَظُنُهُنَّ كُنَّ فُرْهَةً قُلْ لَهُ يَذْبَحُ مَكَانَ كُلِّ طَيْرِ شَاةً.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 235 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 112 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 40

chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Safwan narrated from Al-'Ays ibn Al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about purchasing doves in Mecca and Medina.
Imam {a.s} said: "I do not like that anything be taken out from them."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى صَفْوَانُ عَنِ الْعِيصِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ قَالَ : سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ شِرَاءِ الْقَمَارِيّ بِمَكَّةَ وَ
الْمَدِينَةً فَقَالَ مَا أَحِبُّ أَنْ يُخْرَجَ مِنْهَا شَيْءٌ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Hariz narrated from Zurara that Al-Hakam asked Abu Ja‘far {a.s} about a man
who was gifted a pigeon with clipped wings in the Haram.
Imam {a.s} said: "Pluck its feathers, feed it well, and when its feathers have grown back,
release it."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى حَرِيزٌ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ : أَنْ الْحَكَمَ سَألَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ أُهْدِيَ لَهُ فِي الْحَرَمِ حَمَامَةٌ
مَقْصُوصَةٌ فَقَالَ «اِنْتِفْهَا وَ أَحْسِنْ عَلَفَهَا حَتَّى إِذَا اِسْتَوَى رِيشُهَا فَخَلَّ سَبِيلَهَا».

Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

وَ رَوَى حَرِيزٌ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ : سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلِ أَهْدِيَ لَهُ حَمَامٌ أَهْلِيْ وَ

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from Abdul-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man who hunted an animal in the Ḥill (permissible
area) while heading towards the Haram, in the area between the post station and the
mosque. He struck it in the Ḥill, but the hunted animal moved towards the Haram and
died there. I asked if he would be liable for a penalty.
Imam {a.s} replied: "There is no penalty upon him. The example of this is like a person
who sets a trap in the Ḥill, near the boundary of the Haram, and an animal falls into the
trap and struggles until it enters the Haram and dies there. He is not liable for the
penalty because the trap was set in a permissible place, and similarly, he hunted in a
permissible area. Therefore, he is not accountable for what happens afterward."
I said: "This resembles analogy (qiyas) according to the people."
Imam {a.s} replied: "I only drew a parallel between things so that you may understand."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى صَفْوَانُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ : سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ
رَمَى صَيْداً فِي الْجِلِّ وَ هُوَ يَوْمُ ٱلْحَرَمَ فِيمَا بَيْنَ البَرِيدِ وَ الْمَسْجِدِ فَأَصَابَهُ فِي الْجِلِّ فَمَضَى بِرَمْيَتِهِ حَتَّى دَخَلَ
الْحَرَمَ قَمَاتَ مِنْ رَمْيَتِهِ هَلْ عَلَيْهِ جَزَاءً فَقَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ جَزَاءُ إِنَّمَا مَثَلُ ذَلِكَ مَثَلُ مَنْ نَصَبَ شَرَكاً فِي الْحِلِّ إِلَى
جَانِبِ الْحَرَمِ فَوَقَعَ فِيهِ صَيْدٌ فَاضْطَرَبَ حَتَّى دَخَلَ الْحَرَمَ فَمَاتَ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ جَزَاؤُهُ لِأَنَّهُ نَصَبَ حَيْثُ نَصَبَ وَ
هُوَ لَهُ حَلاَلْ وَ رَمَى حَيْثُ رَمَى وَ هُوَ لَهُ حَلاَلْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ فِيمَا كَانَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ» فَقُلْتُ هَذَا الْقِيَاسُ عِنْدَ
النَّاسِ فَقَالَ «إِنَّمَا شَبَّهْتُ لَكَ الشَّيْءَ بِالشَّيْءِ لِتَعْرِفَهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Ilal al-Sharai’, Vol. 2, p. 454 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 67 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 96, p. 153

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Al-Muthanna narrated from Karib al-Sayrafi:
We were a group who collectively purchased a bird, clipped its feathers, and entered
Makkah with it. The people of Makkah disapproved of this action. Karib sent someone
to Abu Abdullah {a.s} to inquire about it.
Imam {a.s} said: "Entrust it to a Muslim man or woman from the people of Makkah, and
when its feathers grow back, release it."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْمُثَنَّى عَنْ كَرِبِ الصَّيْرَفِيِّ قَالَ : كُنَّا جَمِيعاً فَاشتَرَيْنَا طَيْراً فَقَصَصْنَاهُ فَدَخَلْنَا بِهِ مَكَّةَ فَعَابَ ذَلِكَ
أَهْلُ مَكَّةَ فَأَرْسَلَ كَرِبٌ إِلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ فَسَأَلَهُ فَقَالَ «اِسْتَوْدِعُوهُ رَجُلاً مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ ، مُسلِماً أَو
اِمْرَأَةً مُسْلِمَةً فَإِذَا اِسْتَوَى خَلَّوْا سَبِيلَهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 233 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 103

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Ibn Muskan narrated from Ibrahim ibn Maymun:
I said to Abu Abdullah {a.s}, "A man plucked the feathers of a pigeon from the pigeons of
the Haram."
Imam {a.s} replied: "He should give charity to a needy person and with the hand that
plucked the feathers, for he has caused it pain."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَيْمُونِ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ رَجُلُ نَتَفَ حَمَامَةً مِنْ
حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ فَقَالَ «يَتَصَدَقُ بِصَدَقَةٍ عَلَى مِسْكِينٍ وَ يُعْطِي بِالْيَدِ آلَّتِي نَتَفَ بِهَا فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ أَوْجَعَهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 235 • Ilal al-Sharai’, Vol. 2, p. 453 • Al- Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 113 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 96, p. 153

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Safwan narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim:
I said to Abu Abdullah {a.s}, "A slaughtered bird was gifted to us in Mecca, and our family
ate it."
Imam {a.s} replied: "The people of Mecca see no harm in it."
I asked: "What do you say about it?"
Imam {a.s} said: "They are liable for its price."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى صَفْوَانُ عَنْ مَنْصُورِ بْنِ حَازِمِ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَهْدِيَ لَنَا طَيْرٌ مَذْبُوحْ بِمَكَّةَ
فَأَكَلَهُ أَهْلُنَا فَقَالَ «لا يَرَى بِهِ أَهْلُ مَكَّةَ بَأْساً» قُلْتُ فَأَيَّ شَيْءٍ تَقُولُ أَنتَ قَالَ «عَلَيْهِمْ ثَمَنُهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 236 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 376 • Al-Istibsar, Part 2, p. 213 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 113 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 424 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 25 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 39

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Safwan narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
Abu Abdullah {a.s} said: "Hunting is not to be slaughtered in the Sacred Sanctuary
(Haram), even if it was hunted in the permissible (Hil)."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى صَفْوَانُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «لا يُذْبَحُ الصَّيْدُ فِي الْحَرَمِ وَ
إنْ صِيدَ فِي الْحِلِّ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 118 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 425 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 431

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Al-Nadr narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan:
I heard Abu Abdullah {a.s} say: "For the pigeons of Mecca and the domesticated birds
from the pigeons of the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram), whoever slaughters a bird from
them must give charity greater than its value. If the person was in the state of Ihram,
then a sheep is required for each bird."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى النَّضْرُ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللهِ بْنِ سِنَانِ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ يَقُولُ : «فِي حَمَامٍ مَكَّةَ اَلطَّيْرُ
الْأَهْلِيُّ مِنْ حَمَامِ الْحَرَمِ مَنْ ذَبَحَ مِنْهُ طَيْراً فَعَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَتَصَدَّقَ بِصَدَقَةِ أَفْضَلَ مِنْ ثَمَنِهِ فَإِنْ كَانَ مُحْرِماً فَشَاةٌ عَنْ
كُلِّ طَيْرٍ
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 235 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 111 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 23

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Muawiyah ibn Ammar asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a domesticated bird that
entered the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram).
Imam {a.s} replied: "It should not be taken or touched because Allah {SWT}, the Almighty,
says: 'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : عَنْ طَيْرٍ أَهْلِيَّ أَقْبَلَ فَدَخَلَ الْحَرَمَ فَقَالَ «لا يُوخَذُ وَ
لاَ يُمَسُّ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ: «وَ مَنْ دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِناً» ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Muslim asked one of the Imams {a.s} about a gazelle entering
the Sacred Sanctuary (Haram).
Imam {a.s} replied: "It should not be taken or touched because Allah {SWT}, the Almighty,
says: 'And whoever enters it shall be safe.'"
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمِ أَحَدَهُمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ : عَنِ الظَّبْيِ يَدْخُلُ الْحَرَمَ فَقَالَ «لا يُوْخَذُ وَ لا يُمَشَ لِأَنْ
اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَقُولُ: «وَ مَنْ دَخَلَهُ كانَ آمِنا) ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 362 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 104 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 557 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 75

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Ibn Maskan narrated from Yazid ibn Khalifa, who said:
"There was a basket near my house containing two eggs of the Sacred Sanctuary’s
pigeons. My servant, unaware of the eggs, overturned the basket, breaking them. I
went out and met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and I mentioned this to him.
He said: 'Give in charity two handfuls of flour.'
Later, I met Abu Abdullah {a.s} and informed him.
Imam {a.s} said: 'He must pay the price of two birds, feeding the pigeons of the Sacred
Sanctuary with it.'
I then met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and informed him of this.
He said: 'He {a.s} has spoken the truth; follow it, for He {a.s} has taken this from his
forefathers {a.s}.'"
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ يَزِيدَ بْنِ خَلِيفَةَ قَالَ : كَانَ فِي جَانِبِ بَيْتِي مِكْتَلْ كَانَ فِيهِ بَيْضَتَانِ مِنْ حَمَامٍ
الْحَرَمِ فَذَهَبَ غَلامِي فَكَبَّ الْمِكْتَلَ وَ هُوَ لا يَعْلَمُ أَنّ فِيهِ بَيْضَتَيْنٍ فَكَسَرَهُمَا فَخَرَجْتُ فَلَقِيتُ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ ٱلْحَسَنِ
فَذَكَزْتُ ذَلِكَ لَهُ فَقَالَ تَصَدَّقَ بِكَفَّيْنِ مِنْ دَقِيقٍ قَالَ فَلَقِيتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ بَعْدُ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ فَقَالَ لِي عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ «عَلَيْهِ ثَمَنُ طَيْرَيْنِ يُطعِمُ بِهِ حَمَامَ الْحَرَمِ » فَلَقِيتُ عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ الْحَسَنِ فَأَخْبَرْتُهُ فَقَالَ صَدَقَ خُذْ بِهِ فَإِنَّهُ
أَخَذَ عَنْ آبَائِهِ عَلَيْهِمُ السِّلاَمُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 236 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 115
text_chunk:
Ibn Maskan narrated from Yazid ibn Khalifa, who said:
"There was a basket near my house containing two eggs of the Sacred Sanctuary’s
pigeons. My servant, unaware of the eggs, overturned the basket, breaking them. I
went out and met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and I mentioned this to him.
He said: 'Give in charity two handfuls of flour.'
Later, I met Abu Abdullah {a.s} and informed him.
Imam {a.s} said: 'He must pay the price of two birds, feeding the pigeons of the Sacred
Sanctuary with it.'
I then met Abdullah ibn al-Hasan and informed him of this.
He said: 'He {a.s} has spoken the truth; follow it, for He {a.s} has taken this from his
forefathers {a.s}.'"

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Shihab ibn Abd Rabbihi narrated:
"I said to Abu Abdullah {a.s}: 'I partake in Suhoor with chicks brought from outside
Mecca, which are slaughtered in the Sacred Sanctuary, and I partake in Suhoor with
them.'
Imam {a.s} replied: 'What an evil Suhoor is your Suhoor! Do you not know that whatever
you bring into the Sacred Sanctuary alive becomes forbidden for you to slaughter and
to retain?'"
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيّ عَنْ شِهَابِ بْنِ عَبْدِ رَبِّهِ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ إِنَّي أَتَسَحَرُ بِفِرَاخٍ أَتِيَ بِهَا مِنْ غَيْرٍ
مَكَّةَ فَتُذْبَحُ فِي الْحَرَمِ فَأْتَسَحَرُ بِهَا فَقَالَ «بِئسَ السِّحُورُ سَحُورُكَ أَمَا عَلِمْتَ أَنَّ مَا أَدْخَلْتَ بِهِ الْحَرَمَ حَيّأْ فَقَدْ
حَرُمَ عَلَيْكَ ذَبْحُهُ وَ إِمْسَاكُهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 119 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 31

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Humran narrated from Abu Abdullah {a.s} from his father {a.s},
who said: "I was with Ali ibn al-Husayn {a.s} in the Sacred Sanctuary, and he saw me
troubling the swallows.
Imam {a.s} said: 'O my son, do not kill them and do not harm them, for they do not harm
anything.'"
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ حُمْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا السَلاَمُ قَالَ : «كُنْتُ مَعَ عَلِيَّ بْنِ ٱلْحُسَيْنِ
عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلامُ بِالْحَرَمِ فَرَآنِي أُوذِي الْخَطَاطِيفَ فَقَالَ» «يَا بُنِّيّ لا تَقْثُلْهُنَّ وَ لا تُوْذِهِنَّ فَإِنَّهُنَّ لا يُوْذِينَ شَيْئاً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 120 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 35

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj narrated: "I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about two
young birds dressed in feathers that I slaughtered while I was in Mecca.
Imam {a.s} said to me: 'Why did you slaughter them?'
I replied: 'A girl from the people of Mecca brought them to me and asked me to
slaughter them, and I thought I was in Kufa and did not recall the sanctity of the
Haram.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Give charity equivalent to their value.'
I asked: 'How much?'
Imam {a.s} said: 'A dirham, which is better than them.'"
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ ٱلْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ : سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ فَرْخَيْنِ مُسَرْوَلَيْنِ ذَبَحْتُهُمَا
وَ أَنَا بِمَكَّةَ فَقَالَ لِي «لِمَ ذَبَحْتَهُمَا» فَقُلْتُ جَاءَثْنِي بِهِمَا جَارِيَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ مَكَّةَ فَسَأَلَثْنِي أَنْ أَدْبَحَهُمَا فَظَنَئْتُ أَنَّي
بِالْكُوفَةِ وَ لَمْ أَذْكُرِ الْحَرَمَ قَالَ «تَصَدَّقُ بِقِيمَتِهِمَا» قُلْتُ كَمْ قَالَ «دِرْهَماً وَ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِنْهُمَا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 237 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 117

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Zurara narrated:
He asked (Imam {a.s}) about a man who took a bird from Mecca to Kufa.
The Imam {a.s} said: "He must return it to Mecca."
text_ar: - وَ سَأْلَهُ زُرَارَةُ : عَنْ رَجُلٍ أَخْرَجَ طَيْراً مِنْ مَكَّةَ إِلَى الْكُوفَةِ فَقَالَ «يَرُدّهُ إِلَى مَكَّةَ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Al-Muthanna narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Hakam:
He said: I told a servant of ours, "Prepare our meal." So he took birds from Mecca,
slaughtered them, and cooked them.
I went to Abu Abdullah {a.s}, and Imam {a.s} said: "Bury them and offer compensation
(fidya) for each bird among them."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْمُثَنَّى عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي الْحَكَمِ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لِغَلامٍ لَنَا هَيَّى لَنَا غَدَاءَنَا فَأَخَذَ لَنَا مِنْ أَطْيَارِ مَكَّةَ
فَذَبَحَهَا وَ طَبَخَهَا فَدَخَلْتُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ فَقَالَ «إِدْفِنْهُنَّ وَ اِفْدٍ عَنْ كُلِّ طَيْرٍ مِنْهُنَّ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 103

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Ali ibn Abi Hamzah narrated from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdullah {a.s}:
Regarding a man who killed a bird of the sanctuary while he was in a state of ihram
within the Haram,
Imam {a.s} said: "He must offer a sheep as compensation, and the value of the bird is
one dirham, with which he should feed the pigeons of the Haram. If it was a chick, then
he must offer a lamb, and the value of the chick is half a dirham, with which he should
also feed the pigeons of the Haram."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَلِيْ بْنُ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلَاَمُ : فِي رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ طَيْراً مِنْ طُيُورٍ
اَلْحَرَمِ وَ هُوَ مُحْرِمٌ فِي الْحَرَمِ فَقَالَ «عَلَيْهِ شَاةْ وَ قِيمَةُ ٱلْحَمَامِ دِرْهَمْ يَعْلِفُ بِهِ حَمَامَ ٱلْحَرَمِ وَ إِنْ كَانَ فَرْحاً فَعَلَيْهِ
حَمَلٌ وَ قِيمَةُ الْفَرْخِ نِصْفُ دِرْهَمِ يَعْلِفُ بِهِ حَمَامَ الْحَرَمِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 13, p. 770 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 30

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Al-Halabi narrated from Abi Abdullah {a.s}:
"Do not purchase [meat] in the Haram unless it has been slaughtered in the Hill
(outside the Haram) and then brought to the Haram after being slaughtered; in such a
case, there is no issue with it for someone who is not in a state of ihram."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَلَبِي عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «لا تَشْتَرِيَنَّ فِي الْحَرَمِ إِلاَّ مَذْبُوحاً قَدْ ذُبِحَ فِي الْجِلِّ
ثُمَّ جِيءَ بِهِ إِلَى الْحَرَمِ مَذْبُوحاً فَلاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ لِلْحَلاَلِ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 425

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Sa'id ibn Abdullah Al-A'raj asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about an ostrich egg that
he ate while in the Haram.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Give in charity the equivalent of its price."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ سَعِيدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللّهِ الْأَعْرَجُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : عَنْ بَيْضَةٍ نَعَامَةٍ أَكَلْتُ فِي الْحَرَمِ فَقَالَ
«تَصَدَّقْ بِتَمَنِهَا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2

Imam {a.s} replied: "Give in charity the equivalent of its price."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE PROHIBITION OF HUNTING IN THE SANCTUARY AND ITS RULINGS
text_en:
Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj narrated that Abu Abdullah {a.s} said:
"The value of a pigeon is one dirham, the value of a chick is half a dirham, and the value
of an egg is a quarter of a dirham."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «فِي قِيمَةِ الْحَمَامَةِ دِرْهَمْ وَ فِي
الْفَرْخِ نِصْفُ دِرْهَمِ وَ فِي البَيْضَةِ رُبُعُ دِرْهَمٍ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 4, p. 234 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 107 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 25

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT IS PERMITTED TO BE
text_en:
Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah {a.s}, who said:
"It is not permissible to slaughter in the Haram except for camels, cows, sheep, and
chickens."
text_ar:
بَابٌ مَا يَجُوزُ أُنْ يُذْبَحَ فِي الْحَرَمِ وَيُخْرَجَ بِهِ مِنْهُ
رَوَى اِبْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «لَاَ يُذْبَحُ فِي الْحَرَمِ إِلَّ الْإِبِلُ وَ الْبَقَرُ
وَ اَلْغَنَمُ وَ الدَّجَاجُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 367 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 124 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 125 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 548

Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdullah {a.s}, who said:
"It is not permissible to slaughter in the Haram except for camels, cows, sheep, and
chickens."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT IS PERMITTED TO BE
text_en:
Mu'awiya ibn Ammar asked Imam {a.s} about Ethiopian chickens.
Imam {a.s} replied: "It is not considered part of the game (sayd); game birds are those
that fly between the sky and the earth and flap their wings."
text_ar:
وَ سَأْلَهُ مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنْ عَمَّارٍ : عَنْ دَجَاجِ الْحَبَشِ فَقَالَ «لَيْسَ مِنَ الصَّيْدِ إِنَّمَا الطَّيْرُ مَا طَارَ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَ
الأَرض وَصَفَّ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2
text_chunk:

Imam {a.s} replied: "It is not considered part of the game (sayd); game birds are those

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT IS PERMITTED TO BE
text_en:
Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Muslim reported that Abu Abdullah {a.s}
was asked about Sindhi chickens being taken out of the Haram.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, because they cannot fly independently."
In another narration: "They only flutter lightly."
text_ar:
وَ قَالَ جَمِيلُ بْنُ دَرَّاجٍ وَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنْ مُسْلِمِ : سُئِلَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنِ الدَّجَاجِ السِّنْدِيِّ يُخْرَجْ بِهِ
مِنَ الْحَرَمِ فَقَالَ «نَعَمْ لِأَنَّهَا لا تَسْتَقِلُ بِالطَّيَرَانِ.
وَ فِي خَبَرٍ آخَرَ: «أَنَّهَا تَدُفٌ دَفِيفاً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 80
text_chunk:
Jamil ibn Darraj and Muhammad ibn Muslim reported that Abu Abdullah {a.s}
was asked about Sindhi chickens being taken out of the Haram.
Imam {a.s} said: "Yes, because they cannot fly independently."
In another narration: "They only flutter lightly."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT IS PERMITTED TO BE SLAUGHTERED IN THE SANCTUARY AND TAKEN OUTSIDE
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn al-Sayqal asked Imam {a.s} about the chickens and birds of
Mecca.
Imam {a.s} said: "What does not glide (in flight), you may eat it, and what glides, let it go."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَهُ الْحَسَنُ بْنُ الصَّيْقَلِ : عَنْ دَجَاجِ مَكَّةَ وَ طَيْرِهَا فَقَالَ «مَا لَمْ يَصُفَّ فَكُلْهُ وَ مَا كَانَ يَصْفٌ فَخَلَ
سَبِيلَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2
text_chunk:
Al-Hasan ibn al-Sayqal asked Imam {a.s} about the chickens and birds of
Mecca.
Imam {a.s} said: "What does not glide (in flight), you may eat it, and what glides, let it go."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT IS PERMITTED TO BE SLAUGHTERED IN THE SANCTUARY AND TAKEN OUTSIDE
text_en:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who brought
his cheetah into the sacred sanctuary (Al-Haram). Is he allowed to take it out?
Imam {a.s} replied: "It is a predator. Whatever predator you bring into the sanctuary as a
captive, you are allowed to take it out."
text_ar:
وَ سُئِلَ الصَّادِقُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : عَنْ رَجُلِ أَدْخَلَ فَهْدَهُ إِلَى الْحَرَمِ أَلَهُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَهُ فَقَالَ «هُوَ سَبُعْ فَكُلُّ مَا
أَذْخَلْتَ مِنَ السَّبُعِ الْحَرَمَ أَسِيراً فَلَكَ أَنْ تُخْرِجَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 367 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 125 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 13, p. 82 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 2, p. 199
text_chunk:
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} was asked about a man who brought
his cheetah into the sacred sanctuary (Al-Haram). Is he allowed to take it out?
Imam {a.s} replied: "It is a predator. Whatever predator you bring into the sanctuary as a
captive, you are allowed to take it out."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT IS PERMITTED TO BE SLAUGHTERED IN THE SANCTUARY AND TAKEN OUTSIDE
text_en:
Muawiya ibn Ammar narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}
that he said: "There is no harm in killing ants and bedbugs in the sacred sanctuary (Al-
Haram)."
Imam {a.s} also said: "There is no harm in killing lice both within the sanctuary and
outside of it."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ عَمَّارِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ : «لا بَأْسَ بِقَتَلِ النَّمْلِ وَ اَلْبَقّ فِي الْحَرَمِ » وَ قَالَ «لا
بَأَسَ بِقَثَلِ الْقَمْلَةِ فِي الْحَرَمِ وَ غَيْرِهِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol. 5, p. 366 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 12, p. 551

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON TRAVELLING FOR HAJJ AND OTHER
text_en:
Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq
{a.s} who said: "In the wisdom of the family of Dawood {a.s} it is stated that it is incumbent
upon the intelligent person not to travel except for one of three purposes: gathering
provisions for the Hereafter, seeking sustenance for livelihood, or indulging in
permissible pleasure."
text_ar:
بَابُ مَا جَاءَ فِي السَّفَرِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ وَغَيْرِهِ مِنَ الطَّاعَاتِ
رَوَى عَمْرُو بْنُ أَبِي الْمِقْدَامِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «فِي حِكْمَةِ آلِ دَاوُدَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ أَنَّ عَلَى
اَلْعَاقِلِ أَنْ لا يَكُونَ ظَاعِناً إِلاَّ فِي ثَلَاَثٍ تَزَوْدٍ لِمَعَادٍ أَوْ مَرَمَّةٍ لِمَعَاشٍ أَوْ لَذَّةٍ فِي غَيْرِ مُحَرِّمٍ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Adab ad-Diniyah, Pt 1, p. 129 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Pt 1, p. 240 • Al-Wafi, V. 12, p. 351 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, V. 11, p. 343 • Al-Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 3, p. 338

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON TRAVELLING FOR HAJJ AND OTHER
text_en:
Al-Sakuni narrated through his chain that the Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace
and blessings be upon him and his family, said:
"Travel, and you will gain health; strive in the way of Allah {SWT}, and you will attain
victory; and perform Hajj, and you will become self-sufficient."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى السِّكُونِيُّ بِإِسْنَادِهِ قَالَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «سَافِرُوا تَصِحُوا وَ جَاهِدُوا تَغْنَمُوا
وَاحُجّوا تَسْتَغْنُوا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 345 • Al-Adab ad-Diniyah, Part 1, p. 129 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 240 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 351 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 345 • Al- Fusul al-Muhimmah, Part 3, p. 230 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 221 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 96, p. 10 • Mustadrak Al-Wasail, Vol. 11, p. 16

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON TRAVELLING FOR HAJJ AND OTHER
text_en:
Ja'far ibn Bashir narrated from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, from Abu Abdullah Imam
Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"When Allah {SWT}, the Glorious and Majestic, decrees sustenance for a servant in a
particular land, He creates a need for him in that land."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى جَعْفَرُ بْنُ بَشِيرٍ عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ ٱلْفَضْلِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «إِذَا سَبَّبَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ
جَلَّ لِعَبْدٍ الرَّزْقَ فِي أَرْضِ جَعَلَ لَهُ فِيهَا حَاجَةً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 345 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 240 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 351 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 345 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 221

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR
text_en:
Hafs ibn Ghayath al-Nakha'i narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s}:
"Whoever intends to travel should travel on a Saturday, for if a stone were to be
dislodged from a mountain on a Saturday, Allah {SWT}, the Glorious and Majestic, would
return it to its place. And whoever finds difficulties in fulfilling their needs should seek
them on a Tuesday, for it is the day on which Allah {SWT}, the Glorious and Majestic,
softened iron for Dawood (David), peace be upon him."
text_ar:
بَابُ الْأَيَّامِ وَالْأَوْقَاتِ الَّتِي يُسْتَحَبُّ فِيهَا السَّفَرُ، وَالْأَيَّامِ وَالْأَوْقَاتِ الَّتِي يُكْرَهُ فِيهَا السَّفَرُ
رَوَى حَفْصُ بْنُ غِيَاتِ النَّخَعِي عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «مَنْ أَرَادَ سَفَراً فَلْيُسَافِزْ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ
فَلَوْ أَنَّ حَجَراً زَالَ عَنْ جَبَلٍ فِي يَوْمِ السَّبْتِ لَرَدَّهُ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ إِلَى مَكَانِهِ وَ مَنْ تَعَذَّرَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوَائِجُ فَلْيَلْتَمِسْ
طَلَبَهَا يَوْمَ الثَّلاَثَاءِ فَإِنَّهُ الْيَوْمُ الَّذِي أَلآنَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ فِيهِ اَلْحَدِيدَ لِدَاوُدَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Khasal, Part 2, p. 386 • Rawdat Al-Wa'ezin, Vol. 2, p. 392 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 240 • Al-Aman, Part 1, p. 30 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 352 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 56, p. 35 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 224

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR
text_en:
Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya al-Madani narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad
Al-Sadiq {a.s}: "There is no harm in setting out on a journey on the night of Friday."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ أَبِي يَحْيَى الْمَدِينِيُ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ : «لا بَأْسَ بِالْخُرُوجِ فِي السَّفَرِ لَيْلَةَ
الجُمُعَةً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 347 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 240 • Al-Sara’ir, Part 3, p. 648 • Al-Aman, Part 1, p. 30 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 353 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 358 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 56, p. 33 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 226 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 226

chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR
text_en:
Abdullah ibn Sulayman narrated from Imam Abu Ja'far {a.s}:
"The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace be upon him and his family, used to travel on
Thursdays."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ سُلَيْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ
يُسَافِرُ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 358

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
Imam {a.s} said: "Thursday is a day loved by Allah {SWT}, His Messenger, and His
angels."
text_ar: - وَ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ: « يَوْمُ الْخَمِيسِ يَوْمٌ يُحِبُّهُ اللَهُ وَ رَسُولُهُ وَ مَلاَئِكَتُهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Misbah al-Za’ir, Part 1, p. 26

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
Some Baghdadis wrote to Imam al-Hassan al-Thani {a.s} asking about traveling
on a Wednesday that does not rotate.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Whoever departs on a Wednesday that does not rotate, in
opposition to those who believe in bad omens, will be protected from all harm, healed
from every affliction, and Allah {SWT}, the Exalted, will fulfill his need."
text_ar:
وَ كَتَبَ بَعْضُ الْبَغْدَادِيَّينَ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الثَّانِي عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ : يَسْأَلُهُ عَنِ الْخُرُوجِ يَوْمَ الْأَرْبِعَاءِ لا يَدُورُ
فَكَتَبَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ «مَنْ خَرَجَ يَوْمَ ٱلْأَرْبِعَاءِ لاَ يَدُورُ خِلاَفاً عَلَى أهلِ الطّيَرَةِ وُقِيَ مِنْ كُلِّ آفَةٍ وَ عُوفِيَ مِنْ كُلِّ
عَاهَةٍ وَ قَضَى اللَهُ عَزَّ وَ جَلَ لَهُ حَاجَتَهُ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al-Aman, Part 1, p. 32 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 353 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 362

chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
The Messenger of Allah {SWT}, peace and blessings be upon him and his family,
said:
"Travel by night, for the earth is folded during the night."
text_ar: - وَ قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «عَلَيْكُمْ بِالسَّيْرِ بِاللَّيْلِ فَإِنَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ تُطْوَى بِاللَّيْلِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 346 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 241
text_chunk:

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
In a narration by Jamil ibn Darraj and Hammad ibn Uthman from Abu Abdullah
{a.s} he said: "The earth is folded at the end of the night."
text_ar:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ جَمِيلٍ بْنِ دَرَّاجِ وَ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ : «الْأَرْضُ تُطْوَى مِنْ
آخِرٍ اللّيْلِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Al Mahasin, Part 2, p. 346 • Al-Kafi, Vol. 8, p. 314 • Al- Mazar (Lilmufid) Vol. 1, p. 64 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 241 • Al-Mazar al-Kabir, Part 1, p. 51 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 391 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 364 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 73, p. 278

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Yahya Al-Khath'ami narrated from Him, peace be upon him:
"Do not go out on Friday for any need, but if it is Saturday and the sun has risen, then
go out for your need."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى الْخَتْعَمِيُّ عَنْهُ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «لا تَخْرُجْ يَوْمَ الْجُمُعَةِ فِي حَاجَةٍ فَإِذَا كَانَ يَوْمُ
السَّبْتِ وَطَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ فَاخْرُجْ فِي حَاجَتِكَ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 241 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 352 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 349 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 56, p. 34

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz and Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about
the saying of Allah {SWT}, the Exalted:
"So when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the
bounty of Allah {SWT}." (Surah Al-Jumu'ah 62:10)
Imam {a.s} said: "The prayer refers to the day of Friday, and the dispersal refers to the
day of Saturday."
text_ar:
وَ سَأَلَ أَبُو أَيُوبَ الْخَزَّازُ وَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ سِنَانٍ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ قَوْلِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ «فَإِذا
قَضِيَتِ الصَّلاَةُ فَانْتَشِرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَ اِبْتَغُوا مِنْ فَضْلِ ٱللُّهِ» فَقَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَلامُ «الصْلاَةُ يَوْمَ ٱلْجُمُعَةِ وَ ٱلْإِنْتِشَارُ
يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 241 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p.
text_chunk:
Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz and Abdullah ibn Sinan asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en: Imam {a.s} said: "Saturday is for us, and Sunday is for Banu Umayyah."
text_ar: - وَ قَالَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : « السَّبْتُ لَنَا وَ الْأَحَدُ لِبَنِي أَمَيَّةَ ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
It is narrated from Abu Ayyub Al-Khazzaz that he said:
"We intended to leave, so we went to bid farewell to Abu Abdullah {a.s}.
Imam {a.s} said: 'It seems you are seeking the blessing of Monday.'
We said: 'Yes.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'What day is more ominous than Monday? On that day, we lost our
Prophet {saws}, may Allah {SWT} bless him and his family, and revelation ceased to
descend upon us. Do not depart on Monday; instead, depart on Tuesday.'"
text_ar:
ا اا
وَ رُوِيّ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ الْخَزَّازِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ : أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَخْرُجَ فَجِئُنَا نُسَلَّمُ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ فَقَالَ
«كَأَنَّكُمْ طَلَبْثُمْ بَرَكَةَ ٱلْإِثْنَيْنِ » قُلْنَا نَعَمْ قَالَ («فَأَيّ يَوْمِ أَعْظَمُ شُوْماً مِنْ يَوْمِ ٱلْإِثْتَيْنِ فَقَدْنَا فِيهِ نَبِيَّنَا صَلَّى اللَّهُ
عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ وَ اِرْتَفَعَ الْوَحْيُ عَنَّا لاَ تَخْرُجُوا يَوْمَ الْإِثْنَيْنِ وَ أُخْرُجُوا يَوْمَ الثَّلاَثَاءِ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
It is narrated by Muhammad ibn Humran by his father, from Abu Abdullah {a.s}:
"Whoever travels or marries while the moon is in Scorpio will not see goodness."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ حُمْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ : «مَنْ سَافَرَ أَوْ تَزَوَّجَ وَ الْقَمَرُ فِي
اَلْعَقْرَبٍ لَمْ يَرَ الْحُسْنَى.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
It is narrated from Abdul Malik ibn A'yan who said: "I said to Abu Abdullah {a.s}
'I have been tested with this knowledge (of astrology). When I intend to fulfill a need
and observe the rising star, if I see it as unfavorable, I sit and do not proceed. But if I
see it as favorable, I proceed with my need.'
Imam {a.s} said to me: 'Do you accomplish it?' I said: 'Yes.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'Burn your books.'"
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلْمَلِكِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لِأَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ إِنَّي قَدِ أُبْثُلِيتُ بِهَذَا الْعِلْمِ فَأْرِيدُ
الْحَاجَةَ فَإِذَا نَظَرْتُ إِلَى الطَّالِعِ وَ رَأَيْتُ الطَّالِعَ الشَّرَّ جَلَسْتُ وَ لَمْ أَذْهَبْ فِيهَا وَ إِذَا رَأَيْتُ الطَّالِعَ الْخَيْرَ ذَهَبْتُ فِي
الْحَاجَةٍ فَقَالَ لِي «تَقْضِي » قُلْتُ نَعَمْ قَالَ «أَحرِقْ كُتُبَكَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol. 2 • Makarim al-Akhlaq, Part 1, p. 242 • Silwat al-Hazeen, Part 1, p. 112 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 12, p. 355 • Al-Wafi, Vol. 26, p. 521 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’a, Vol. 11, p. 370 • Bihar Al-Anwar, Vol. 55, p. 272 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Part 4, p. 407 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Part 11, p. 139

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON DAYS AND TIMES RECOMMENDED FOR TRAVEL AND DISLIKED FOR TRAVEL
text_en:
It is narrated by Sulaiman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari from Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa
ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim {a.s}:
"Ill omen for a traveler on his journey lies in six things:
A croaking crow on his right side,
A dog wagging its tail,
A howling wolf that howls facing the man, sitting on its tail, howling and then raising
and lowering itself three times,
A deer crossing from the right to the left,
A screeching owl,
And an old gray-haired woman exposing herself, or a mutilated she-donkey, meaning
one with clipped ears.
Whoever feels apprehension in themselves from any of these, let them say: 'I seek
refuge with You, my Lord {AZJ}, from the evil that I sense within myself; so protect me
from it.'
Imam {a.s} said: 'They will then be protected from it.'"
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ جَعْفَرِ الْجَعْفَرِيُ عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ : «الشُوْمُ لِلْمُسَافِرِ
فِي طَرِيقِهِ فِي سِتَّةِ اَلْغُرَابِ النَّاعِقِ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ وَ الْكَلْبِ اَلنَّاشِرِ لِذَنَبِهِ وَ الذِّلْبِ اَلْعَاوِي الَّذِي يَعْوِي فِي وَجْهِ الرَّجُلِ
وَ هُوَ مُقْعٍ عَلَى ذَنَبِهِ يَعْوِي ثُمَّ يَرْتَفِعُ ثُمَّ يَنْخَفِضُ ثَلاَثاً وَ ٱلظَّبْيِ ٱلسَّانِحِ مِنْ يَمِينِ إِلَى شِمَالٍ وَ الْبُومَةِ الصَّارِحَةِ
وَ الْمَرْأَةِ الشَّمْطَاءِ تَلْقَى فَرْجَهَا وَ الْأَتَانِ الْعَضْبَاءِ يَعْنِي الْجَدْعَاءَ فَمَنْ أَوْجَسَ فِي نَفْسِهِ مِنْهُنَّ شَيْئًا فَلْيَقُلِ اِغْتَصَمْتُ
بِكَ يَا رَبِّ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا أَجِدُ فِي نَفْسِي فَاغْصِمْنِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ قَالَ فَيُعْصَمُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON BEGINNING A JOURNEY WITH CHARITY
text_en:
It is narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abdul Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj that
Abu Abdullah {a.s} said: "Give charity and then set out on your journey on any day you
wish."
text_ar:
بَابُ افتِتَاحِ السّفّرِ بِالصَّدَقَةِ
رَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو عَنْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : «تَصَدَّقْ وَ
أخْرُج أَيَّ يَوْمِ شِئْتَ.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON BEGINNING A JOURNEY WITH CHARITY
text_en:
It is narrated from Hammad ibn Uthman who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} whether it is disliked to travel on certain days considered
unfavorable, such as Wednesdays and others.
Imam {a.s} replied: "Begin your journey with charity, set out whenever it seems
appropriate to you, recite Ayat al-Kursi, and perform cupping (hijama) if you feel the
need."
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثُمَانَ قَالَ : قُلْتُ لأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ أَ يُكْرَهُ السَّفَرُ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ
الْمَكْرُوهَةِ مِثْلِ الْأَرْبِعَاءِ وَ غَيْرِهِ فَقَالَ «اِفْتَتِحْ سَفَرَكَ بِالصَّدَقَةِ وَ أُخْرُجْ إِذَا بَدَا لَكَ وَ اِقْرَأُ آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيَّ وَ اِحْتَجِمْ
إذَا بَدَا لَكَ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON BEGINNING A JOURNEY WITH CHARITY
text_en:
It is narrated from Ibn Abi Umair who said: I used to observe the stars and
understand their movements and their rise, and from this, certain thoughts would
enter my mind. I complained about this to Abu al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-
Kadhim, peace be upon them both.
Imam {a.s} said: "If something enters your mind, give charity to the first needy person
you encounter, and then proceed, for Allah {SWT}, the Exalted and Glorious, will ward off
harm from you."
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيّ عَنْ اِبْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ : كُنْتُ أَنظُرُ فِي النُّجُومِ وَ أَعْرِفُهَا وَ أَعْرِفُ الطَّالِعَ فَيَدْخُلُنِي مِنْ ذَلِكَ
شَيْءٌ فَشَكَوْتُ ذَلِكَ إِلَى أَبِي الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلَامُ فَقَالَ «إِذَا وَقَعَ فِي نَفْسِكَ شَيْءُ فَتَصَدَّقْ
عَلَى أَوَّلِ مِسْكِينٍ ثُمَّ اِمْضٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ يَدْفَعُ عَثكَ ».
