author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MAN WHO KILLS HIS SON, HIS
text_en:
Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Baṣir
from Abu Abdullah {a.s} who said: "A father is not executed for killing his son, but a son
is executed for killing his father."
Imam {a.s} also said: "Two men who kill one another do not inherit from each other."
text_ar:
بَابُ الرَّجُلٍ يَقْتُلُ ابْنَهُ أَوْ أَبَاهُ أَوْ أُمَّهُ
رَوَى الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ع قَالَ: «لا يُقْتَلُ ٱلْأَبُ
بِابْنِهِ إِذَا قَتَلَهُ وَ يُقْتَلُ الاِبْنُ بِأَبِيهِ إِذَا قَتَلَ أَبَاهُ» وَ قَالَ «لا يَتَوَارَثُ رَجْلاَنِ قَتَلَ أُحَدُهُمَا صَاحِبَهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.120
text_chunk:
Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Baṣir
from Abu Abdullah {a.s} who said: "A father is not executed for killing his son, but a son
is executed for killing his father."
Imam {a.s} also said: "Two men who kill one another do not inherit from each other."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MAN WHO KILLS HIS SON, HIS
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-
Baqir {a.s} that he said regarding a man who killed his mother:
"If he killed her accidentally, he is entitled to a share of her inheritance. However, if he
killed her intentionally, he does not inherit anything from her."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمِّدُ بْنُ قَيْسِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ أَنْهُ قَالَ: فِي رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ أَمَّهُ قَالَ «إِذَا كَانَ خَطَأَ فَإِنَّ
لَهُ نَصِيباً مِنْ مِيرَاثِهَا وَ إِنْ كَانَ قَتَلَهَا مُتَعَمَّداً فَلاَ يَرِثُ مِنْهَا شَيْئاً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.120 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.237

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MAN WHO KILLS HIS SON, HIS
text_en:
Amr ibn Shimr narrated from Jabir from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali
Al-Baqir {a.s} regarding a man who kills his son or his slave.
Imam {a.s} said: “He is not to be killed for that, but he should be severely beaten and
exiled from his hometown."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَمْرُو بْنُ شِمْرٍ عَنْ جَابِرٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي الرَّجُلِ يَقْتُلُ اِبْنَهُ أَوْ عَبْدَهُ قَالَ «لا يُقْتَلُ
بِهِ وَ لَكِنْ يُضْرَبُ ضَرْباً شَدِيداً وَ يُنْفَى مِنْ مَسْقَطِ رَأْسِهِ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MAN WHO KILLS HIS SON, HIS FATHER, OR HIS MOTHER
text_en:
Ali ibn Riʾab narrated from Abu Ubaydah who said:
I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who killed his
mother.
Imam {a.s} said: “He does not inherit from her, and he should be killed for it in a state of
humiliation. Yet, I do not think that his killing would be an expiation for his sin."
text_ar:
رَوَى عَلِيُّ بْنُ رِئَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرِ ع عَنْ رَجُلٍ قَتَلَ أَمَّهُ قَالَ لَا يَرِثُهَا وَ يُقْتَلُ بِهَا وَ
هُوَ صَاغِرٌ وَ لَا أَظُنُّ قَثْلَهُ بِهَا كَفَارَةً لِذَنْبِهِ.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.120

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE,
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Riʾab from Muhammad ibn Qays
from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} who said:
"A Muslim is not subjected to retaliation (qiṣaṣ) for killing a Dhimmi (non-Muslim under
Muslim protection) in cases of murder or bodily injury. However, the Muslim is
required to compensate for his offense against the Dhimmi according to the extent of
his harm, and this is equivalent to the Diyyah (blood money) of the Dhimmi, which is
eight hundred dirhams."
text_ar:
بَابُ الْمُسْلِمِ يَقْتُلُ الذَّمَّيَّ أَوِ الْعَبْدَ أَوِ الْمُدَبَّرَ أَوِ الْمُكَاتَبَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُونَ الْمُسْلِمَ
رَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «لا
يُقَادُ مُسْلِمٌ بِذِمِّيَّ فِي الْقَتَلِ وَ لاَ فِي الْجِرَاحَاتِ وَ لَكِنْ يُوْخَذُ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِ فِي جِنَايَتِهِ لِلذَّمِّيِّ بِقَدْرٍ جِنَايَتِهِ عَلَى
اَلذَّمِّيِّ عَلَى قَدْرِ دِيَةِ الذَّمِّيَّ ثَمَانِمَائَةِ دِرْهَمِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.310 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.121 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.188 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.4 p.270 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.2 p.362 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.657 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.108 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.170

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE,
text_en:
Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Baṣir who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about the blood money (diyyah) for a Jew, a Christian, and a
Magian.
Imam {a.s} replied: “They are equal - eight hundred (dirhams), eight hundred (dirhams)."
I asked: “May I be your ransom, if they are caught committing an immoral act in the
land of the Muslims, is the legal punishment (hadd) applied to them?"
Imam {a.s} said: “Yes, they are judged according to the rulings of the Muslims."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مُسْكَانَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ دِيَةِ الْيَهْودِيَّ وَ النِّصْرَانِيّ وَ
الْمَجُوسِيَّ قَالَ «هُمْ سَوَاءً ثَمَانُمِائَةِ ثَمَانُمِائَةِ» قَالَ قُلْتُ جُعِلَتْ فِدَاكَ إِنْ أُخِذُوا فِي بَلَدِ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ هُمْ يَعْمَلُونَ
الْفَاجِشَةَ أَيُقَامُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْحَدُ قَال «نَعَمْ يُحكَمُ فِيهم بِأَحْكَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.121 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.186 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.662 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.219

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Samaah ibn Mihran who reported from Abu
Abdullah {a.s} that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) sent Khalid ibn Al-
Walid to Bahrain, where he was involved in shedding the blood of some Jews,
Christians, and Magians.
Khalid wrote to the Messenger of Allah {SWT} (peace be upon him and his family), saying:
"I have shed the blood of some Jews and Christians, and I paid their blood money
(diyyah) as eight hundred (dirhams) each. I also shed the blood of some Magians, but
you did not give me any prior instruction regarding them."
The Messenger of Allah {SWT} (peace be upon him and his family) wrote back to him:
"Their blood money is the same as that of the Jews and Christians," and he added,
"They are People of the Book."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «بَعَثَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللّهُ
عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ خَالِدَ بْنَ الْوَلِيدِ إِلَى الْبَحْرَيْنِ فَأَصَابَ بِهَا دِمَاءَ قَوْمٍ مِنَ ٱلْيَهُودِ وَ النَّصَارَى وَ الْمَجُوسِ فَكَتَبَ إِلَى رَسُولٍ
اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ إِنِّي أَصَبْتُ دِمَاءَ قَوْمٍ مِنَ الْيَهُودِ وَ النَّصَارَى فَوَدَيْتُهُمْ ثَمَانَمِائَةٍ ثَمَانَمِائَةٍ وَ أَصَبْتُ دِمَاءَ
قَوْمٍ مِنَ الْمَجُوسِ وَ لَمْ تَكُنْ عَهِدْتَ إِلَيْ فِيهِمْ عَهْداً قَالَ فَكَتَبَ إِلَيْهِ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ «إِنَّ دِيَتَهُمْ
مِثْلُ دِيَةِ الْيَهُودِ وَ النَّصَارَى » وَ قَالَ «إِنَّهُمْ أَهْلُ كِتَابِ» ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.121 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.186 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.4 p.268 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.612 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.661 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.218

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Riʾab from Ḍurays Al-Kunasi who
reported from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} regarding a Christian
man who killed a Muslim. When he was captured, he accepted Islam.
Imam {a.s} was asked: “Should he be killed for the Muslim he murdered?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “Yes."
It was then asked: “And if he does not accept Islam?"
Imam {a.s} said: “He will be handed over to the heirs of the murdered person. If they
wish, they may kill him, if they wish, they may pardon him, and if they wish, they may
enslave him. And if he possesses any tangible wealth, it will be handed over to the
heirs of the murdered person along with him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ ضُرَيْسِ الْكُنَاسِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي
نَصْرَانِيّ قَتَلَ مُسْلِماً فَلَمَّا أُخِذَ أَسْلَمَ أَقْتِلُهُ بِهِ قَالَ «نَعَمْ» قِيلَ فَإِنْ لَمْ يُسْلِمْ قَالَ »يُدْفَعُ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ فَإِنْ
شَاءُوا قَتَلُوا وَ إِنْ شَاءُوا عَفَوْا وَ إِنْ شَاءُوا اِسْتَرَقُّوا وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَعَهُ مَالٌ عَيْنٌ لَهُ دُفِعَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ هُوَ وَ
مَالَهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.310 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.121 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.190 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.590 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.659 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.110

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Baṣir,
who reported from Abu Abdullah {a.s} that he said:
"The blood money (diyyah) for a Jew and a Christian is four thousand (dirhams), four
thousand (dirhams), and the blood money for a Magian (Zoroastrian) is eight hundred
dirhams."
Imam {a.s} also said: "Indeed, the Magians have a book called Jamaspf."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْقَاسِمُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ أَبِي حَمْرَةَ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «دِيَةُ
اَلْيَهُودِيِّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيَّ أَرْبَعَةُ الاَفِ أَرْبَعَةُ آلاَفِ وَدِيَةُ ٱلْمَجُوسِيَّ ثَمَانُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمِ» وَ قَالَ «أَمَا إِنَّ لِلْمَجُوسِ كِتَاباً يُقَالُ
لَهُ جَامَاسْفُ ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.122

وَ قَدْ رُوِيَ: «أَنَّ دِيَةَ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيِّ وَ ٱلْمَجُوسِيّ أَرْبَعَةُ آلاَفِ دِرْهَمِ أَرْبَعَةُ آلاَفِ دِرْهَمِ لِأَنَّهُمْ أَهْلُ
الكِتَابٍ»

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Abdullah ibn Al-Mughirah narrated from Mansur, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from
Abu Abdullah {a.s} who said:
"The blood money (diyyah) for a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is equal to that of a
Muslim."

Scholar's Note:
The compiler of this book, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, commented that these
narrations differ according to circumstances. Their differences are not due to
inconsistency but rather to varying conditions.
If the Jew, Christian, or Magian adheres to the terms of their covenant, refraining from
openly consuming alcohol, committing adultery, engaging in usury, eating carrion and
pork, marrying close relatives, publicly eating and drinking during the day in Ramadan,
entering Muslim mosques, and if they conduct their activities by leaving at night and
entering during the day for trade and fulfilling their needs, then whoever kills one of
them must pay four thousand dirhams.
However, opponents have taken the apparent meaning of the narration without
considering the specific conditions.
If the Imam grants them protection, includes them under his covenant, and they
uphold the agreed-upon conditions - such as paying the jizyah - then if one of them is
killed by mistake, the killer must pay the full blood money equal to that of a Muslim.
This ruling aligns with the principles of justice and protection established by the
covenant.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ مَنصُورٍ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ تَغْلِبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «دِيَةُ
الْيَهُودِيّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيّ وَ الْمَجُوسِيِّ دِيَةُ الْمُسْلِمِ».
قَالَ مُصَنَّفُ هَذَا الْكِتَابِ رَجِمَهُ اللَّهُ هَذِهِ الْأَحْبَارُ اخْتَلَفَتْ لِاخْتِلَافِ الْأَحْوَالِ وَ لَيْسَتْ هِيَ عَلَى اخْتِلَافِهَا فِي حَالٍ وَاحِدَةٍ مَتَى
كَانَ الْيَهُودِيُّ وَ النَّصْرَانِيُ وَ الْمَجُوسِيُ عَلَى مَا عُوهِدُوا عَلَيْهِ مِنْ تَرْكِ إِظْهَارِ شُرْبِ الْخُمُورِ وَ إِثْيَانِ الزِّنَا وَ أَكْلِ الرِّبَا وَ الْمَيْتَةِ
وَ لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَ نِكَاحِ الْأَخَوَاتِ وَ إِظْهَارِ الْأَكْلِ وَ الشُّرْبِ بِالنَّهَارِ فِي شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ وَ اجْتِنَابٍ صُعُودِ مَسَاجِدِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ
اسْتَعْمَلُوا الْخُرُوجَ بِاللَّيْلِ عَنْ ظَهْرَانَيِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ الدُّخُولَ بِالنَّهَارِ لِلتَسَوْقِ وَ قَضَاءِ الْحَوَائِجِ فَعَلَى مَنْ قَتَلَ وَاحِداً مِنْهُمْ أَرْبَعَةُ
آلَافِ دِرْهَمِ وَ مَرَّ الْمُخَالِفُونَ عَلَى ظَاهِرِ الْحَدِيثِ فَأَخَذُوا بِهِ وَ لَمْ يَعْتَبِرُوا الْحَالَ وَ مَتَى آمَنَهُمُ الْإِمَامُ وَ جَعَلَهُمْ فِي عَهْدِهِ وَ
عَقْدِهِ وَ جَعَلَ لَهُمْ ذِمَّةً وَ لَمْ يَنْقُضُوا مَا عَاهَدَهُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الشَّرَائِطِ الَّتِي ذَكَرْنَاهَا وَ أَقَرُوا بِالْجِزْيَةِ وَ أَدَّوْهَا فَعَلَى مَنْ قَتَلَ
وَاجِداً مِنْهُمْ خَطَأْ دِيَةُ الْمُسْلِمِ وَ تَصْدِيقُ ذَلِكَ.
commentary:
The compiler of this book, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, commented that these
narrations differ according to circumstances. Their differences are not due to
inconsistency but rather to varying conditions.
If the Jew, Christian, or Magian adheres to the terms of their covenant, refraining from
openly consuming alcohol, committing adultery, engaging in usury, eating carrion and
pork, marrying close relatives, publicly eating and drinking during the day in Ramadan,
entering Muslim mosques, and if they conduct their activities by leaving at night and
entering during the day for trade and fulfilling their needs, then whoever kills one of
them must pay four thousand dirhams.
However, opponents have taken the apparent meaning of the narration without
considering the specific conditions.
If the Imam grants them protection, includes them under his covenant, and they
uphold the agreed-upon conditions - such as paying the jizyah - then if one of them is
killed by mistake, the killer must pay the full blood money equal to that of a Muslim.
This ruling aligns with the principles of justice and protection established by the
covenant.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Aban, from Zurara, from Abu
Abdullah {a.s} who said: "Whoever was granted protection (dhimmah) by Messenger of
Allah {SWT} (peace be upon him and his family), his blood money (diyyah) is complete (to
that of a muslim)."

Scholar's Note:
Zurara commented: "These are the people about whom Abu Abdullah {a.s} spoke,
referring to those whom the Prophet {saws} granted protection."
Furthermore, whoever opposes the Imam by intentionally killing one of these
protected individuals deserves capital punishment - not because of the sanctity of the
dhimmi himself but due to the transgression against the authority of the Muslim
leader.
text_ar:
مَا رَوَاهُ الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ سَعِيدِ عَنْ فَضَالَةَ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «مَنْ أَعْطَاهُ
رَسُولُ اللّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ ذِمَّةً فَدِيَتُهُ كَامِلَةٌ»
قَالَ زُرَارَةُ فَهَوْلاءِ مَا قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ وَ هُمْ مَنْ أَعْطَاهَمْ ذِمَةً. وَ عَلَى مَنْ خَالَفَ الإِمَامَ فِي قَتْلٍ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ
مُتَعَمَّداً الْقَتْلُ لِخِلَافِهِ عَلَى إمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَا لِحُرْمَةِ الذَمَّيَّ.
commentary:
Zurara commented: "These are the people about whom Abu Abdullah {a.s} spoke,
referring to those whom the Prophet {saws} granted protection."
Furthermore, whoever opposes the Imam by intentionally killing one of these
protected individuals deserves capital punishment - not because of the sanctity of the
dhimmi himself but due to the transgression against the authority of the Muslim
leader.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ali ibn Al-Hakam narrated from Abu Al-Maghra, from Abu Basir, from Abu
Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"If a Muslim kills a Christian and the family of the Christian wishes to execute him, they
may do so, but they must pay the difference between the two blood monies (diyyahs)."

Scholar's Note:
Similarly, if the Muslim was habitually killing them, he would be executed due to his
opposition to the authority of the Imam {a.s}, even if the Christians were openly hostile
and deceitful towards the Muslims.
text_ar:
كَمَا رَوَاهُ عَلِي بْنُ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبِي ٱلْمَغْرَاءِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قَتَلَ
الْمُسْلِمُ النَّصْرَانِيّ فَأَرَادَ أَهْلُ النَّصْرَانِيَّ أَنْ يَقْثُلُوهُ قَتَلُوهُ وَ أَدَّوْا فَضْلَ مَا بَيْنَ الدِّيَتَيْنِ».
وَ كَذَلِكَ إِذَا كَانَ الْمُسْلِمُ مُتَعَوِّداً لِقَثْلِهِمْ قُتِلَ لِخِلَافِهِ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ ع وَ إِنْ كَانُوا مُظْهِرِينَ الْعَدَاوَةَ وَ الْغِشَّ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ
commentary:
Similarly, if the Muslim was habitually killing them, he would be executed due to his
opposition to the authority of the Imam {a.s}, even if the Christians were openly hostile
and deceitful towards the Muslims.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ali ibn Al-Hakam narrated from Aban, from Ismail ibn Al-Fadl, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about the blood of the Magians, Jews, and Christians -
whether there is any penalty upon someone who kills them if they deceive the Muslims
and openly display hostility and treachery towards them.
Imam {a.s} replied: “No, unless he is habitual in killing them."
He further said: I asked Imam {a.s} about a Muslim being killed for killing a person from
the People of the Book (Ahl Al-Dhimmah) or from the People of the Scripture.
Imam {a.s} replied: “No, unless he is accustomed to doing so and does not desist from
killing them, then he will be killed and humiliated."

Scholar's Note:
If the Jews, Christians, and Magians fail to uphold the conditions they were bound by,
then whoever kills one of them must pay eight hundred dirhams in compensation, and
a Muslim is not executed for killing them nor for injuring them, as I mentioned earlier
in this chapter.
However, rebellion against the Imam and refusal to comply with his authority can
warrant execution even for lesser offenses, similar to the ruling on the man who
swears to avoid his wife (Al-Mu'li). If after four months he neither reconciles with his
wife nor divorces her, the Imam orders him to choose, and if he refuses, his neck is
struck for defying the authority of the Muslim leader.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَلِيْ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ عَنْ أَبَانٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ الْفَضْلِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ دِمَاءٍ
الْمَجُوسِ وَ الْيَهُودِ وَ النَّصَارَى هَلْ عَلَى مَنْ قَتَلَهُمْ شَيْءَ إِذَا غَشُوا الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَ أَظْهَرُوا الْعَدَاوَةَ وَ الْغِشِّ لَهُمْ قَالَ
«لا إلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مُتَعَوِّداً لِقَثلِهِمْ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْمُسْلِمِ يُقْتَلُ بِأَهْلِ الذَّمَّةِ وَ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ إِذَا قَتَلَهُمْ قَالَ «لا إلا
أَنْ يَكُونَ مُعْتَاداً لِذَلِكَ لاَ يَدَعُ قَثْلَهُمْ فَيُقْتَلُ وَ هُوَ صَاغِرٌ».
وَ مَتَى لَمْ يَكُنِ الْيَهُودُ وَ النَّصَارَى وَ الْمَجُوسُ عَلَى مَا عُوهِدُوا عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الشَّرَائِطِ التِي ذَكَرْنَاهَا فَعَلَى مَنْ قَتَلَ وَاجِداً مِنْهُمْ
ثَمَانُمَائَةِ دِرْهَمِ وَ لَا يُقَادُ لَهُمْ مِنْ مُسْلِمِ فِي قَتْلٍ وَ لَا جِرَاحَةٍ كَمَا ذَكَرْتُهُ فِي أوَّلِ هَذَا الْبَابِ وَ الْخِلَافُ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ وَ الاِمْتِنَاعُ
عَلَيْهِ يُوجِبَانِ الْقَثَلَ فِيمَا دُونَ ذَلِكَ كَمَا جَاءَ فِي الْمُوْلِي إِذَا وَقَفَ بَعْدَ أَرْبَعَةِ أَشهُرِ أَمَرَهُ الْإِمَامُ بِأَنْ يَفِيءَ أَوْ يُطَلِّقَ فَمَتَى لَمْ
يَفِى وَ امْتَنَعَ مِنَ الطَّلَاقِ ضُرِبَتْ عُنُقُهُ لِامْتِنَاعِهِ عَلَى إِمَامِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ.
commentary:
If the Jews, Christians, and Magians fail to uphold the conditions they were bound by,
then whoever kills one of them must pay eight hundred dirhams in compensation, and
a Muslim is not executed for killing them nor for injuring them, as I mentioned earlier
in this chapter.
However, rebellion against the Imam and refusal to comply with his authority can
warrant execution even for lesser offenses, similar to the ruling on the man who
swears to avoid his wife (Al-Mu'li). If after four months he neither reconciles with his
wife nor divorces her, the Imam orders him to choose, and if he refuses, his neck is
struck for defying the authority of the Muslim leader.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
The Prophet Muhammad {saws}, peace be upon him and his family, said:
"Whoever harms one under my protection (dhimmah) has indeed harmed me."

Scholar's Note:
If causing harm to them equates to harming the Prophet {saws} himself, then how severe
must it be when it comes to killing them?
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) intended through this statement to
emphasize the sanctity of his daughter, Sayyidah Fatimah {s.a} (peace be upon her).
Prophet {saws} stated: "Whoever harms one under my protection has harmed me," to
prevent any form of oppression or harm towards them. How much greater then is the
harm caused to my daughter (Fatimah {s.a}), my own flesh and blood, who is the leader
of the women of all times?
Prophet {saws} reinforced this meaning by saying: "Whoever harms her (Sayyidah Fatima
{s.a}) has harmed me, whoever angers her (Sayyidah Fatima {s.a}) has angered me, and
whoever pleases her (Sayyidah Fatima {s.a}) has pleased me."
text_ar:
وَ قَدْ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ : «مَنْ آذَى ذِمَّتِي فَقَدْ آذَانِي».
فَإِذَا كَانَ فِي إِيذَائِهِمْ إِيذَاءُ النَّبِيِّ ص فَكَيْفَ فِي قَثْلِهِمْ وَ إِنَّمَا أَرَادَ النَّبِيُّ ص بِذَلِكَ- فَاطِمَةَ ص وَ قَالَ إِذَا كَانَ مَنْ آذَى ذِمَّتِي
فَقَدْ آذَانِي لِمَنْعِي مِنْ ظُلْمِهِ وَ إِيذَائِهِ فَكَيْفَ مَنْ آذَى ابْنَتِي وَ وَاحِدَتِي الَتِي هِيَ بَضْعَةٌ مِنَّي وَ سَيِّدَةُ نِسَاءِ الْأَوْلِينَ وَ الْآَخِرِينَ
وَأْتْبَعَ ع ذَلِكَ بِأنْ قَالَ: «مَنْ آذَاهَا فَقَدْ آذَانِي وَ مَنْ غَاظَهَا فَقَدْ غَاظَنِي وَ مَنْ سَرَهَا فَقَدْ سَرَّنِي».

chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Buraid Al-Ijli narrated from Abu Abdullah {a.s} that he was asked about a
Muslim who gouged out the eye of a Christian.
Imam {a.s} replied: “The blood money (diyyah) for the eye of a dhimmi (non-Muslim
under Islamic protection) is four hundred dirhams."

Scholar's Note:
This ruling applies to one whose full blood money for their life is eight hundred
dirhams.
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ بُرَيْدِ ٱلْعِجْلِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَلامُ عَنْ مُسْلِمِ
فَقَاَ عَيْنَ نَصْرَانِيّ فَقَالَ «إِنَّ دِيَةَ عَيْنِ الذَّمِّيِّ أَرْبَعْمِائَةِ دِرْهَمِ».
هَذَا لِمَنْ دِيَةُ نَفْسِهِ ثَمَانُمِائَةٍ دِرْهَمِ.
commentary:
This ruling applies to one whose full blood money for their life is eight hundred
dirhams.

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Uthman ibn Isa narrated from Sama'ah that Abu Abdullah {a.s} said:
“A slave is to be killed for killing a free man, but a free man is not to be killed for killing
a slave. However, he must pay the slave's value and be severely beaten so that he does
not repeat such an act."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عُثْمَانُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «يُقْتَلُ الْعَبْدُ بِالْحُرِّ وَ لا يُقْتَلُ
الْحُرُّ بِالْعَبْدِ وَ لَكِنْ يُغَرَّمُ قِيمَتَهُ وَ يُضْرَبُ ضَرْباً شَدِيداً حَتَّى لا يَعُودَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.125

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi that Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said regarding a man who intentionally kills his slave:
"I prefer that he frees a slave, fasts for two consecutive months, and feeds sixty needy
people, and then he should repent after that."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى حَمَّادٌ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي رَجُلٍ يَقْتُلُ مَمْلُوكَهُ مُتَعَمِّداً قَالَ
«يُعْجِبُنِي أَنْ يُفْتِقَ رَقَبَةً وَ يَصُومَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ وَ يُطْعِمَ سِتَّينَ مِسْكِيناً ثُمَّ تَكُونَ النَّوْبَةُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ».

chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Humran asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man
who struck his slave, and the slave died as a result of the beating.
Imam {a.s} replied: “He must free a slave."
text_ar: - وَسَأَلَ حُمْرَانْ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ : عَنْ رَجُلٍ ضَرَبَ مَمْلُوكا لَهُ فَمَاتَ مِنْ ضَرْبِهِ قَالَ «يُفْتِقُ رَقَبَةً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.125

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Yahya ibn Abi Al-'Ala narrated from Abu Abdullah {a.s} who said:
"If a slave kills a free man, the family of the murdered person has the choice: if they
wish, they may kill him, and if they wish, they may enslave him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى يَحْيَى بْنُ أَبِي الْعَلاَءِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: («إِذَا قَتَلَ ٱلْعَبْدُ الْحُرَّ فَلِأُهْلِ الْمَقْتُولِ إِنْ
شَاءُوا قَتَلُوا وَ إِنْ شَاءُوا اِسْتَعْبَدُوا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.125 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.194 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.639 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.100

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}, Commander of the Faithful, ruled regarding a
mukatab (a slave who had a contract for freedom) who was killed: "The portion of him
that had been freed is calculated, and the blood money for that part is paid as that of
a free man, and the portion that remained in servitude is paid as the blood money of a
slave."
Imam {a.s} also said: “A slave does not burden his family with any liability beyond
himself."
text_ar:
: «وَ قَضَى أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ فِي مُكَاتَبِ قُتِلَ فَقَالَ «يُحْسَبُ مَا عَتَقَ مِنْهُ فَيُوَدى دِيَةُ اَلْحُرِّ وَ
مَا رَقَّ دِيَةُ الْعَبْدِ» » وَ قَالَ «اَلْعَبْدُ لاَ يُغْرِمُ أَهْلَهُ وَرَاءَ نَفْسِهِ شَيْئا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.126 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.651

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} was asked about a slave who injured a free man.
Imam {a.s} said: “If the free man wishes, he may take retribution (qisas) from him, and if
he wishes, he may take the slave if the injury is severe enough to warrant his execution.
If the injury does not warrant execution, then the slave’s master must pay
compensation (diyyah).
If the master refuses to pay the compensation, then the injured free man has a right
over the slave equivalent to the diyyah of his injury, and the rest belongs to the master.
The slave is then sold, the injured party takes his due, and the remainder is returned
to the master.”
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنِ الْفُضَيْلِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي
عَبْدٍ جَرَحَ حُرَاً قَالَ «إِنْ شَاءَ الْحُرُ اِقْتَصَّ مِنْهُ وَ إِنْ شَاءَ أَخَذَهُ إِنْ كَانَتِ الْجِرَاحَةُ تُجِيطُ بِرَقَبَتِهِ وَ إِنْ كَانَثْ لا
تُجِيطُ بِرَقَبَتِهِ اِفْتَدَاهُ مَوْلاهُ فَإِنْ أَبَى مَوْلاهُ أَنْ يَفْتَدِيَهُ كَانَ لِلْحُرِّ الْمَجْرُوحِ مِنَ الْعَبْدِ بِقَدْرِ دِيَةِ جِرَاحَتِهِ وَ الْبَاقِي
بِلْمَوْلَى يُبَاعُ الْعَبْدُ فَيَأْخُذُ ٱلْمَجْرُوحُ حَقّهُ وَ يُرَدْ الْبَاقِي عَلَى ٱلْمَوْلَى».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.305 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.126 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.196 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.641 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.166 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.210

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Imam Abu Abdullah {a.s} was asked about a man who inflicted a mudhiha (a
wound exposing the bone) on a slave.
Imam {a.s} said: “He is liable to pay half of one-tenth of the slave's value."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ الْعَبْدِيِّ عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلامُ :
فِي رَجْلٍ شَجَّ عَبْداَ مُوضِحَةً قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ نِصْفُ عُشَرِ قِيمَتِهِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.306 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.126 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.193 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.643 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.167 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.388

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} was asked about a slave who
injured two men.
Imam {a.s} said: “He is to be divided between them if his crime equals his full value."
It was asked: “What if he injured one man in the morning and another in the evening?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “He is to be divided between them as long as the governor has not
ruled regarding the first injured person. But if the governor had already ruled and
handed the slave over to the first injured party due to his injury, and then the slave
committed another injury afterward, then his liability for that second injury falls upon
the latter victim."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ : فِي عَبْدِ جَرَحَ رَجُلَيْنِ قَالَ
«هُوَ بَيْنَهُمَا إنْ كَانَتْ جِنَايَتُهُ تُحِيطُ بِقِيمَتِهِ» قِيلَ لَهُ فَإِنْ جَرَحَ رَجُلاً فِي أَوَلِ النَّهَارِ وَ جَرَحَ آخَرَ فِي آخِرِ النَّهَارِ
قَالَ «هُوَ بَيْنَهُمَا مَا لَمْ يَحْكُمِ الْوَالِي فِي الْمَجْرُوحِ الْأَوَّلِ فَإِنْ كَانَ الْوَالِي قَدْ حَكَمَ فِي الْمَجْرُوحِ الْأَوَّلِ فَدَفَعَهُ إِلَيْهِ
بِجِنَايَتِهِ فَجَنَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ جِنَايَةً فَإِنَّ جِنَايَتَهُ عَلَى الْأَخِيرِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.127 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.195 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.4 p.274 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.2 p.360 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.586 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.641 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.104

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
“If a free man kills a slave, he must pay the slave's value and be disciplined."
It was asked: “What if the value of the slave is twenty thousand?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “The value of a slave cannot exceed the blood money (diyyah) of a
free person."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَلِي بْنُ رِئَابٍ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلامُ قَالَ: «إِذَا قَتَلَ ٱلْحُرُ ٱلْعَبْدَ غُرِّمَ قِيمَتَهُ وَ
أَدِّبَ» قِيلَ لَهُ فَإِنْ كَانَتْ قِيمَتُهُ عِشرِينَ أَلْفا قَالَ «لا يُجَاوَزُ بِقِيمَةِ عَبْدٍ عَنْ دِيَةٍ حُرَّ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.305 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.127 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.193 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.4 p.274 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.636 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.97 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.207

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
In the narration of Al-Sakuni, Commander of the Faithful {a.s} said:
“The injuries of slaves are to be compensated in the same manner as the injuries of
free people, according to their value."
text_ar:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ السَّكُونِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : «جِرَاحَاتُ الْعَبِيدِ عَلَى نَحْوِ جِرَاحَاتٍ
اَلْأَحْرَارِ فِي الثَّمَنِ».

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Muhammad Al-Wabishi who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a group of people who claimed that a slave had
committed an offense warranting his execution, and the slave confessed to it.
Imam {a.s} said: “The confession of a slave is not valid against his master."
Imam {a.s} further said: “But if they establish evidence for what they claimed against the
slave, they may take the slave for it or his master may ransom him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي مُحَمَّدِ ٱلْوَابِشِيِّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ عَنْ قَوْمِ إِدَّعَوْا عَلَى
عَبْدٍ جِنَايَةً تُجِيطُ بِرَقَبَتِهِ فَأَقَرَّ الْعَبْدُ بِهَا قَالَ «لا يَجُوزُ إقْرَارُ الْعَبْدِ عَلَى سَيِّدِهِ» قَالَ «فَإِنْ أَقَامُوا ٱلْبَيّنَةَ عَلَى مَا
اِدَّعَوْا عَلَى الْعَبْدِ أَخَذُوا الْعَبْدَ بِهَا أَوْ يَفْتَدِيَهُ مَوْلاهُ».

text_chunk:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Muhammad Al-Wabishi who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a group of people who claimed that a slave had
committed an offense warranting his execution, and the slave confessed to it.
Imam {a.s} said: “The confession of a slave is not valid against his master."
Imam {a.s} further said: “But if they establish evidence for what they claimed against the
slave, they may take the slave for it or his master may ransom him."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham bin Salim from Abu Basir who said:
I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a mudabbar (a slave
promised freedom after the owner's death) who intentionally killed a man.
Imam {a.s} said: “He is to be killed in retaliation."
I asked: “What if he killed him by mistake?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “He is handed over to the heirs of the murdered person, and he
becomes their slave. If they wish, they can enslave him, and if they wish, they can sell
him, but they have no right to kill him."
Then Imam {a.s} said: “O’ Abu Muhammad, indeed the mudabbar is still a slave."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ مُدَبَّرٍ قَتَلَ
رَجُلاً عَمْداً قَالَ «يُقْتَلُ بِهِ» قُلْتُ فَإِنْ قَتَلَهُ خَطَأْ قَالَ «يُذْفَعُ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ فَيَكُونُ لَهُمْ رِقَا فَإِنْ شَاءُوا اِسْتَرَقُوا
وَ إِنْ شَاءُوا بَاعُوا وَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ أَنْ يَقْتُلُوهُ» ثُمَّ قَالَ «يَا أَبَا مُحَمَّدٍ إِنَّ الْمُدَبَّرَ مَمْلُوكٌ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.305 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.127 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.197 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.647 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.102

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad bin Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a mukatab (a slave who
has a contract for gradual emancipation) who unintentionally killed a man.
Imam {a.s} said: “If his master, when drafting the emancipation contract, stipulated that
if he fails to fulfill the payment, he would return to slavery, then he is treated like a
slave and handed over to the heirs of the murdered person.
If they wish, they may enslave him, and if they wish, they may sell him.
But if his master, when drafting the contract, did not make such a stipulation and the
mukatab had already paid part of the contract amount, then Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib {a.s}
used to say:
'He is freed in proportion to what he has paid of his contract, and it is upon the Imam
to pay the heirs of the murdered person an amount equivalent to the portion of
freedom the mukatab had earned. The blood of a Muslim must not be wasted.'
I {a.s} also believe that regarding the remaining unpaid portion of the contract, the
mukatab should remain as a slave to the heirs of the murdered person, serving them
for the rest of his life in proportion to what remains of his contract, but they are not
permitted to sell him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُّوبَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرِ عَ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِ قَتَلَ رَجْلاً
خَطَأ فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ مَوْلاهُ جِينَ كَاتَبَهُ اِشتَرَطَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ إِنْ عَجَزَ فَهُوَ رَدَّ إِلَى ٱلرِّقَ فَهُوَ بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْمَمْلُوكِ يُدْفَعُ إِلَى
أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ فَإِنْ شَاءُوا اِسْتَرَقُوا وَ إِنْ شَاءُوا بَاعُوا وَ إِنْ كَانَ مَوْلاهُ حِينَ كَاتَبَهُ لَمْ يَشْتَرِطْ عَلَيْهِ وَ كَانَ قَدْ أَدَّى
مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ شَيْئاً فَإِنَّ عَلِيّاً عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ كَانَ يَقُولُ «يُعْتَقُ مِنَ ٱلْمُكَاتَبِ بِقَدْرٍ مَا أَدَّى مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ وَ عَلَى الْإِمَامِ
أَنْ يُوَدِّيَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ بِقَدْرٍ مَا أُعْتِقَ مِنَ ٱلْمُكَاتَبِ وَ لا يُبْطَلُ دَمُ اِمْرِي مُسْلِمِ » وَ أَرَى أَنْ يَكُونَ بِمَا بَقِيَ
عَلَى الْمُكَاتَبِ مِمَّا لَمْ يُؤَدَّهِ رِقَاً لِأَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ يَسْتَخْدِمُونَهُ حَيَاتَهُ بِقَدْرٍ مَا بَقِيَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ أَنْ يَبِيعُوْهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.308 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.128 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.198 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.652 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.105

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali bin Ri'ab from Abu Abdullah {a.s} regarding a man
who placed his slave on a riding animal, and the animal trampled a man.
Imam {a.s} said: “The compensation is upon the master."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجُلِ حَمَلَ عَبْداً لَهُ عَلَى دَابَّةٍ
فَوَطِئَتْ رَجُلاً قَالَ «اَلْغُرْمُ عَلَى الْمَوْلَى».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.351 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.128 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.155 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.227 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.844 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.253

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali bin Ri'ab from Abu Al-Ward who said:
I asked Imam Abu Jafar Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who accidentally killed a slave.
Imam {a.s} said: “He must pay the slave's value, and his value should not exceed ten
thousand dirhams."
I asked: “Who will appraise his value when he is dead?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “If the master has witnesses that his value on the day he was killed
was such and such, then the killer must pay that amount. If the master has no
witnesses, the killer must swear four times by Allah {SWT} that the slave's value was no
more than what he has appraised. If he refuses to swear and the oath is passed to the
master, then the master is given the amount he swore upon, but the value must not
exceed ten thousand dirhams."
Imam {a.s} further said: “If the slave was a believer and he was killed intentionally, the
killer must pay his value, free a slave, fast for two consecutive months, feed sixty
needy people, and repent to Allah {SWT}, the Mighty and Majestic."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَلِيَّ بْنِ رِئَابٍ عَنْ أَبِي الْوَرْدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسِّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجْلٍ قَتَلَ
عَبْداً خَطَأْ قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ قِيمَتُهُ وَ لا يُجَاوَزُ بِقِيمَتِهِ عَشَرَةَ آلآَفِ دِرْهَمِ» قُلْتُ وَ مَنْ يُقَوِّمُهُ وَ هُوَ مَيِّثُ قَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ
لِمَوْلاهُ شُهُودٌ أَنَّ قِيمَتَهُ يَوْمَ قَتَلَهُ كَذَا وَ كَذَا أُخِذَ بِهَا قَاتِلْهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِمَوْلاهُ شُهُودٌ كَانَتِ ٱلْقِيمَةُ عَلَى اَلَّذِي قَتَلَهُ
مَعَ يَمِينِهِ يَشْهَدُ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ بِاللّهِ مَا لَهُ قِيمَةُ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا قَوْمُتُهُ وَ إِنْ أَبَى أَنْ يَحْلِفَ وَ رَدَّ الْيَمِينَ عَلَى الْمَوْلَى أَعْطِيَ
الْمَوْلَى مَا حَلَفَ عَلَيْهِ وَ لا يُجَاوَزُ بِقِيمَتِهِ عَشَرَةَ آلافِ دِرْهِمِ» قَالَ «وَ إِنْ كَانَ الْعَبْدُ مُومِناً فَقَتَلَهُ عَمْداً أُعْرِمَ قِيمَتَهُ
وَ أَعْتَقَ رَقَبَةً وَ صَامَ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ وَ أَطْعَمَ سِتَّينَ مِسْكِينا وَ تَابَ إِلَى اللّهِ عَزَّ وَ جَلَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.128 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.193 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.637 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.208

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON A MUSLIM KILLING A DHIMMI, A SLAVE, A MUDABBAR, OR A MUKATAB, OR THEM KILLING A MUSLIM
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a mukatab (a slave who has entered into a contract for
his freedom) who committed an offense against a free man.
Imam {a.s} said: “If he has paid part of his mukataba (freedom contract), he is liable for
the offense in proportion to what he has paid. If he cannot cover the liability for the
offense, the remainder is taken from the master who set the contract with him."
I asked: “What if the offense was against another slave?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “It is the same; the mukatab is handed over to the master of the
injured slave. There is no compensation between the mukatab and the slave if the
mukatab has paid part of his contract. However, if he has not paid anything from his
mukataba, then compensation is taken directly from him or his master must pay for
all the damage caused by the mukatab because he is still his slave until he pays part
of his contract."
Imam {a.s} further said: “The child of a mukataba woman follows her status: if she
remains a slave, her child is a slave; and if she is freed, her child is also free."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي وَلادِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ عَنْ مُكَاتَبِ جَنَى عَلَى رَجْلٍ حُرّ
جِنَايَةً فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ أَدَّى مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ شَيْئاً، غُرِّمَ فِي جِنَايَتِهِ بِقَدْرٍ مَا أَدَّى مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ لِلْحُرِّ وَ إِنْ عَجَزَ عَنْ حَقُّ
الْجِنَايَةِ أَخِذَ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الْمَوْلَى الَّذِي كَاتَبَهُ، » قُلْتُ فَإِنْ كَانَتِ الْجِنَايَةُ لِعَبْدٍ قَالَ «عَلَى مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ يُدْفَعُ إِلَى مَوْلَى
الْعَبْدِ الَذِي جَرَحَهُ الْمُكَاتَبُ وَ لَا يُقَاصُ بَيْنَ الْمُكَاتَبِ وَ بَيْنَ الْعَبْدِ إِذَا كَانَ الْمُكَاتَبُ قَدْ أَدْى مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ شَيْئاً فَإِنْ
لَمْ يَكُنْ أَدَّى مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ شَيْئاً فَإِنَّهُ يُقَاصُّ لِلْعَبْدِ مِنْهُ أَوْ يُغَرَّمُ الْمَوْلَى كُلَّ مَا جَنَى الْمُكَاتَبُ لِأَنَّهُ عَبْدُهُ مَا لَمْ يُؤَدٍّ
مِنْ مُكَاتَبَتِهِ شَيْئًا» قَالَ »وَ وَلَدُ الْمُكَاتَبَةِ كَأُمِّهِ إِنْ رَقَتْ رَقَّ وَ إِنْ عَتَقَتْ عَتَقَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.129 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.651 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.214

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY
text_en:
In the narration of Al-Sakooni, it is reported that Commander of the Faithful
{a.s} said: "For the male child’s private part, there is full blood money (diyyah), and for
the impotent man’s private part, there is also full blood money (diyyah)."
text_ar:
بَابٌ مَا يَجِبُ فِيهِ الدِّيَةُ وَ نِصْفُ الدِّيَةِ فِيمَا دُونَ النَّفْسِ
فِي رِوَايَةِ السَّكُونِيِّ أَنْ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَالَ: «فِي ذَكَرِ الصِّبِيِّ الدِّيَةُ وَ فِي ذَكَرِ الْعِنَّينِ الدِّيَةُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.313 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.129 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.249 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.704 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.339 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.18 p.375

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY
text_en:
Abdullah ibn Maymoon narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} who
said:
"A man was brought to Commander of the Faithful {a.s} who had struck another man,
causing a reduction in his eyesight.
Commander of the Faithful {a.s} called men of similar age as the injured man and
showed them something to observe how much his vision had diminished. Imam {a.s}
then awarded the injured man blood money (diyyah) equivalent to the extent of his lost
eyesight."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَيْمُونٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَنْ أَبِيهِ عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «أَتِيَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ بِرَجْلٍ قَدْ ضَرَبَ رَجُلاً حَتَّى اِنْتَقَصَ مِنْ بَصَرِهِ فَدَعَا بِرِجَالٍ مِنْ أَسْنَانِهِ ثُمَّ أَرَاهَمْ شَيْئاً فَنَظَرَ مَا اِنْتَقَصَ
مِنْ بَصَرِهِ فَأُعْطَاهُ دِيَةَ مَا اِنْتَقَصَ مِنْ بَصَرِهِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.130 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.268 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.735 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.369
text_chunk:
Abdullah ibn Maymoon narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn
Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} who
said:
"A man was brought to Commander of the Faithful {a.s} who had struck another man,
causing a reduction in his eyesight.
Commander of the Faithful {a.s} called men of similar age as the injured man and
showed them something to observe how much his vision had diminished. Imam {a.s}
then awarded the injured man blood money (diyyah) equivalent to the extent of his lost
eyesight."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Musa ibn Bakr narrated from Al-Abd Al-Salih Imam Al-Kadhim {a.s} regarding a
man who struck another man with a stick and did not lift it from him until he died.
Imam {a.s} said: "The killer should be handed over to the heirs of the murdered man, but
he should not be left to be tortured for pleasure. Rather, retribution should be carried
out upon him with the sword."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُوسَى بْنُ بَكْرٍ عَنِ ٱلْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ : فِي رَجْلٍ ضَرَبَ رَجْلاً بِعَصاً فَلَمْ يَرْفَعْ عَنْهُ الْعَصَا
حَثَّى مَاتَ قَالَ «يُدْفَعُ إِلَى أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ وَ لَكِنْ لاَ يُثْرَكُ يُتَلَذَّذُ بِهِ وَ لَكِنْ يُجَازُ عَلَيْهِ بِالسَّيْفِ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.279 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.130 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.157 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.591 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.39 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.127

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Ibn Al-Mughira narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdullah {a.s} who
said: "The blood money (diyya) for a hand if it is cut off is fifty camels.
As for wounds that are less severe than complete amputation, a ruling shall be made
concerning them by two just individuals among you.
And whoever does not judge by what Allah {SWT} has revealed, then they are the
disbelievers."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ ٱلْمُغِيرَةِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «دِيَةُ ٱلْيَدِ إِذَا قُطِعَتْ
خَمْسُونَ مِنَ الابِلِ فَمَا كَانَ جُرُوحا دُونَ الإِصْطِلامِ فَيَحكُمُ بِهِ ذَوَا عَدْلٍ مِنْكُمْ «وَ مَنْ لَمْ يَحْكُمْ بِمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَهُ
فَأُولِئِكَ هُمُ الْكَافِرُونَ» »

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from one of the two Imams {a.s} about a man
who gouged out another man's eye, cut off his nose and ears, and then killed him.
Imam {a.s} said: "If he inflicted these injuries on him separately, then retaliation (qisas)
will be taken for each injury, and then he will be killed. But if he struck him with a single
blow that resulted in all those injuries, his neck will be struck (he will be executed),
and retaliation will not be taken for the individual injuries."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ قَيْسِ عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا: فِي رَجُلٍ فَقَاَ عَيْنَ رَجُلٍ وَ قَطَعَ أَنْفَهُ وَ أَذْنَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَتَلَهُ فَقَالَ »إِنْ كَانَ
فَرَّقَ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ أُقْتُصَّ مِنْهُ ثُمَّ قُتِلَ وَ إِنْ كَانَ ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً فَأَصَابَهُ ذَلِكَ ضُرِبَتْ عُنْقُهُ وَ لَمْ يُقْتَصَّ مِنْهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.326 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.130 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.252 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.582 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.686 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.112 • Al-Fusul Al- Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.531

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub from Buraid Al-Ijli from Abu Jafar Imam
Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} who said:
"For the tongue of a mute person, the eye of a blind person, and the private parts and
testicles of a free eunuch, one-third of the full blood money (diyya) is due.
However, for the private part of a young boy, the full blood money is due."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي أَيُوبَ عَنْ بُرَيْدِ الْعِجْلِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «إِنَّ فِي لِسَانٍ
الْأَحْرَسِ وَ عَيْنِ الْأَعْمَى وَ ذَكَرِ الْخَصِيِّ الْحُرِّ وَ أُنْتَيَنِهِ ثُلُثَ أَلدِّيَةِ وَ فِي ذَكَرِ الْغَلامِ اَلدِّيَةَ كَامِلَةً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.131

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah {a.s} say:
"The Commander of the Faithful {a.s} ruled regarding a man who was struck on his hips,
causing him to lose control over his stool and urine, that the full blood money (diyya)
is due for that."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ إسحَاقَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ قَالَ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ يَقُولُ: «قَضَى أَمِيرُ
الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ فِي الرَّجُلِ يُضْرَبُ عَلَى عِجَانِهِ فَلا يَسْتَمْسِكُ غَائِطُهُ وَ لا بَوْلُهُ «إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ الدِّيَةَ كَامِلَةً»)».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.313 • Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.315 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.131 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.248 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.699 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.371

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih from Abu Ubaydah Al-Hadhdha’
who said: I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who
struck another man on his head with the pole of a tent, delivering a single blow that
penetrated to his brain, causing him to lose his mind.
Imam {a.s} said: "If the struck man can no longer comprehend the prayer, nor
understand what is said to him or what he says, then he should be observed for a year.
If he dies within that year, the striker is subject to retaliation (qisas). However, if he
does not die within that period and his mind does not return, the striker must pay the
full blood money (diyya) from his wealth due to the loss of the victim's intellect."
I said to Imam {a.s}: What do you rule upon him regarding the head injury (shajja)?
Imam {a.s} replied: "Nothing, because he only struck him once, and that single blow
caused two injuries. Therefore, I imposed upon him the more severe of the two
injuries, which is the blood money (diyya).
Had he struck him twice, causing two separate injuries, I would have imposed upon
him compensation for both injuries, whatever they may have been - except if one of
them resulted in death, in which case the striker would face retaliation (qisas), and the
second injury would be disregarded."
Imam {a.s} further said: "If he struck him three times, one after the other, resulting in
three injuries, I would impose upon him the liability for whatever the three injuries
amounted to, unless one of them led to death, in which case the striker would face
retaliation."
Imam {a.s} added: "And if he struck him ten times, but they resulted in a single injury, I
would hold him accountable only for that single injury caused by the ten blows,
regardless of its severity, as long as it did not result in death."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِح عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ الْحَذَّاءِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ
رَجُلٍ ضَرَبَ رَجُلاً بِعَمُودِ فُسْطَاطِ عَلَى رَأْسِهِ ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً فَأْجَافَهُ حَتَّى وَصَلَتِ الضَّرْبَةُ إِلَى دِمَاعِهِ فَذَهَبَ عَقْلُهُ
فَقَالَ «إِنْ كَانَ الْمَضْرُوبُ لاَ يَعْقِلُ مِنْهَا الصَّلاَةَ وَ لاَ يَعْقِلُ مَا قَالَ وَ لاَ مَا قِيلَ لَهُ فَإِنَّهُ يُنْتَظَرُ بِهِ سَنَةً فَإِنْ مَاتَ فِيمَا
بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ السِّنَّةِ أَقِيدَ بِهِ ضَارِبُهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يَمُثْ فِيمَا بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَ السَّنَّةِ وَ لَمْ يَرْجِعْ إِلَيْهِ عَقْلُهُ أَعْرِمَ ضَارِبُهُ الدِّيَةَ
فِي مَالِهِ لِذَهَابِ عَقْلِهِ» قَالَ فَقُلْتُ لَهُ فَمَا تَرَى عَلَيْهِ فِي الشَّجَةِ شَيْئاً فَقَالَ «لا لِأَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً فَجَنَتِ
الضَّرْبَةُ جِنَايَتَيْنِ فَأَلْزَمْتُهُ أَغْلَظَ الْجِنَايَتَيْنِ وَ هِيَ الدِّيَةُ وَ لَوْ كَانَ ضَرَبَهُ ضَرْبَتَيْنِ فَجَنَتِ الضَّرْبَتَانِ جِنَايَتَيْنِ لَأَلْزَمْتُهُ
جِنَايَةَ مَا جَنَتِ الضَّرْبَتَانِ كَائِناً مَا كَانّتَا إِلاَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِيهِمَا ٱلْمَوْتُ فَيُقَادَ بِهِ ضَارِبُهُ وَ تُطْرَحَ الأُخْرَى » قَالَ «وَ إِنْ
ضَرَبَهُ ثَلاَثَ ضَرَبَاتٍ وَاحِدَةً بَعْدَ وَاحِدَةٍ فَجَنَيْنَ ثَلاَثَ جِنَايَاتٍ أَلْزَمْثُهُ جِنَايَةَ مَا جَنَيْنَ الثَّلاثُ الضَّرَبَاتِ كَائِنَاتٍ مَا
كُنَّ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِنَّ ٱلْمَوْتُ فَيُقَادَ بِهِ ضَارِبُهُ» قَالَ «وَ إنْ ضَرَبَهُ عَشْرَ ضَرَبَاتٍ فَجَنَيْنَ جِنَايَةً وَاحِدَةً أَلْزَمْتُهُ تِلْكَ
اَلْجِنَايَةَ اَلَتِي جَنَتْهَا الْعَشْرُ الضَّرَبَاتِ كَائِنَةً مَا كَانَتْ مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهَا الْمَوْتُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.325 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.131 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.253 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.685 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.366

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Habib Al-Sijistani who
said:
I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who cut off the
right hands of two men.
Imam {a.s} replied: “O’ Habib, his right hand is to be cut off in retaliation for the man
whose right hand he first severed, and his left hand is to be cut off for the man whose
right hand he severed afterward. This is because he initially cut off the first man's right
hand, and his own right hand is taken as retaliation for that. Then, for the second man,
his left hand is taken."
I said: “But Commander of the Faithful {a.s} used to cut off the right hand and the left
foot."
Imam {a.s} replied: “That ruling was for the rights of Allah {SWT}, the Exalted. However,
regarding the rights of Muslims, O’ Habib, their rights are taken in full. A hand is taken
for a hand in retaliation if the offender has two hands, and a foot is taken for a hand if
the offender has no hands."
I then asked: “Shouldn't the blood money (diyya) be imposed on him, and his foot be
spared?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “Blood money is only required when he cuts off a man's hand and
the perpetrator has neither two hands nor two feet. In such a case, blood money is
imposed because there is no remaining limb from which retaliation can be taken."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَخْبُوبٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ حَبِيبِ السِّجِسْتَانِيّ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ عَنْ
رَجُلٍ قَطَعَ يَدَيْنِ لِرَجُلَيْنِ الْيَمِينَيْنِ فَقَالَ «يَا حَبِيبُ تُقْطَعُ يَمِينُهُ لِلرَّجُلِ الَّذِي قَطَعَ يَمِينَهُ أَوْلاً وَ يُقْطَعُ يَسَارُهُ لِلَّذِي
قَطَعَ يَمِينَهُ آخِراً لِأَنَّهُ إِنَّمَا قَطَعَ يَدَ الرَّجُلِ الْأَخِيرِ وَ يَمِينُهُ قِصَاصٌ لِلرَّجُلِ الْأَوَّلِ» فَقُلْتُ إِنَّ أَمِيرَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ
السَّلاَمُ إِنَّمَا كَانَ يَقْطَعُ الْيَدَ الْيُمْنَى وَ الرِّجْلَ الْيُسْرَى فَقَالَ «إِنَّمَا كَانَ يَفْعَلُ ذَلِكَ فِيمَا يَجِبُ مِنْ حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَ
جَلَّ فَأَمَّا حُقُوقُ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ يَا حَبِيبُ فَإِنَّهُ يُوْخَذُ لَهُمْ حُقُوقُهُمْ فِي قِصَاصِ الْيَدِ بِالْيَدِ إِذَا كَانَتْ لِلْقَاطِعِ يَدْ وَ الرَّجْلُ
بِالْيَدِ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ لِلْقَاطِعِ يَدَانِ» فَقُلْتُ لَهُ أَمَا تُوجَبُ عَلَيْهِ الدِّيَةُ وَ تُثْرَكُ لَهُ رِجْلُهُ فَقَالَ «إِنَّمَا تُوجَبُ عَلَيْهِ الدِّيَةُ
إِذَا قَطَعَ يَدَ رَجُلٍ وَ لَيْسَ لِلْقَاطِعِ يَدَانٍ وَ لا رِجْلانٍ فَثَمَّ تُوجَبُ عَلَيْهِ الدِّيَةُ لِأنَّهُ لَيْسَتْ لَهُ جَارِحَةٌ يُقَاصُّ مِنْهَا».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.319 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.132 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.259 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.587 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.683 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.174
text_chunk:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Habib Al-Sijistani who
said:
I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} about a man who cut off the
right hands of two men.
Imam {a.s} replied: “O’ Habib, his right hand is to be cut off in retaliation for the man
whose right hand he first severed, and his left hand is to be cut off for the man whose
right hand he severed afterward. This is because he initially cut off the first man's right
hand, and his own right hand is taken as retaliation for that. Then, for the second man,
his left hand is taken."
I said: “But Commander of the Faithful {a.s} used to cut off the right hand and the left
foot."
Imam {a.s} replied: “That ruling was for the rights of Allah {SWT}, the Exalted. However,
regarding the rights of Muslims, O’ Habib, their rights are taken in full. A hand is taken
for a hand in retaliation if the offender has two hands, and a foot is taken for a hand if
the offender has no hands."
I then asked: “Shouldn't the blood money (diyya) be imposed on him, and his foot be
spared?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “Blood money is only required when he cuts off a man's hand and
the perpetrator has neither two hands nor two feet. In such a case, blood money is
imposed because there is no remaining limb from which retaliation can be taken."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara
from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"For the hand, there is half of the full blood money (diyya), and for both hands together,
the full diyya is due. Similarly, for both legs, the full diyya applies.
For the male organ, if the glans (Al-hashafa) and above it are cut off, the full diyya is
required.
For the nose, if the soft part (Al-marin) is cut off, the full diyya applies."

Scholar's Note:
The compiler of this book, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, commented:
I found in the book of Ibn Al-A'rabi regarding the description of human anatomy that
Al-marin refers to the soft part of the cartilage, and cartilage is the thin, white, bone-
like tissue found in the soft part of the nose. The entire marin consists of cartilage.
Imam {a.s} further said: "For the lips, the full diyya applies. For both eyes, the full diyya
is due, and for one eye, half of the diyya is required."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ عُرْوَةَ عَنِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
«فِي أَلْيَدِ نِصْفُ الدِّيَةِ وَ فِي الْيَدَيْنِ جَمِيعا الدِّيَةُ وَ فِي الرِّجْلَيْنِ كَذَلِكَ وَ فِي الذَّكَرِ إِذَا قُطِعَتِ الْحَشَفَةُ وَ مَا قَوْقَ
ذَلِكَ اَلدِّيَةُ وَ فِي الْأَنْفِ إِذَا قُطِعَ الْمَارِنُ الدِّيَةُ»
قَالَ مُصَنِّفُ هَذَا الْكِتَابِ رَجِمَهُ اللَهُ وَجَدْتُ فِي كِتَابِ اِبْنِ الْأَعْرَابِيّ فِي صِفَةِ خَلْقِ ٱلْإِنْسَانِ أَنَّ ٱلْمَارِنَ مَا لآَنَ مِنْ غُضْرُوفِهِ وَ
ٱلْغُضْرُوفَ هُوَ ٱلرَّقِيقُ ٱلْأَبْيَضُ كَالْعَظْمِ يَكُونُ فِي ٱلْمَارِنِ وَ ٱلْمَارِنَ كُلّهُ غَضَارِيفُ («وَ فِي الشَّفَتَيْنِ الدَّيَةُ وَ فِي ٱلْعَيْنَيْنِ الدِّيَةُ وَ
فِي إحدَاهُمَا نِصْفُ الدِّيَةِ».
commentary:
The compiler of this book, may Allah {SWT} have mercy on him, commented:
I found in the book of Ibn Al-A'rabi regarding the description of human anatomy that
Al-marin refers to the soft part of the cartilage, and cartilage is the thin, white, bone-
like tissue found in the soft part of the nose. The entire marin consists of cartilage.
Imam {a.s} further said: "For the lips, the full diyya applies. For both eyes, the full diyya
is due, and for one eye, half of the diyya is required."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Jameelah from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu
Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"For the lower lip, the compensation is six thousand (dirhams), and for the upper lip, it
is four thousand (dirhams) because the lower lip holds water."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أَبِي جَمِيلَةَ عَنْ أَبَانِ بْنِ تَغْلِبَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «فِي الشَّفَةِ
السُفْلَى سِتَّةُ آلآَفِ وَ فِي الْعُلْيَا أَرْبَعَةُ آلاَفِ لِأَنَّ السُفْلَى ثُمْسِكُ ٱلْمَاءَ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.312 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.132 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.246 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.4 p.288 • Nuzhat Al-Nazir, Vol.1 p.139 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.634 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.692 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.294

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad
ibn Ali Al-Baqir {a.s} who said:
"The Commander of the Faithful {a.s} ruled concerning a man who lost one of his eyes
that an ostrich egg should be taken, and the man's healthy eye should be covered so
he cannot see with it. Then, his vision should be measured to its limit, and the distance
between the range of his injured eye and his healthy eye should be calculated.
Compensation should be paid accordingly based on that measurement."
text_ar:
وَ رُوِيَ عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ قَيْسِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ قَالَ: «قَضَى أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُوْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَلاَمُ فِي
رَجُلٍ أُصِيبَ إحدَى عَيْتَيْهِ أَنْ تُوْخَدَ بَيْضَةُ نَعَامَةٍ فَيُمْشَى بِهَا وَ تُوثَقَ عَيْئُهُ الصِّجِيحَةُ حَثَّى لا يُنصِرَ بِهَا وَ يَنْتَهِيّ
بَصَرُهُ ثُمَّ يُحْسَبَ مَا بَيْنَ مُنتَهَى بَصَرٍ عَيْنِهِ الَّتِي أُصِيبَثْ وَ بَيْنَ عَيْنِهِ الصِّجِيحَةِ فَيُوَدى بِحِسَابٍ ذَلِكَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.133 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.266 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.735 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.369

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
It is narrated from Ibn Abi Umair from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdullah
Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said:
"Everything in the human body that exists in pairs carries the full blood money (diyya)
for both, and half the blood money for one. And whatever exists as a single part in the
body carries the full blood money."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ عَنْ هِشَامِ بْنِ سَالِمِ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «كُلُّ مَا كَانَ فِي ٱلْإِنْسَانِ
اِثْنَيْنِ فَفِيهِمَا الدِّيَةُ وَ فِي إِحْدَاهُمَا نِصْفُ الدِّيَةِ وَ مَا كَانَ وَاجِداً فَفِيهِ الدِّيَةُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.133 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.258 • Nuzhat Al-Nazir, Vol.1 p.145 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.629 • Awali Al-La’ali, Vol.3 p.633 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.691 • Wasa’il Al- Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.287 • Al-Fusul Al-Muhimmah, Vol.2 p.536

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
It is narrated from Ibn Mahbub from Abdul Wahhab ibn Al-Sabbah from Ali
from Abu Basir from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} that he said
regarding a man who was struck in his ear and claimed that one of his ears had
diminished in hearing.
Imam {a.s} said: “The injured ear should be tightly bound, and the healthy ear should be
left open. A bell should be struck in front of his face, and he should be asked to listen.
If the sound of the bell becomes faint for him, its position should be noted.
Then, the bell should be taken behind him and rung until the sound fades for him; when
it fades, its position should be marked. The distance between the two positions is then
measured. If they are equal, it is known that he has spoken the truth.
Then, the bell should be taken to his right side and rung until the sound fades, and its
position should be marked. Similarly, the bell should be taken to his left side and rung
until the sound fades, and its position should be marked. If the distances are equal, it
is confirmed that he has spoken the truth."
Imam {a.s} further said: “Then the affected ear should be opened, and the healthy ear
should be tightly bound. The bell should be rung in front of him, and the process
repeated as it was initially done with the healthy ear. Then, the difference between the
healthy and the affected ear should be measured, and compensation determined
accordingly."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ الْوَهَّابِ بْنِ الصِّبَّاحِ عَنْ عَلِيَّ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ
أَنَّهُ قَالَ: فِي رَجُلٍ وُجِئَ فِي أَذُنِهِ فَادَّعَى أَنَّ إِحْدَى أَذُنَيْهِ نَقَصَ مِنْ سَمْعِهِ بِهَا شَيْءَ قَالَ «تُشَدُّ الَّتِي ضُرِبَتْ شَدّاً
جَيِّداً وَ تُفْتَحْ ٱلصَّجِيحَةُ فَيُضْرَبُ لَهُ بِالْجَرَسِ جِيَالَ وَجْهِهِ وَ يُقَالُ لَهُ اِسْمَعْ فَإِذَا خَفِيَ عَلَيْهِ صَوْتُ ٱلْجَرَسِ عُلَمَ
مَكَانُهُ ثُمَّ يُذْهَبُ بِالْجَرَسِ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ فَيُضْرَبُ بِهِ مِنْ خَلْفِهِ حَتَّى يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ الصَّوْتُ فَإِذَا خَفِيَ عَلَيْهِ عُلَّمَ مَكَانُهُ
ثُمَّ يُقَاسُ مَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَإِنْ كَانَا سَوَاءً عُلِمَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ صَدَقَ ثُمَّ يُوْخَذُ بِهِ عَنْ يَمِينِهِ فَيُضْرَبُ بِهِ حَتَّى يَخْفَى ثُمَّ يُعَلَّمُ ثُمَّ
يُوخَذُ بِهِ عَنْ يَسَارِهِ فَيُضْرَبُ بِهِ حَتَّى يَخْفَى ثُمَّ يُعَلَّمُ بِهِ ثُمَّ يُقَاسُ مَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَإِنْ كَانَا سَوَاءً عُلِمَ أَنَّهُ قَدْ صَدَقَ»
قَالَ «ثُمَّ تُفْتَحُ أُذْنُهُ ٱلْمُعْتَلَّةُ وَ ثُشَدُ ٱلْأُخْرَى شَدَاً جَيَّداً ثُمَّ يُضْرَبُ بِالْجَرَسِ مِنْ قُدَامِهِ ثُمَّ يُعَلَّمُ حَتَّى يَخْفَى يُصْنَعُ
بِهِ كَمَا صُنعَ أَوْلَ مَرَّةٍ بِأُذُنِهِ الصَّجِيحَةِ ثُمَّ يُقَاسُ مَا بَيْنَ الصِّجِيحَةِ وَ ٱلْمُعْتَلّةِ فَيُقَوْمُ مِنْ جِسَابٍ ذَلِكَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.133

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
It is narrated from Ibn Mahbub from his father from Hammad ibn Ziyad from
Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who
said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about a man who struck another man's ear with a bone, and the man
claimed that he had completely lost his hearing.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should be given a respite for one year, and two just witnesses
should observe him. If they testify that he heard and responded to hearing, then he has
no right (to compensation).
But if it cannot be confirmed that he heard, he should be made to swear an oath, and
then he should be given the full compensation (blood money)."
I asked: “What if he regains his hearing after receiving the compensation?"
LIFE
Imam {a.s} replied: “It is something Allah {SWT} the Exalted has granted him."
I then asked Imam {a.s} about someone who claimed he could no longer see with his
eye.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should be given a respite for one year, and after the year, he should
swear an oath that he cannot see, and then he should be given the full compensation
(blood money)."
I asked: “What if he regains his sight after that?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “It is something Allah {SWT} has granted him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ أبِيهِ عَنْ حَمَادِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللهِ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ قَالَ:
سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ وَجَأَ أَذُنَ رَجُلٍ بِعَظْمِ فَادَّعَى أَنَّهُ ذَهَبَ سَمْعُهُ كُلْهُ قَالَ «يُؤَجَّلُ سَنَةً وَ يُتَرَصَّدُ بِشَاهِدَيْ عَدْلٍ فَإِنْ
جَاءًا فَشَهِدَا أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ وَ أَنَّهُ أَجَابَ عَلَى سَمْعٍ فَلا حَقَّ لَهُ وَ إِنْ لَمْ يُعْتَرْ عَلَى أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ أسْشُحْلِفَ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أُغْطِيَ الدِّيَةَ»
قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنَّهُ يَسْمَعُ بَعْدَ مَا أُغْطِيَ الدِّيَةَ قَالَ «هُوَ شَيءُ أَعْطَاهُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى إِيَّاهُ» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْثُهُ عَنِ ٱلْعَيْنِ يَدَّعِي
صَاحِبُهَا أَنْهُ لا يُنْصِرُ بِهَا قَالَ »يُوَجَّلُ سَنَةً ثُمَّ يُسْتَحْلَفُ بَعْدَ السَّنَةِ أَنْهُ لا يُنْصِرُ ثُمَّ يُعْطَى الدِّيَةَ» قُلْتُ فَإِنّهُ أَبْصَرَ
بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ «هُوَ شَيْءُ أَعْطَاهُ اللَهُ إِيَاهُ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.133
text_chunk:
It is narrated from Ibn Mahbub from his father from Hammad ibn Ziyad from
Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who
said:
I asked Imam {a.s} about a man who struck another man's ear with a bone, and the man
claimed that he had completely lost his hearing.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should be given a respite for one year, and two just witnesses
should observe him. If they testify that he heard and responded to hearing, then he has
no right (to compensation).
But if it cannot be confirmed that he heard, he should be made to swear an oath, and
then he should be given the full compensation (blood money)."
I asked: “What if he regains his hearing after receiving the compensation?"
LIFE
Imam {a.s} replied: “It is something Allah {SWT} the Exalted has granted him."
I then asked Imam {a.s} about someone who claimed he could no longer see with his
eye.
Imam {a.s} said: “He should be given a respite for one year, and after the year, he should
swear an oath that he cannot see, and then he should be given the full compensation
(blood money)."
I asked: “What if he regains his sight after that?"
Imam {a.s} replied: “It is something Allah {SWT} has granted him."

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
In the narration of Al-Sakooni, it is reported that Commander of the Faithful
{a.s} ruled that if the spine is broken, the full blood money (diya) is due.
text_ar: - وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ السَّكُونِيِّ : «أَنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُومِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَاَمُ قَضَى فِي الصُّلْبِ إِذَا اِنْكَسَرَ الدِّيَةَ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.134 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.695
text_chunk:
In the narration of Al-Sakooni, it is reported that Commander of the Faithful

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Hisham ibn Salim narrated from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man whose coccyx (tailbone) was broken, resulting
in his inability to control his bowels.
Imam {a.s} replied: “The full blood money (diya) is due."
Sulayman further asked Imam {a.s} about a man who engaged in intercourse with a slave
girl and caused ifda’ (a severe injury of female reproductive organs), and she, in that
condition, would never be able to bear children.
Imam {a.s} replied: “The full blood money (diya) is due."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى هِشَامُ بْنُ سَالِمِ عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ خَالِدِ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ كُسِرَ بُعْصُوصُهُ
فَلَمْ يَمْلِكِ اِسْتَهُ مَا فِيهِ مِنَ الدِّيَةِ فَقَالَ «آلدِّيَةُ كَامِلَةً» قَالَ وَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ وَقَعَ بِجَارِيَةٍ فَأَفْضَاهَا وَ هِيَ إِذَا
نَزَلَتْ بِتِلْكَ الْمَنْزِلَةِ لَمْ تَلِدْ فَقَالَ «الدِّيَةُ كَامِلَةً».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.313 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.134 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.248 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.698 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.370

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON WHAT REQUIRES FULL BLOOD MONEY AND HALF BLOOD MONEY IN CASES OTHER THAN THE TAKING OF A
text_en:
Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah {a.s} about a man who married a slave girl, then had intercourse
with her and caused ifda’ (a severe injury of female reproductive organs).
Imam {a.s} replied: “He is responsible for providing for her needs as long as she is alive."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى حَمَّادٌ عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْثُهُ عَنْ رَجُلٍ تَزَوَّجَ جَارِيَةً فَوَقَعَ عَلَيْهَا
فَأَفْضَاهَا قَالَ «عَلَيْهِ ٱلْإِجْرَاءُ عَلَيْهَا مَا دَامَثْ حَيَّةً».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.134 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.249 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.4 p.294 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.702 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.20 p.494 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.282

text_en:
In the narration of Al-Sakuni, it is reported that Commander of the Faithful {a.s}
said: "An eye is not to be examined (for diyyah) on a cloudy day."
text_ar: - وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ السَّكُونِيِّ قَالَ قَالَ أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلاَمُ : «لا تُقَاسُ عَيْنٌ فِي يَوْمِ غَيْمِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.134 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.267 • Tahdhib Al- Ahkam, Vol.10 p.268 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.736 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.365 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.365 • Mustadrak Al-Wasa’il, Vol.18 p.394

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE BLOOD MONEY FOR FINGERS,
text_en:
It is narrated by Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar
ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} who said: I asked Imam {a.s} about the fingers - whether
some of them have more value over others in terms of blood money (diyyah).
Imam {a.s} replied: "They are all equal in blood money (diyyah)."
text_ar:
بَابُ دِيَةِ الْأَصَابِعٍ وَ الْأَسْنَانِ وَ الْعِظَامِ
رَوَى عُثُمَانُ بْنُ عِيسَى عَنْ سَمَاعَةً عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السِّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْأَصَابِعِ هَلْ لِبَعْضِهَا
عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَصْلْ فِي الدِّيَةِ قَالَ «هُنَّ سَوَاءُ فِي الدَّيَةِ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.134 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.259 • Al-Istibsar, Vol.4 p.291 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.716 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.347

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE BLOOD MONEY FOR FINGERS,
text_en:
It is narrated by Asim ibn Humaid from Abu Basir from Abu Abdullah {a.s} who
said: I asked Imam {a.s} about a tooth or an arm that is intentionally broken - does it
require compensation (financial payment) or is there retaliation (qisas)?
Imam {a.s} replied: "Retaliation (qisas)."
I asked: “What if they offer him blood money instead?"
Imam {a.s} replied: "If he is satisfied with whatever they offer, then it is permissible for
him."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى عَاصِمُ بْنُ حُمَيْدٍ عَنْ أَبِي بَصِيرٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: سَألْتُهُ عَنِ السِّنَّ وَ الذِّرَاعِ
يُكْسَرَانِ عَمْداً أَلَهُمَا أَرْش أَوْ قَوَدٌ فَقَالَ «قَوَدٌ» قَالَ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ أَضْعَفُوا لَهُ آلدِّيَةَ فَقَالَ «إنْ أَرْضَوْهُ بِمَا شَاءَ فَهُوَ لَهُ».
cross_references: Al-Kafi, Vol.7 p.320 • Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.135 • Tahdhib Al-Ahkam, Vol.10 p.275 • Al-Wafi, Vol.16 p.682 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.176 • Tafsir Nur Al-Thaqalayn, Vol.1 p.636 • Tafsir Kanz Al-Daqaiq, Vol.4 p.128

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE BLOOD MONEY FOR FINGERS,
text_en:
In the narration of Ibn Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Abdullah {a.s}, he said:
"For each finger, there is a compensation of ten camels if it is cut off from its base or
becomes paralyzed."
text_ar:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ اِبْنِ بُكَيْرٍ عَنْ زُرَارَةَ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «فِي الْإِصْبَعِ عَشَرٌ مِنَ ٱلْإِبِلِ إِذَا
قُطِعَتْ مِنْ أَصْلِهَا أَوْ شَلَّتْ».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, V.4 p.135 • Al-Wafi, V.16 p.714 • Wasa’il Al-Shi’ah, Vol.29 p.348

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE BLOOD MONEY FOR FINGERS, TEETH, AND BONES
text_en:
In the narration of Jameel from some of our companions from one of the
Imams (peace be upon them), that it was reported regarding the tooth of a child that
is struck by a man and falls out but later grows back
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no retaliation (qisas) upon him, but he must pay compensation
(arsh)."
Regarding a man whose hand is broken but later heals,
Imam {a.s} said: "There is no retaliation against him, but he must pay compensation
(arsh)."
When Jamil was asked about the amount of compensation for the child's tooth and
the broken hand, Imam {a.s} replied: "It is a small amount"

Scholar's Note:
However. Imam {a.s} did not narrate any specific value for it.
text_ar:
وَ فِي رِوَايَةِ جَمِيلٍ عَنْ بَعْضٍ أَصْحَابِنَا عَنْ أَحَدِهِمَا عَلَيْهِمَا السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: فِي سِنَّ الصَّبِيِّ يَضْرِبُهَا الرَّجُلُ
فَتَسْقُطُ ثُمَّ تَثْبُتُ قَالَ «لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ قِصَاص وَ عَلَيْهِ الْأَرْشُ» وَ قَالَ فِي الرَّجُلِ تُكْسَرُ يَدُهُ ثُمَّ تَبْرَأُ يَدُهُ قَالَ «لا
يُقْتَصُّ مِنْهُ وَ لَكِنْ يُغطَى الْأَرْشَ» وَ سُئِلَ جَمِيلْ كَمِ الْأَرْش فِي سِنَّ الصَّبِيِّ وَ كَسْرِ ٱلْيَدِ قَالَ «شَيْءٌ يَسِيرٌ».
وَ لَمْ يَرْوِ فِيهِ شَيْئاً مَعْلُوماً.
commentary: However. Imam {a.s} did not narrate any specific value for it.
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.135

author: Shaykh al-Saduq
chapter_title: CHAPTER ON THE BLOOD MONEY FOR FINGERS, TEETH, AND BONES
text_en:
Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The fingers of the hands and feet are equal in compensation (diyyah)."
Imam {a.s} also said: "If a tooth is struck, it should be observed for a year. If it falls out,
the striker must pay five hundred dirhams. However, if it does not fall out but turns
black, the striker must pay two-thirds of its compensation."
text_ar:
وَ رَوَى اِبْنُ مَحْبُوبِ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلاَمُ قَالَ: «أَصَابِعُ ٱلْيَدَيْنِ وَ الرِّجْلَيْنِ
فِي الدِّيَةِ سَوَاء» وَ قَالَ «فِي السِّنَّ إِذَا ضُرِبَتِ أنْتُظِرَ بِهَا سَنَةً فَإِنْ وَقَعَتْ أُغْرِمَ الضَّارِبُ خَمْسَمَائَةِ دِرْهَمِ وَ إِنْ لَمْ
تَقَعْ وَ اسْوَدَّثْ أَغْرِمَ ثُلْثَيْ دِيَتِهَا».
cross_references: Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih, Vol.4 p.135
text_chunk:
Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq {a.s} said:
"The fingers of the hands and feet are equal in compensation (diyyah)."
Imam {a.s} also said: "If a tooth is struck, it should be observed for a year. If it falls out,
the striker must pay five hundred dirhams. However, if it does not fall out but turns
